body.translated_text: <s>Sphuṭārthā Śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkā</s> (The Clear-Meaning Commentary on the Venerable Compendium of Proper Conduct)

body.text: | namo buddhāya ||
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.translated_text: Those who have abandoned all defilements without remainder, who have conquered [their] enemies, who have reached the far shore of the ocean of the knowable, who are compassionate —

children.text: saddharmasacchiṣyagaṇān samastān namāmi buddhān bahuśaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with all the assemblies of true disciples of the true <s>Dharma</s>, I salute the <s>Buddha</s>s repeatedly with joined palms.
Whose root of good conduct has grown through the sprinkling-water of generosity, whose beauty has arisen as fresh shoots of loving-kindness and compassion [...],

children.text: bodhyaṅgamārgaphalitaṃ hi jinālijuṣṭaṃ mañjuśriyaṃ ca śubhakalpataruṃ namāmi ||
children.translated_text: bearing the fruit of the path of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyāṅga</s>), frequented by the bee-line of the Conquerors — I salute <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the auspicious wish-fulfilling tree.

body.text:
ācārasaṃgrahasyāsya smṛtaye mandamedhasāṃ
vistīrṇasūtrasaṃkṣepāt kriyate 'yaṃ viniścayaḥ ||
body.translated_text: This determination is made by summarizing extensive <s>sūtra</s>s, for the remembrance of those of dull intellect, regarding this compendium of conduct.

body.text: tatra prāyeṇa hi santo gurviṣṭadevatāṃ pūjayitvā kriyāyāṃ pravartante puṇyaprasavārtha, tato vighnopaśamanārthaṃ maṅgalārthañceti | ahamapi ca sadācāro 'yamiti kṛtvā śrīghanā cārasaṃgrahārambhe svadevatānamaskāraṃ kartuṃ pravṛtta iti darśayannāha | prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśa iti vistaraḥ | tatra trividhaḥ saṃkleśaḥ- kleśasaṃkleśaḥ karmasaṃkleśaḥ janmasaṃkleśaśca | kliśyanti kāyavākcittāni iti kleśāḥ | te ca rāgādikamaṣṭottaraśataṃ | aṣṭānavatiranuśayāḥ | daśa paryavasthānāni | kleśa eva (

children.text:
) saṃkleśaḥ kleśasaṃkleśaḥ kleśasvabhāvatvāt kleśasaṃkleśahetutvācca kleśasaṃkleśa ityuccate | kasya kleśasaṃkleśahetutvāditi cet karmasaṃkleśasyeti brūmaḥ | yataḥ kleśānalalīḍhahṛdayā[ḥ]
kuśalamarīcitoyākārapratibhāsamavagāhanāya paryeṣante | trividhaṃ karma- kāyikaṃ vācikaṃ mānasikañca | kāyikamapi trividhaṃ kuśalamakuśalamavyākṛtañca | evaṃ vācikamānasike vistareṇohye | karmaiva saṃkleśaḥ karmasaṃkleśaḥ saṃkleśakaratvāt saṃkleśahetutvācca | kleśasaṃkleśajani[ta]tvā[t] yasya saṃkleśakaratvamavagantavyaṃ, janmakleśahetutvāt saṃkleśahetutvaṃ | janma utpattiḥ prādurbhāva ityanarthāntaraṃ | janmaiva saṃkleśaḥ janmasaṃkleśaḥ janmasaṃkleśaphalatvāt saṃkleśahetutvācca | yataḥ karmasaṃkleśād rāgiṇāṃ janma vītarāgajanmādarśanāt | ataḥ kleśakarma saṃkleśakarma saṃkleśaphalatvāt kleśasaṃkleśahetutvācca janmasaṃkleśa ityucyate | ata eva nirdeśo nālpīyān na ca bhūyān ratnatrayavat | adhunā tripadyeva bahuvrīhiḥ | prahīṇāḥ [paritya]ktāḥ apanītāstiraskṛtāḥ aśeṣāḥ nikhilā vāsanāsahitāḥ saṃkleśā kleśa[karma]janmākhyāyena [buddhena] bhagavatā, sa bhavati prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśaḥ | anena buddhasya bhagavataḥ prahāṇasaṃpadaṃ darśayati | nanu [prahīṇa]saṃkleśa ityeva vaktavyaṃ, kimaśeṣagrahaṇena? naitadasti | yadi prahīṇasaṃkleśa ityevocyate, tadā śrāvakapratyekabuddh[ānāmapi] grahaṇaṃ prāpnoti | te 'pi prahīṇasaṃkleśā bhavanti kliṣṭājñānātyantābhāvāt, na tu prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśāḥ akliṣṭā [jñānātyantābhā]vāt | tathāpyeṣāṃ pratyekajinaśrāvakāṇāṃ balavaiśā[ra]dyādiṣu (
children.translated_text: ) it is called the defilement of affliction because its nature is affliction and because it is the cause of the defilement [of affliction]. "The cause of which defilement?" we say: of the defilement of <s>karma</s>. For those whose hearts are licked by the fire of afflictions seek to plunge into what appears as the water-mirage of wholesome [deeds]. <s>Karma</s> is threefold: bodily, verbal, and mental. Bodily <s>karma</s> too is threefold: wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. Likewise verbal and mental [<s>karma</s>] should be understood in detail. <s>Karma</s> itself being defilement is the defilement of <s>karma</s> — because it causes defilement and because it is the cause of defilement. Its capacity to cause defilement should be understood from the fact that it is produced by the defilement of afflictions, and its being the cause of defilement is because it is the cause of the affliction of birth. Birth, arising, and manifestation are synonymous. Birth itself being defilement is the defilement of birth — because it is the result of the defilement of birth and because it is the cause of defilement. For the birth of those with passion arises from the defilement of <s>karma</s>, since the birth of those free from passion is not observed. Therefore, the defilement of affliction, the defilement of <s>karma</s>, and the defilement of birth [are named thus] because they are the results of defilement and the causes of the defilement of affliction. Hence the exposition is neither too brief nor too extensive, like the Three Jewels. Now the compound is a <s>bahuvrīhi</s> with three terms: "abandoned" means relinquished, removed, cast aside; "without remainder" means complete, including the residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>s); "defilements" means the afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and birth — by that [<s>Buddha</s>], the Blessed One. He is the one who has abandoned all defilements without remainder. By this, he shows the perfection of abandonment (<s>prahāṇasaṃpad</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One. [Objection:] Should one not simply say "who has abandoned defilement"? What is the purpose of adding "without remainder"? This is not so. If one said only "who has abandoned defilement," then <s>Śrāvaka</s>s and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s would also be included. They too have abandoned defilement, because of the complete absence of afflictive ignorance (<s>kliṣṭājñāna</s>); but they have not abandoned all defilements without remainder, because of the [incomplete] absence of non-afflictive [ignorance]. Moreover, these <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s and <s>Śrāvaka</s>s, with regard to the
[SŚ 3]

children.text: ) tathāgatadharmeṣu anekaloka[dhātuga]teṣu deśeṣu atītānāgatabhedabhinneṣu ca na bhavatyevākliṣṭamajñānaṃ | [kiṃ punaḥ] saṃjānīṣe tvaṃ sāriputra, tathāgatasya śīlaskandhaṃ samādhiskandhaṃ prajñāskandhaṃ vimuktiskandhaṃ vimuktijñāna[darśana]skandhamiti pṛṣṭenoktaṃ- no bhadanteti sūtrāt āryamahāmaudgalyāyanasya svamātṛjanmadeśāparijñānāt ā[rya]sāriputreṇa ca pravrajyāpekṣapuruṣapratyākhyānāt mayūracandrakādiniṣpattikarmaviśeṣāparijñānācceti | ato mābhūt teṣāṃ grahaṇaṃ | jñeyaṃ boddhavyaṃ parijñātavyamityanarthāntaraṃ | niścayena dhīyante avatiṣṭhante asmin bhāvā iti nidhirādhāraḥ | ambhasāṃ vāriṇāṃ nidhirambhonidhiḥ | loke hi ambhonidhiśabdo bāhyavastuni prasiddhaḥ | iha tu tatsādharmyāt yathā mahāsamudro gambhīratvāt atiduruttaratvāccāmbhonidhirucyate, evaṃ jñeyamapi duṣparijñānāt samastānāvedyatvena duravagāhayatvāt ambhonidhiḥ | jñeyamevāmbhonidhiḥ jñeyāmbhonidhiḥ | pāraṃ gacchatīti jñeyāmbho[ni]dhipāragaḥ pārāvāragamanavat | anenāpi jñānasaṃpadaṃ daśabalasya darśayati | prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśaścāsau jñeyāmbhonidhipāragaśceti prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśajñeyāmbho[ni]dhipāragaḥ | atastaṃ prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśajñeyāmbhoni[dhi]pāragaṃ | tamīdṛgviśiṣṭaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ praṇamya kāyavāṅmanobhiriti śeṣaḥ | samānakartṛkayoḥ kriyayoḥ pūrvakāle 'yaṃ ktvā vidhīyate prāṇamyeti | yathā snātvā bhuṃkta iti | ataḥ pṛcchayate kaṃ praṇamya kiṃ kariṣyasītyāha- śrāmaṇerāṇāmācāraḥ saṃgrahīṣyate | tatra śrāmaṇamuccaṃ nirvāṇapuramīranti gacchantīti śrāmaṇerāḥ | (
children.translated_text: ) <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities such as the powers and fearlessnesses, in numerous world-systems, and with respect to distinctions of past and future — non-afflictive ignorance indeed persists [in them]. [As the <s>sūtra</s> states:] "Do you know, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s aggregate of morality, aggregate of concentration, aggregate of wisdom, aggregate of liberation, and aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation?" When asked, he said: "No, Venerable Sir" — from this <s>sūtra</s>. Also because the noble <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> did not fully know the land of his own mother's birth, and because the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> rejected [a person] seeking ordination, and because of not fully knowing the particular <s>karma</s> that produced [beings like] <s>Mayūracandrakā</s> and others. Therefore, lest they be included, [the qualification "without remainder" is added]. "The knowable" (<s>jñeya</s>) means what is to be known, to be understood, to be fully comprehended — these are synonymous. "That in which things are firmly placed" is a receptacle (<s>nidhi</s>), a container. "The receptacle of waters" is the ocean (<s>ambhonidhi</s>). In common usage, the word "ocean" is well-known for an external object. But here, by analogy with it: just as the great ocean is called the ocean because of its depth and extreme difficulty to cross, so too the knowable is called the ocean because it is difficult to fully comprehend and difficult to fathom due to its being unknowable in its entirety. The knowable itself being the ocean is "the ocean of the knowable" (<s>jñeyāmbhonidhi</s>). "One who goes to the far shore" of the ocean of the knowable is "one who has reached the far shore of the ocean of the knowable," like crossing to the other shore. By this too, he shows the perfection of knowledge of the Ten-Powered One. And he who has abandoned all defilements without remainder and who has reached the far shore of the ocean of the knowable is [described by the compound] "the one who has abandoned all defilements without remainder and reached the far shore of the ocean of the knowable." Therefore, "having bowed" to that <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, who is thus distinguished — with body, speech, and mind, this is the remainder. The absolutive (<s>ktvā</s>) is used when the same agent performs a prior action, as in "having bathed, he eats." Therefore, when asked "Having bowed to whom, what will you do?" he says: the conduct of <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s will be compiled. Therein, those who go toward the supreme city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> are <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s.
[SŚ 4]

children.text: ) athavā śrāmaṇyamamalo mārgaḥ tamīranti gacchantīti śrāmaṇerāḥ | śrāmaṇānāmerā dāsā iti kecit | teṣāṃ kiṃ? ācāraḥ saṃgrahīṣyate | ācaraṇamācāraḥ akuśalaparivarjanaṃ kuśalabhajanaṃ ceti yo 'rthaḥ | nanu ca evaṃ sati granthasyācāratvaṃ na prāpnoti kriyārūpatvāt | naiṣa doṣaḥ | ācārapratipādako 'pi grantha ācāra ucyata iti upacārāt jātakamālāvat kaṃsavadhavat | ācarantyasminniti kṛtvā ācāraśabdena śrīghanācārasaṃgraha evākhyāyate | saṃgrahīṣyata iti saṃgrahaḥ | kariṣyate āripsata iti yāvat | mayeti vākyaśeṣaḥ | anyathā uttamapuruṣeṇaiva nirdeśamakariṣyat, ācāraṃ saṃgrahīṣyāmīti | saṃkṣepato 'smin śloke buddhasya bhagavataḥ prahāṇasaṃpat jñānasaṃpat, trailokya śāstṛtvaṃ, aviparītaśāsanakāraṇañca paridīpitaṃ prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśaśabdena jñeyāmbhonidhipāragaśabdena ca | yataḥ prahīṇāśeṣasaṃkleśatvaṃ prahāṇasaṃpadaṃ nātivartate, jñeyāmbhonidhipāragatvaṃ ca jñānasaṃpadaṃ | prahāṇajñānasaṃpajjñāne yo yuktaḥ, sa trailokya gururbhavati yathābhūtaśāstāceti |
children.translated_text: ) Or, those who go toward <s>śrāmaṇya</s> (the stainless path) are <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s. Some say: "<s>erā</s> means servants of <s>śramanā</s>s (renunciants)." What about them? Their conduct will be compiled. Conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) means behavior — the meaning being the avoidance of unwholesome [actions] and the cultivation of wholesome [ones]. [Objection:] But if so, the text cannot be [called] conduct, since it is in the form of an action [description, not the action itself]. This is no fault. A text that teaches conduct is also called "conduct" by figurative usage, like the <s>Jātakamālā</s> or the <s>Kaṃsavadha</s>. Because "one conducts oneself in accordance with it," by the word "conduct" the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> itself is designated. "Will be compiled" (<s>saṃgrahīṣyate</s>) means "will be composed," i.e., "is desired" — "by me" is the sentence-completion. Otherwise he would have stated it in the first person only: "I shall compile the conduct." In summary, in this verse the perfection of abandonment, the perfection of knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, his being the teacher of the three worlds, and the reason for his undeviating teaching are illuminated — by the word "who has abandoned all defilements without remainder" and by the word "who has reached the far shore of the ocean of the knowable." For the abandonment of all defilements without remainder does not exceed the perfection of abandonment, and reaching the far shore of the ocean of the knowable [does not exceed] the perfection of knowledge. One who is endowed with the perfection of abandonment and the perfection of knowledge becomes the teacher of the three worlds, as a teacher in accordance with reality.

body.translated_text: In this regard, generally the virtuous, having worshipped the deity favored by their teacher, engage in [their] work for the sake of producing merit, and for the purpose of removing obstacles and for auspiciousness. "I too, thinking 'this is proper conduct,' have undertaken to make obeisance to my own deity at the beginning of the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>" — showing this, he says: "Who has abandoned all defilements without remainder" — this is the elaboration. Therein, defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) is threefold: the defilement of afflictions (<s>kleśasaṃkleśa</s>), the defilement of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmasaṃkleśa</s>), and the defilement of birth (<s>janmasaṃkleśa</s>). That which afflicts body, speech, and mind — those are the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>s). They number one hundred and eight, beginning with passion (<s>rāga</s>). Ninety-eight are latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>s) and ten are entanglements (<s>paryavasthāna</s>s). Affliction itself being defilement is the defilement of affliction —

children.translated_text: The perfection of abandonment, the perfection of knowledge, being the sole teacher of the three worlds,
and the cause of correct teaching — these are stated by the verse, in order.

body.text: iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ || 1 ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the summary verse. [End of commentary on verse] 1.

body.text: śaraṇaṃ bhavediti vistaraḥ | nanu cācāraḥ saṃgrahīṣyata iti anantarābhidhānādācāraḥ saṃgrahītavyaḥ kasmāt śaraṇagamanādikamucyate? yadyapyetacchrāmaṇerāṇāmityanantaraṃ prakṛtaṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāmācāraḥ saṃgrahīṣyata iti | te ca śrāmaṇerā daśaśikṣā padaparigṛhītā eva prādhānyenābhipretāḥ, na gṛhiṇaḥ | sa eṣa śrāmaṇeramāvaḥ teṣāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāṃ kathaṃ bhavati, yena śrāmaṇerabhāvena samanvāgatānāmācāraḥ saṃgrahīṣyata iti | ato yathoddeśaḥ tathā nirdeśa iti nyāyāt śrāmaṇerabhāva eva tāvadādau vaktavya ityāha | śaraṇaṃ gatavāniti ślokaḥ | tatra trāṇārthaḥ śaraṇārthaḥ | ata evāha bhagavān-
body.translated_text: "May [the <s>Buddha</s>] be [our] refuge" — this is the elaboration. [Objection:] Since "the conduct will be compiled" was stated immediately [before], the conduct should be compiled — why is refuge-taking and so forth discussed [first]? Although this follows immediately upon "of <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s," the subject being "the conduct of <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s will be compiled," those <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s are primarily understood as those who have undertaken the ten training precepts, not householders. This is the state of being a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> of those <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s — how does it come about? The conduct of those endowed with that state of being a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> will be compiled. Therefore, by the principle that "the exposition follows the order of the introduction," the state of being a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> itself must first be stated. Thus he says: "[The <s>Buddha</s> is his] refuge" — this is the verse. Therein, the meaning of "refuge" (<s>śaraṇa</s>) is "protection." Hence the Blessed One has said:

children.text: bahavaḥ śaraṇaṃ yānti parvatāṃśca vanāni ca |
children.translated_text: Many take refuge in mountains and forests,
in parks, <s>caitya</s>s, and trees — people threatened by fear.

body.text: iti gāthāvacanāt | gatavāniti prayātavān | buddhamiti | yathā dinakarakarodayādāpāditasakalakarṇikārapramuditadvirephavṛndaparipīyamānakamalaṣaṇḍo buddha ityucyate, evaṃ bhagavānapi bhūtabhāvisāṃpratikādhvanirmuktajñeyabuddhervikāśanāt mohasaṃkocāpagamāt buddha ityucyate | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: Thus, from this verse-passage. "Gone" means "proceeded." As for "<s>Buddha</s>" — just as when the rays of the sun rise, a cluster of lotuses blooms fully, and the swarm of bees, delighted, drinks from the <s>karṇikāra</s> blossoms, and this is called "<s>buddha</s>" (awakened); so too the Blessed One is called "<s>Buddha</s>" because of the blossoming of the knowledge-<s>buddhi</s> (awakening) that has been released regarding the knowable in the past, future, and present time-periods, and because of the departure of the contraction of delusion. And thus it is said:

body.text:
trailokye cādhvanirmukte jñeye vikāśanāddhiyaḥ |
vibuddhapratibuddhādvā mohasaṃkocaghātakaḥ || iti |
body.translated_text:
'And in the three worlds, for the one liberated from the path, what is to be known — because of the expansion of the intellect,
from [the word] <s>vibuddha</s> (fully awakened) or <s>pratibuddha</s> (awakened to), [he is called <s>Buddha</s>], the destroyer of the contraction of delusion.'

body.text: athavā yaḥ puruṣo vyapanītanidraḥ suptotthito vibuddha ityucyate | evaṃ bhagavānapi saṃsāramahāśayanādutthitaḥ ajñānanidrāpagamāt bauddhasya jñānasya sākṣātkaraṇādbuddha ityucyate | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: Alternatively, a person who has cast off sleep, who has risen from slumber, is called <s>vibuddha</s> (awake). Similarly, the Blessed One too, having risen from the great bed of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), because of the departure of the sleep of ignorance, because of the direct realization of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, is called <s>Buddha</s>. And thus it is said:

body.text:
ajñānanidrācchedāttatvajñānasamudbhavāt |
yo vibuddhaḥ sa vai buddho vibuddhapuruṣo yathā || iti |
body.translated_text:
'Because of the cutting of the sleep of ignorance, because of the arising of the knowledge of reality,
he who is fully awakened is indeed the <s>Buddha</s>, just as a man who is awake [is called awake].'

body.text: ajñānatimirapaṭalaparyavanaddhanetrān prāṇino bodhayatīti buddhaḥ, anuttareṇa jñānena budhyate vā śivamiti buddhaḥ | sa ca trividhena dharmasāmbhogikena nairmāṇikena ca vyavasthita iti anyatra śāstrāntare nirdiṣṭamiti granthagauravaparihārārthamiti iha nābhidhīyate | dharmamiti | svalakṣaṇadhāra[ṇa]svabhāvāt, na dhvaṃsyata iti vā dharmaḥ | sa ca dvividhaḥ- adhigamasvabhāvaḥ āgamasvabhāvaśceti | tatrādhigamo bodhipakṣā dharmā anantā anavadyā[ś]ca | āgamaḥ sūtravinayābhidharmā iti | eṣa dvividhaḥ dharmaḥ | saṃghamiti | catvāraḥ pratipannakāḥ catvāraḥ phalāptāḥ abhedyatvena saṃghagatatvāt aṣṭau mahāpuruṣapudgalāḥ saṃgha ityucyante | katame punaste aṣṭau? yaduta strotāpattiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ strotāpannakaḥ, sakṛdāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ sakṛdāgāmī, anāgāmiphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ anāgāmī, arhatphalasākṣātkriyāyai pratipannakaḥ arhanniti | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: He awakens (<s>bodhayati</s>) beings whose eyes are covered by the mass of the veil of the darkness of ignorance — therefore [he is called] <s>Buddha</s>. Or, he cognizes (<s>budhyate</s>) the auspicious through unsurpassed knowledge — therefore [he is called] <s>Buddha</s>. And he is established in three aspects: the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), the <s>Sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment-body), and the <s>Nairmāṇika</s> (emanation-body). This has been explained elsewhere in other treatises, and to avoid prolixity, it is not set forth here. '<s>Dharma</s>' — because its nature is to sustain (<s>dhāraṇa</s>) its own characteristics, or because it is not destroyed (<s>na dhvaṃsyate</s>), it is <s>Dharma</s>. And it is twofold: that whose nature is realization (<s>adhigama</s>) and that whose nature is scripture (<s>āgama</s>). Therein, realization consists of the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa dharmas</s>), which are infinite and blameless. Scripture consists of the <s>Sūtra</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Abhidharma</s>. This is the twofold <s>Dharma</s>. '<s>Saṃgha</s>' — the four who are practicing, the four who have attained the fruits, by virtue of being in the <s>Saṅgha</s> through their indivisibility — these eight great persons (<s>mahāpuruṣapudgalas</s>) are called the <s>Saṅgha</s>. What then are these eight? Namely: one practicing for the direct realization of the fruit of stream-entry (<s>Srotaāpatti</s>), a stream-enterer; one practicing for the direct realization of the fruit of once-returning, a once-returner (<s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s>); one practicing for the direct realization of the fruit of non-returning, a non-returner (<s>Anāgāmin</s>); one practicing for the direct realization of the fruit of <s>Arhat</s>ship, an <s>Arhat</s>. And thus it is said:

body.text:
buddhe dharme tathā saṃghe mārakoṭiśatairapi |
bhettuṃ na śakyate yasmāt tasmāt saṃgho 'bhidhī(ya)te || iti |
body.translated_text:
'In the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and likewise the <s>Saṅgha</s>, even by hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Māras</s>,
it cannot be split — therefore it is called the <s>Saṅgha</s> (assembly).'

body.text: atastaṃ buddhaṃ dharma saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ yo ga[ta]vāniti yāvadeṣaḥ śrāmaṇero munermata (

children.translated_text: [SŚ 7]

children.text: ) iti anena padena saṃbandhanīyaḥ | kadācid bhayādināpi śaraṇaṃ gacchatītyata āha | bhaktitaḥ prasādavegenetyarthaḥ | atha kimarthamādau pañcaśikṣāpadāni na grāhyante śaraṇagama[nā]didānataḥ | yo hi tasya śaraṇaṃ gacchati, sa tasyājñāṃ paripālayati nānyaḥ | ato yadi na pañcaśikṣāpadāni ādau na grāhyante na trīṇi śaraṇagamanādīni pradīyante, tadā mumukṣuṇā śikṣāpadaparipālanaṃ pratyavajñaiva syāt | ato mābhūdavajñetyādau śaraṇagamanapradānataḥ | śikṣāpañcakamādāyeti | śikṣaṇaṃ śikṣā | pravṛttinivṛttyātmake śīle vā pratipattirācaraṇaṃ samādānataḥ śīle sammukhīkaraṇamiti yo 'rthaḥ | śikṣaiva pañcakaṃ śikṣāpañcakaṃ, evaṃ śikṣāpañca[kā]nītyarthaḥ | kārikābandhānuguṇyācca śikṣāpañcakamityuktaṃ | kāni punaḥ śikṣāpadāni? prāṇātipāta-adattādānakāmamithyācāramṛṣāvādasurāmaireyamadyasthānakebhyo viramaṇaṃ | ādāyeti gṛhītvā | kiṃ yo 'nupravrajito jinaṃ? ya iti yaḥ puruṣaḥ | anupravrajita iti paścāt pravrajitaḥ | kaṃ pratītyāha | jinaṃ | jitakleśatvājjinaḥ | jitātmapāpakā dharmāstenopagaḥ | jinoktamiti śratervacanāt | buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pravrajitaṃ anupravrajāmīti yo vācamudīrayatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since sometimes one goes for refuge even out of fear and the like, therefore [the text] says: 'out of devotion' — the meaning is 'by the force of faith.' Now, for what purpose are the five training precepts (<s>śikṣāpadas</s>) not taken first, before giving the refuge? For whoever goes for refuge to him [the <s>Buddha</s>] obeys his commands, and not another. Therefore, if the five training precepts are not taken first and the three refuges are not given [first], then for one desiring liberation there would be contempt for the observance of the training precepts. Therefore, lest there be contempt, the refuges are given first. 'Having taken the five trainings' — training (<s>śikṣā</s>) is the act of learning. Or: undertaking, practice with respect to morality (<s>śīla</s>) consisting of engagement and abstention, which means coming face to face with morality through formal undertaking. The five trainings are the five [precepts] that are the trainings — thus the meaning. And [it is phrased as] 'the five trainings' in accordance with the exigencies of the verse-form. What, then, are the training precepts? Abstention from: taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>), taking what is not given (<s>adattādāna</s>), sexual misconduct (<s>kāmamithyācāra</s>), false speech (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>), and [consuming] liquor, spirits, and intoxicants (<s>surāmaireyamadyasthāna</s>). 'Having taken' means 'having accepted.' 'Who has gone forth following the <s>Jina</s>?' — '<s>ya</s>' means 'which person.' '<s>anupravrajita</s>' means 'one who has gone forth subsequently.' Following whom? [The text] says: 'the <s>Jina</s>.' He is called <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) because he has conquered the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). [Or:] the evil qualities of the self are conquered by him, hence the approach to him. [Or:] because of the scripture saying 'spoken by the <s>Jina</s>.' The meaning is: one who utters the words 'I go forth following the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> who has gone forth.'

body.translated_text: Therefore, one who has gone for refuge to that <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> — this much [should be connected] with the phrase 'this is a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice), approved by the Sage.'

body.text: yāvajjīvaṃ vadhasteyamityādi | yāvajjīvamityanena kālāvadhi darśayati vadhaḥ prāṇātipātaḥ, steyaṃ cauryaṃ, maithunaṃ abrahmacaryaṃ, anṛtavākyaṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ | vadhaśca steyañca maithunaṃ cānṛtavākyaṃ ceti vadhasteyamaithunānṛtavākyaṃ | ataḥ kiṃ tasya, kiṃ virata iti paurastyena padena saṃbandhaḥ | kimetasmādeva yo virataḥ saṃvarī bhaṇyate? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi madyapānācca | surāmaireyamadyapānāccetyarthaḥ | (

children.translated_text: [SŚ 8]

children.text: ) atha surāmaireyamadyapānamiti ko 'rthaḥ? surānnāsavaḥ | maireyaṃ dravyāsavaḥ | te ca kadācit aprāptamadyasadbhāve bhavata iti | ato madyagrahaṇaṃ | pūgaphalakodravādayo madayantīti surāmaireyagrahaṇaṃ | mahoccairityādi | śerate 'sminnidrāṃ prayātīti śayanaṃ | āsyate 'sminniti upaviśanti āsanaṃ | mahoccaiśca śayanañcāsanañca mahoccaiḥ śayanāsanaṃ | ataḥ tasmāduccaśayanamahāśayanayoryo 'rthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, what is the meaning of 'liquor, spirits, and intoxicant-drinking'? <s>Surā</s> is grain-liquor. <s>Maireya</s> is substance-liquor. And these sometimes exist even when the actual state of intoxicant has not been attained. Therefore, the word '<s>madya</s>' (intoxicant) is used [additionally]. Betel-nut, <s>kodrava</s>-grain, and the like intoxicate — hence the use of '<s>surā</s>' and '<s>maireya</s>' [as well]. 'High [beds],' etc. That on which one lies down and goes to sleep is a bed (<s>śayana</s>). That on which one sits is a seat (<s>āsana</s>). High beds and seats together [constitute] '<s>mahoccaiḥ-śayanāsana</s>' (high beds and seats). Therefore, the meaning is: what pertains to high beds and great beds.

body.translated_text: 'As long as life [lasts], killing, stealing,' etc. 'As long as life' shows the time-limit. Killing (<s>vadha</s>) is taking life (<s>prāṇātipāta</s>). Theft (<s>steya</s>) is stealing (<s>caurya</s>). Sexual intercourse (<s>maithuna</s>) is unchastity (<s>abrahmacarya</s>). False speech (<s>anṛtavākya</s>) is lying (<s>mṛṣāvāda</s>). Killing and stealing and sexual intercourse and false speech — [the compound is:] killing-stealing-sexual-intercourse-and-false-speech. From these, what [about] him? [The question] 'Is he abstaining?' connects with the subsequent word. Is one called a 'restrainer' (<s>saṃvarī</s>) only from abstaining from these? No, [the text] says. What then? 'And from drinking liquor' — the meaning is: and from drinking liquor, spirits, and intoxicants.

body.text: nṛtyāderityādi | nartanaṃ nṛtyaṃ | bāhuvikṣepānnartanaṃ nṛtyaṃ | dvayordordaṇḍayoryadutkṣipya nartanaṃ nṛtyamucyate | tathā vakṣyate bāhuvikṣepakaṃ nṛtyamiti | ādiśabdena gītavāditrayorgrahaṇaṃ | tena nṛtyādiriti nṛtyagītavāditrādityarthaḥ | uccaiḥ svareṇa gāyanaṃ gītaṃ | vīṇāveṇumṛdaṅgādivāditravādanaṃ vāditramucyate | gandhamālyā[dyā]diti | gandhyata iti gandho ta ityarthaḥ | upayogo 'tra mālāyāṃ hitaṃ mālyaṃ campakāśokādikusumaṃ | ādau bhavamādyaṃ | ādyaśabdena vilepanasya grahaṇaṃ | tena gandhamālyavilepanādityarthaḥ | haritālādivarṇena vadanamrakṣaṇaṃ vilepanaṃ | vibhūṣaṇārtha vilepanaṃ vilepanamiti kṛtvā | vikālāśanata iti | atra sūryodayādāramya yāvat keśamātrāna tītako madhyāhnakālaśabdenābhidhīyate | vigataḥ sa īdṛgvidhaḥ kālo yasyāparāhṇādeḥ sa vikālaḥ | tasmin kāle 'śanaṃ bhojanaṃ | tasmādvikālāśanādityarthaḥ | tatheti | tathāśabdena yo virataḥ iti saṃbadhyate | rukmarūpyagrahācceti | rukmaṃ suvarṇa, rūpyaṃ rajataṃ, tayorgrahaṇaṃ rūkmarūpyagrahaṇa | ataḥ tasmājjātarūpaparajatapratigrahaṇāditi yāvat | eṣaḥ śrāmaṇero munermata iti | yaḥ prāṇātipā[tā]dvirataḥ yāvajjātarūparaja taparigrahāt sa eṣaḥ śrāmaṇero (

children.translated_text: [SŚ 9]

children.text: ) munermataḥ | buddhasya bhagavata iṣṭo 'bhipreta iti yāvat | yadyapi sarve buddhā bhagavantaḥ kāyavākcittamaunato muniriti sāmānyavācinā muniśabdenābhidhīyante, tathāpi bhagavataḥ śākyamunergrahaṇaṃ veditavyaṃ | tat śāsanapratipannatvādasmadādīnāṃ anyadīyaśāsanāntardhānācca | ślokabandhavaiguṇyāt śākyamunermata iti noktaṃ | śākyaśabdalopaṃ vā kṛtvā idaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ mu narmata iti | yathā satyabhāmābhāmeti | saṃkṣepatastaduktaṃ bhavati- ratnatraye śaraṇaṃ gatvā pañcaśikṣāpadāni parigṛhyabuddha bhagavantaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajāmīti vācamuccārya prāṇātipātādvirato yāvat jātarūparajataparigrahācca sa eṣa śrāmaṇero munermataḥ | abhipreta iti | āha cātra-
children.translated_text: approved by the Sage. [This means:] desired and intended by the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. Although all <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, are designated by the general term '<s>Muni</s>' (Sage) because of their silence of body, speech, and mind, nevertheless, it should be understood as referring to the Blessed <s>Śākyamuni</s>. That is because we and others are practitioners of his teaching, and because the teachings of others have disappeared. Due to the imperfection of verse-composition, it is not said '<s>Śākyamunermata</s>.' Or, having elided the word '<s>Śākya</s>,' this is stated as '<s>munermata</s>' (approved by the Sage) — just as [one says] '<s>Satyabhāmā-bhāmā</s>' [by elision]. In brief, this is what is stated: having gone for refuge to the Three Jewels (<s>Ratnatraya</s>), having accepted the five training precepts, having uttered the words 'I go forth following the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> who has gone forth,' one who is abstaining from taking life and so forth, up to the acceptance of gold and silver — he is this <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, approved by the Sage — that is, intended [by him]. And here it is said:

body.translated_text: 'Dancing,' etc. Dancing (<s>nartana</s>) is <s>nṛtya</s>. Dancing with throwing up the arms is <s>nṛtya</s>. Lifting up both arms and dancing is called <s>nṛtya</s>. As it will be stated: 'Throwing up the arms is dancing.' By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), singing and instrumental music are included. Thus 'dancing etc.' means 'dancing, singing, instrumental music, etc.' Singing aloud is '<s>gīta</s>' (song). Playing instruments such as the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), <s>veṇu</s> (flute), <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drum), etc. is called '<s>vāditra</s>' (instrumental music). 'Perfumes, garlands, etc.' — that which is smelled is perfume (<s>gandha</s>); that is the meaning. What is used for a garland (<s>mālā</s>) is '<s>mālya</s>' — [namely] flowers of <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, and the like. 'Ādya' (the first) [means] that which comes at the beginning. By the word '<s>ādya</s>,' ointment (<s>vilepana</s>) is included. Thus the meaning is: perfumes, garlands, and ointments, etc. Anointing the face with substances such as yellow orpiment is ointment. Ointment [is defined as] anointing for the purpose of adornment. 'From eating at improper times' — here, from sunrise until the time when the sun has not crossed beyond even a hair's breadth, the midday time is denoted by the word '<s>kāla</s>' (proper time). When such a proper time has passed, [meaning] from the afternoon onward, that is the improper time (<s>vikāla</s>). Eating food at that time [is improper-time eating]. Therefore the meaning is: from eating at improper times. 'Thus' — by the word 'thus,' it connects with 'one who is abstaining.' 'And from accepting gold and silver' — '<s>rukma</s>' is gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>); '<s>rūpya</s>' is silver (<s>rajata</s>); accepting both of them is the acceptance of gold and silver. Therefore, the meaning is: from accepting gold and silver. 'This is a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, approved by the Sage' — one who is abstaining from taking life and so forth, up to the acceptance of gold and silver — he is this <s>śrāmaṇera</s>,

children.translated_text: 'First, having given the three refuges and the five training precepts,
one should afterward shave the hair of the aspirant to the vows and bathe him.
One should give him the saffron-colored robe and then cause him to go forth.
The ten training precepts — thus declare those who know the <s>Vinaya</s>.'

body.text: idānīṃ śrāmaṇerabhāvopāyaḥ nirdiśyate | eṣāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāmācārasaṃgrahamārabhate | sakalena śarīreṇetyādi | tatra śīryante 'sminnaṅgānīti śarīraṃ | tacca kaścit pradeśo 'pi saṃbhavati ityataḥ sakalagrahaṇaṃ | tena sakalena śarīreṇa sarveṇa prakāreṇa kāyenetyarthaḥ | śarīrānyatareṇa veti | hastapādamastakādisamudāyasyānyatareṇa hastādinetyarthaḥ | śarīrāvayavena hastapādādinā gṛhītaṃ śarīrapratibaddhaṃ | śarīravyatiriktena latālaguḍenetyarthaḥ | na hanyānna mārayet | kamityāha | prāṇinaṃ | prāṇonāma vāyuḥ, so 'syāstīti prāṇī | sa ca kiṃ viśiṣṭa eva? pañcaśākhādi nirvṛttaḥ parigṛhayate | ataḥ kalalādiśātane saṃvaratyāgo na bhavati | prāṇiśabdena ca manuṣyagatiparyāyaḥ eva gṛhayate na prāṇimātraṃ, sajantukasalilādiparibhoge duṣkṛtavacanāt | jātivācī vāyaṃ śabdaḥ | tena strīpuruṣapaṇḍakaṃ pañcaśākhādi[nir]vṛttaṃ mārayataḥ syādeva saṃvaratyāgaḥ | anena ślokena kāyiko vikramaḥ pratiṣiddho bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Now the means of attaining the state of a novice (<s>śrāmaṇera</s>) is explained. He commences the code of conduct (<s>ācārasaṃgraha</s>) for these novices, [beginning with] 'with the entire body' and so forth. There, '<s>śarīra</s>' (body) is [etymologically explained as] 'that in which the limbs break down' (<s>śīryante 'smin aṅgāni</s>). And since that could also refer to just a part [of the body], the word 'entire' (<s>sakala</s>) is used. Thus, 'with the entire body' means 'with the body in every way.' 'Or with any one [part] of the body' — means with any one [part] such as the hand, foot, or head from the aggregate [of limbs]. 'With a bodily limb' — with a hand, foot, etc. — [means] grasped [by] or connected to the body. 'With something other than the body' means with a vine, a stick, etc. 'One should not strike, should not kill.' Whom? He says: 'a living being' (<s>prāṇin</s>). <s>Prāṇa</s> means the vital breath (wind); one who possesses it is a <s>prāṇin</s>. And is this restricted to a specific [type]? Only five-limbed beings and the like are included. Therefore, in the destruction of an embryo at the <s>kalala</s> stage, there is no loss of restraint (<s>saṃvaratyāga</s>). And by the word '<s>prāṇin</s>,' only synonyms for the human realm are meant, not all living beings indiscriminately, because there is a separate statement of wrongdoing regarding the use of water containing organisms and the like. Or this word denotes a class. Therefore, when killing a woman, man, or <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch) — a five-limbed being — there is indeed a loss of restraint. By this verse, bodily violence is prohibited.

body.text: vācikavikramapratiṣedhapadamāha | mṛtyorvarṇamityādi | mṛtyurjīvitendriyanirodhaḥ | tasya varṇaḥ praśaṃsā, taṃ na bhāṣeta | na vadedityarthaḥ | kṛtapuṇyo bhavān, udyānayātrā tava paralokagamanamiti śrutvā kaścidātmāna hanyāt | tadidānīṃ atra duṣkṛtapūrvakaḥ saṃvaratyāga iti pratiṣidhyate | mṛtyorvarṇa na bhāṣayet, śastrahāraṃ na caiṣayediti | śastraṃ harati vahatīti vā śastrahāro vadhyaghātakaḥ | tatra paryeṣayet | vadhakena māraṇābhiprāyeṇa | cittena manasā | māraṇāya māraṇārthaṃ | na niyojayediti ||
body.translated_text: He states the prohibition of verbal violence: 'the description of death' and so forth. Death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) is the cessation of the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>). Its 'description' (<s>varṇa</s>) means praise thereof; one should not speak it — meaning one should not utter it. [For example, if one says:] 'You are meritorious; your excursion to the park is [really] your journey to the next world,' and upon hearing this, someone kills himself — in that case, it is hereby prohibited as a loss of restraint preceded by a wrongful act. 'One should not praise death, nor should one seek an executioner' — '<s>śastrahāra</s>' (weapon-bearer) is [explained as] one who takes up or carries a weapon, i.e., an executioner. 'Should seek' means with the intention of killing by the executioner. 'With the mind' — mentally. 'For the purpose of killing' — for the sake of killing. 'One should not engage [another to kill].'

body.text: pūrvoktaparyāyavyatirekai ranyairapi prayogairmārayataḥ saṃvaratyāgo bhavatīti pratipādayannāha | virekavamanālepeti vistaraḥ | tatra virekaṃ grastanaṃ, vamanaṃ chardanaṃ | ālepena varṇānyathātve sati vinaśyati | viṣaṃ jātimaṃ kṛtrimañca, śastraṃ kuliśādi | virekaśca vamanaṃ cālepanaṃ cetyādi dvandvaḥ | teṣāmabhisaṃskaraṇamabhisaṃskṛtiḥ | tāṃ na kuryāt | kimartha? prāṇighātāya manuṣyavadhārthaṃ | na ca garbhasya śā[ta]namiti | garbhaśātanaṃ na kuryādityarthaḥ | kecit garbhaśātananimittaṃ virekādikaṃ na kuryāditi nimittasaptamīṃ varṇayanti ||
body.translated_text: To demonstrate that killing by other means beyond those previously mentioned also results in loss of restraint, he says: 'purgative, emetic, ointment' and so forth in detail. There, 'purgative' (<s>vireka</s>) is swallowing [medicines]; 'emetic' (<s>vamana</s>) is inducing vomiting. Through 'ointment' (<s>ālepa</s>), when the complexion is altered, [the person] perishes. 'Poison' (<s>viṣa</s>) is both natural and manufactured. 'Weapon' (<s>śastra</s>) is a thunderbolt and the like. 'Purgative, emetic, and ointment' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Their 'preparation' (<s>abhisaṃskṛti</s>) means the act of preparing them. One should not do that. For what purpose? 'For the slaying of a living being' — for the purpose of killing a human. 'Nor should one cause the destruction of an embryo' — meaning one should not cause abortion. Some interpret the locative as causal: 'one should not administer purgatives and the like for the purpose of causing abortion.'

body.text: na kevalaṃ amunā prayogeṇa mārayituṃ na labhyate maraṇanimittamātramapi kartuṃ na sulabhyata iti pratipādayannāha | nimittaṃ na vratī kuryādityādi | nimittaṃ liṅgaṃ na kuryāt | ko na kuryādityāha | vratī | kaiḥ? svapnolūkādivāśitaiḥ | svapna iti pañca svapnāḥ | svapnālīkānantācīrṇā satyākhyaṃ svapnapañcakamiti vacanāt | ulūkādīnāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ, vāśitāni ruditāni | svapnāśca ulūkādivāśitāni cetyarthaḥ | taiḥ | ādiśabdena nāmagotradānādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ | tacca trividhaṃ dharmāmiṣābhayabhedena | āmiṣadānamapi dvividhaṃ vāhyādhyātmikabhedena | dauḥśīlaṃ śīlaviratiḥ prakṛtisāvadyāt prajñaptisāvadyāt bhagavatā pratiṣiddhādvikālabhojanādeḥ duḥkhatāpopa śamanādapratisārā dinā prahlāditvena śītalatvācchīlaṃ, sukhaṃ śīlasamādānaṃ kāyo na paritapyata iti gāthāvacanāt | śītībhāvaṃ nirvāṇakrameṇa lātītiśīlaṃ | phalāni catvāri srotāpattiphalaṃ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ anāgāmiphalaṃ arhatphalaṃ | (

children.text: ) phalānāmāptirlābhaḥ | dānañca śīlañca phalāptiśceti dānaśīlaphalāpta[ya]ḥ | ataḥ tābhiriti saṃbandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) The attainment of the fruits is 'gain' (<s>lābha</s>). Giving, morality, and the attainment of fruits — these are '<s>dānaśīlaphalāptayaḥ</s>.' Therefore, the connection is with 'by those.'

body.translated_text: To demonstrate that not only is it impermissible to kill by these means, but even creating mere conditions for death is impermissible, he says: 'A vow-observer should not create an omen' and so forth. 'An omen' (<s>nimitta</s>) is a sign; one should not create it. Who should not? He says: 'a vow-observer' (<s>vratī</s>). By what [omens]? 'By dreams, owl-cries, and the like.' 'Dreams' means the five types of dreams; as the saying goes: 'Dreams, false [visions], unending [dreams], [dreams] walked through, and those called true — these are the fivefold dreams.' 'Of owls and other birds' — 'cries' means their calls. 'Dreams and the cries of owls, etc.' is the meaning. By those [omens]. The word 'etc.' includes the taking of names, clan-names, gifts, and the like. And that [gift] is threefold, distinguished as <s>dharma</s>-gift, material gift, and gift of fearlessness. Material gift is also twofold, distinguished as external and internal. 'Misconduct' (<s>dauḥśīla</s>) is abstention from morality — from what is naturally blameworthy, from what is conventionally blameworthy, and from what was prohibited by the Blessed One such as eating at improper times. Because it removes the burning of suffering, because it brings no remorse, because it brings delight, because it is cooling — it is called '<s>śīla</s>' (morality); as stated in the verse: 'The observance of morality is pleasant; the body is not tormented.' '<s>Śīla</s>' [also means] that which leads to cooling in the course of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The fruits are four: the fruit of stream-entry (<s>Srotaāpatti</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>Sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>Anāgāmin</s>), and the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>.

body.text: vadhakenāpi cittena bhrāntyā mārayataḥ saṃvaratyāgo na bhavatī ti darśayannāha | madhyapaścātpurogeṣviti vistaraḥ | madhye paścāt puro gacchantīti madhyapaścātpurogāḥ | atasteṣu madhyapaścātpurogeṣu manuṣyeṣu gacchatsu yatraiva vadhakaṃ manaḥ yasminneva puruṣe vadhakacittaṃ tameva puruṣaṃ dhnato mārayataḥ | asyeti śrāmaṇerasya | hiṃsā prāṇivadhaḥ | nānyaṃ tasmātpuruṣādanyaṃ puruṣaṃ bhrāntyā mārayataḥ asya hiṃsā na bhavatītyarthaḥ | ka evamāha | ityato bravīti | āha sarvavit | sarvaṃ vettīti sarvavit, bhagavān buddhaḥ | sa evamāhetyanenāptāgamaṃ darśayati ||
body.translated_text: To show that even when one kills with murderous intent but by mistake [kills the wrong person], there is no loss of restraint, he says: 'among those in the middle, behind, and in front' in detail. 'Those who go in the middle, behind, and in front' — i.e., those walking in the middle, behind, and in front. Therefore, among those walking in the middle, behind, and in front — among those humans — toward whomever the murderous mind is directed, toward whichever person the murderous intent exists, only that very person [must be killed for it to count]. 'Of this one' — of this novice. '<s>Hiṃsā</s>' means killing a living being. 'Not another' — when killing another person different from that [intended] person by mistake, 'there is no <s>hiṃsā</s> for this one' — meaning there is no [offense of] violence. Who says so? Therefore he says: 'The Omniscient' (<s>sarvavit</s>) — one who knows everything, the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>. By saying 'He said thus,' he indicates the authority of a trusted source (<s>āptāgama</s>).

body.text:
anyadapi prayogāntaraṃ na kāryaṃ māraṇāyeti darśayannāha | kūṭetyādi | kūṭamiti pāśaṃ varṇayanti | avamārthamiti pāśayantraṃ | avaṣṭambhamiti yantrameva, yena sahasākramya hanyāt | avapayamiti avapātaṃ varṇayanti | mantribhiḥ mantraprabhāvena mṛtake piśācādipraveśanaṃ vetālaḥ | kūṭādīnāmabhisaṃskaraṇamabhisaṃskṛtiḥ |
tāmavapayañca kiṃ na kuryāt? māraṇāya śarīriṇāṃ sattvānāṃ | anyathā tu na doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text:
To show that yet another device should not be employed for killing, he says: '<s>kūṭa</s>' and so forth. '<s>Kūṭa</s>' is explained as a snare (<s>pāśa</s>). '<s>Avamārtha</s>' is a snare-trap. '<s>Avaṣṭambha</s>' is a mechanism itself, by which one may seize and kill suddenly. '<s>Avapaya</s>' is explained as a pitfall. 'Through <s>mantras</s>' — by the power of incantations, the entry of a <s>piśāca</s> (spirit) or the like into a dead body is a <s>vetāla</s> (animated corpse). The 'preparation' (<s>abhisaṃskṛti</s>) of snares and the like [is their construction].
Those and the pitfall — why should they not be prepared? 'For the killing of embodied beings' (<s>śarīriṇām</s>). Otherwise, there is no fault.

children.translated_text: A snare is called '<s>kūṭaka</s>'; '<s>avamārtha</s>' is a snare-mechanism;
'<s>Avapaya</s>' is a pitfall, and the mechanism called '<s>stambha</s>' (pillar-trap) [is yet another type].

body.text: iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus the summary verse.

body.text: mṛtyuhetoḥ sthānopadeśamātramapi kartuṃ na labhyate iti darśayitumāha | taskaretyādi | taskaraḥ cauraḥ | ahiḥ sarpaḥ | senā yuddhāya ekatra sannipātaḥ | śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ | caurādibhyo bhayaṃ yatra yasmin mārge pathi bhavati tasya panthānaṃ dehināṃ prāṇināṃ nāśāya vināśārthaṃ yatirna kathayet ||
body.translated_text: To show that even merely indicating a location that could lead to death is impermissible, he says: 'a thief' and so forth. '<s>Taskara</s>' is a robber. '<s>Ahi</s>' is a serpent. '<s>Senā</s>' (army) is a gathering in one place for the purpose of battle. The rest is easy to understand. 'Where there is danger from thieves and the like' — on whichever road or path — 'for the destruction of living beings' — for the purpose of destruction — 'a renunciant should not point out that road.'

body.text: viṣamanadīpratāraṇamapi tartuṃ na kalpayati tamiti darśayitumāha | bhujagetyādi | bhujābhyāṃ gacchatīti bhujagaḥ sapaḥ | āvarto vegī | bhujagaścāvartakaśceti dvandvaḥ | teṣāṃ bhayaṃ | yatra yasyā nadyāḥ tīrthe bhayaṃ bhavet tattīrthaṃ na prakāśayet ||
body.translated_text: To show that one should not even arrange the crossing of a dangerous river [for destructive purpose], he says: '<s>bhujaga</s>' and so forth. '<s>Bhujaga</s>' — one who goes by means of its coils — is a serpent. '<s>Āvarta</s>' is a whirlpool. '<s>Bhujaga</s> and <s>āvarta</s>' is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. 'Their danger' — where there is danger from them. 'At whichever ford of whichever river there is danger, one should not reveal that ford.'

body.text: kiñca rājñā vā yatra ghātyate tanmārgaṃ na prakāśayediti daṇḍādidānapratiṣedhopāyena paraṃ ghātayituṃ na kṣamata iti darśayitumāha | kiñcidbhūpataya ityādi | bhūḥ pṛthvī, tāṃ pālayatīti bhapatiḥ rājā | bhūpataye rājñe kiñcidapi mā dāstvaṃ | kiñcidapi dravyaṃ mā dāsyasītyarthaḥ | varaṃ jīvitaṃ tyajeti | jīvitaparityāgaṃ varaṃ kuru tvamityarthaḥ | ityevaṃ samucitaṃ pratyāyādānārtha pratibaddhasya puruṣa syāntike 'yuktaṃ ayuktarūpaṃ vacanaṃ na vadedityeke | bhadantaparahitaghoṣastvāha | ā | samantāt sarvatra kārye niyuktaḥ ityāyuktaḥ vyāpṛtaka ucyate, tenāyuktena baddhaḥ saṃruddha yo 'nyaḥ puruṣaḥ tasmin baddhāyukte puruṣe ityevaṃ na vadet | varaṃ mriyasva mā tvaṃ kiñcit dravyaṃ rājñe dehīti | anyathā hi yaḥ saruddho vyāpṛtakaḥ tasmin baddhāyukta ityevaṃ na vadedityarthaḥ pūrvavat | anyathā varaṃ mriyasva mā tvaṃ kiñcidayuktāya dehi ityuktaṃ syāt | na bhūpataya iti niyuktairnānyasya puruṣasya baddhatvāt ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, to show that one should not reveal a road where the king executes [people], and that one is not permitted to cause another's death by the means of imposing fines and the like, he says: 'something to the king' and so forth. '<s>Bhūpati</s>' — one who protects (<s>pālayati</s>) the earth (<s>bhū</s>) — is a king. 'Do not give even a little to the king' — meaning 'do not give even a small amount of wealth.' '[It is] better to give up your life' — meaning 'consider the abandonment of your life as preferable.' 'Thus [one should not speak] inappropriate words to a person who is bound [by the king's officer] for the purpose of extracting [payment]' — this is [the view of] some. But the venerable <s>Parahitaghoṣa</s> says: '<s>Āyukta</s>' — one who is employed everywhere in all affairs — means an officer (<s>vyāpṛtaka</s>); 'bound by the officer' means a person who is restrained and confined by such an officer. To such a bound person, one should not say: 'It is better to die than to give anything to the king.' Otherwise [interpreted], regarding one who is restrained as an officer — to such a '<s>baddhāyukta</s>' (bound officer) — one should not speak thus, as before. Otherwise, it would [wrongly] mean: 'It is better to die than to give anything to one who is not an officer.' [The correct reading is:] 'Not to the king' — because another person is bound by the appointed [officers].

body.text:
sabhayaṃ layanaṃ vadhakacittenopadeṣṭuṃ na kalpata iti darśayannāha | bhujagetyādi | atra vihāraśabdena layanamevocyate viharantyasminniti kṛtvā | tenāyaṃ vākyārtho jāyate
| (

children.text: ) yasmin layane sarpādibhayaṃ bhavati tadvadhakābhi prāyeṇāgantukāyabhikṣave noddiśet | ya uddiśati tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati asati maraṇe, maraṇe tu saṃvaratyāgo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ) One should not, with murderous intent, point out to a visiting <s>bhikṣu</s> a lodging where there is danger from serpents and the like. One who points it out incurs a wrongful act (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) if death does not occur; but if death does occur, there is a loss of restraint (<s>saṃvaratyāga</s>).

body.translated_text: To show that one should not point out a dangerous dwelling with murderous intent, he says: '<s>bhujaga</s>' and so forth. Here, by the word '<s>vihāra</s>' (dwelling), only '<s>layana</s>' (lodging) is meant, because [beings] dwell (<s>viharanti</s>) in it. Therefore this sentence-meaning arises:

body.text: marjārādivyapadeśenāpi śatru mārayannayatirbhavatīti pratipādayitumāha | vyāghrādivyapadeśenetyādi | yaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ śaṭhajātīyaḥ vyāghraṃ hanmīti vyapadeśaṃ kṛtvā śatruṃ hanyāt sa vihārād ghaṭṭanīyaḥ | āśu śīghraṃ | asau cellakairnirdvāraṇīyaḥ | vairiṇi mṛte satīti boddhavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: To demonstrate that even one who kills an enemy under the pretext of [killing] a cat etc. becomes [a fallen] ascetic, he says 'under the pretext of a tiger, etc.' Whichever <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice), being of a deceitful nature, having made the pretext 'I shall kill a tiger,' kills an enemy — he should be expelled from the monastery (<s>vihāra</s>). Quickly, swiftly! That one should be expelled by the attendants (<s>cellakas</s>) through [formal] expulsion. It should be understood [that this applies] when the enemy has died.

body.text: adhārmikakriyākāramapi pratiṣedhayati tathā kāryamityādinā | tathā kartavyaṃ yathā na jovedekāpyariḥ śatruriti | evamarīn śatrūn | yatiḥ | adharmyā na kriyā, adhārmikakriyākāro na kāryaḥ | saṃsmṛtya krakacopama iti | krakacena karayantreṇa upamā yasmin mṛte tadevamucyate | tattu saṃsmṛtya kiṃ? adhārmikakriyākāro na kārya iti saṃbandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: He prohibits even the appearance of unrighteous conduct, saying 'thus it should be done, etc.' It should be done in such a way that not even one enemy is [harmed] — [the word] 'ari' [means] enemy — thus enemies [should not be harmed by] an ascetic (<s>yati</s>). Unrighteous conduct (<s>adhārmika-kriyā-kāra</s>) should not be performed. 'Remembering the saw simile' — '<s>krakaca</s>' is a hand-saw instrument; when someone dies [under torture with it], it is said thus. Remembering that, what [follows]? The connection is: unrighteous conduct should not be performed.

body.text: paraprayogeṇāpi mārayannayatirbhavatīti darśayati | vadhā ityādi | eko dvau trayo vāpi ye śrāmaṇerā vadhīkṛtā māraṇābhiprāyato | yugapadekakālaṃ | tat prayoga iti | ghātayituṃ | śrāmaṇerasya prayogeṇa manuṣyaṃ mārayati, te vihārānnāśayitavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: He shows that even one who kills through another's agency becomes [a fallen] ascetic, saying 'killing, etc.' One, two, or three <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> who have been made killers (<s>vadhīkṛtā</s>) — with murderous intent. Simultaneously, at one time. 'By that instigation' — to cause to kill. [When] a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, through his own instigation, kills a human being, they should be expelled from the monastery.

body.text: ebhiraṅgairmanuṣyavadho bhavatīti darśayan parāṃścodayannāha | upakrama ityādi | tatra śastrādigrahaṇamupakramaḥ | manuṣyo 'yamiti saṃjñā nṛsaṃjñā | kadācidupakramaṃ karoti nṛsaṃjñānavati na tvasau manuṣya ityāha | nara iti | yadyasau manuṣyo bhavati | kadācidetāni trīṇyaṅgāni saṃbhavanti, na vadhakacetaneti | ato vadhakacetanāvacanaṃ | kadācidupakramaḥ prajñāyate, nṛsaṃjñā vadhakace[ta]nāvān ca naro bhavate, na tu jīvitādvyaparopayatīti | ata āha | jīvitasya kṣayaśceti | tadupakrama ityekamaṅgaṃ, nṛsaṃjñā ceti dvitīyamaṅgaṃ, nara iti tṛtīyamaṅgaṃ, vadhakacetaneti caturthamaṅgaṃ, jīvitakṣayaśceti pañca[mama]ṅgaṃ ityetāni pañcāṅgāni nṛghātane manuṣyavadhe veditavyāni | kecittu mandadhiyaḥ prāhuḥ | nare vadhakacetaneti saptamyantaṃ paṭhanti | teṣāṃ pañcāṅgāni na siddhyanti nare vadhakacetanetyasya padasyaikāṅgatvāt | vinayaśca tairvilopito bhavati | eṣa hi vinaye nirdeśaḥ | prāṇī ca bhavati, prāṇisaṃjñī ca bhavati, vadhakacittañca pratyupasthitaṃ bhavati, upakramañca karoti, jīvitā dravyaparopito bhavati iyatā prāṇātipātī bhavati | atra ca prāṇī bhavati ityādi sarvaḥ prathamānto nirdeśaḥ | tathā kārikāntareṇāpi upakrama iti nṛsaṃjñāvadhakacetaneti prathamāntanirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ | tasmāt prathamānta eva nirdeśaḥ avagantavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Showing that homicide consists of these factors, and addressing the other aspects, he says 'preparation (<s>upakrama</s>), etc.' Therein, the taking up of weapons etc. is the preparation (<s>upakrama</s>). The cognition 'this is a human being' is the perception of a human (<s>nṛsaṃjñā</s>). Sometimes one makes a preparation without the cognition that [the victim] is a human — therefore he says '[it must be] a person (<s>nara</s>)' — meaning if that [victim] is indeed a human. Sometimes these three factors are present, but not the intention to kill (<s>vadhaka-cetanā</s>) — therefore the statement about murderous intention. Sometimes the preparation is manifest, the perception of a human and the murderous intention are present, and it is a person, yet [the killer] does not deprive [the victim] of life — therefore he says 'and the destruction of life.' Thus: 'preparation' is the first factor; 'perception of a human' is the second factor; 'a person' is the third factor; 'murderous intention' is the fourth factor; 'destruction of life' is the fifth factor — these five factors should be known in the slaying of a human, in homicide. However, certain dull-witted persons say [otherwise] — they read 'in a person, murderous intention' with a locative ending. For them, the five factors are not established, since 'in a person, murderous intention' would be a single factor. And the <s>Vinaya</s> would be distorted by them. For this is the statement in the <s>Vinaya</s>: '[The victim] is a living being, and [the killer] has the cognition of a living being, and the mind of killing is present, and he makes a preparation, and [the victim] is deprived of life — by this much one becomes a destroyer of life (<s>prāṇātipātin</s>).' And here, '[the victim] is a living being' etc. — the entire statement is in the nominative case. Likewise, by another verse too, 'preparation' and 'perception of a human' and 'murderous intention' — the statement is made in the nominative. Therefore, the statement should be understood as nominative only.

body.text: viṣaśastrādiprayogeṇāpi mārayituṃ na nirdiśyata iti darśayannāha | śrāmaṇeretyādi | yadviṣaśastrādi yatinā prayuktaṃ narasya nāśāya, yadi tenaiva prayogeṇa naro mriyate tadāsau prayoktāsaṃvarī saṃvarādbhraśyate | athānyadīyena tadā neti anenāsyāpattirbhavatīti kathayati ||
body.translated_text: Showing that even killing by means of poison, weapons, etc. is not prescribed [as legitimate], he says 'of the <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, etc.' Whatever poison, weapon, etc. is employed by an ascetic (<s>yati</s>) for the destruction of a person — if by that very means the person dies, then that perpetrator loses his <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic vow), falling from the <s>saṃvara</s>. But if [the person dies] by another's [means], then he says 'no' — [meaning] thereby no offense accrues to him.

body.text: avakrītādirityādi | eṣa yatiḥ kenacidavakrīto bhavati | yo bhṛtako vā sa vinayānabhijñatvāt, vinayajño 'pi cānusmaraṇāt | ādiśabdena dveṣābhibhavāt | avakrītādeḥ saṃvaratyāgo [na] bhavatīti matvā naraṃ mārayet | mārayan saṃvarakṣobhalābhī bhavati | nonmattādikaḥ | unmattavikṣiptacetasastu śrāmaṇerā mārayanto na dauḥ śīlyabhājo bhavanti smṛterabhāvāt |
body.translated_text: 'Hired (<s>avakrīta</s>), etc.' This ascetic is hired by someone. Or one who is a hired servant (<s>bhṛtaka</s>) — [kills] through ignorance of the <s>Vinaya</s>, or even if knowledgeable of the <s>Vinaya</s>, through lack of mindfulness. The word 'etc.' [includes killing] due to being overpowered by hatred. One who has been hired etc., thinking that [there will be] no abandonment of <s>saṃvara</s> [vow], kills a person. Killing, he incurs the disturbance of the <s>saṃvara</s>. But not one who is insane etc. — <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> who are insane or mentally deranged, when they kill, do not incur moral fault (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), because of the absence of mindfulness.

body.text: sattvapīḍākriyāyāḥ kāraṇamāha | kāyetyādinā | kaṃ ruṇaddhīti karuṇā | tasyāṃ bhavāḥ kāruṇikāḥ | tathā hi paraduḥkhaduḥkhino buddhā bhagavantaḥ, taiḥ kāruṇikaiḥ maitraṃ kāyakarma maitraṃ vākkarma maitraṃ manaḥ karma prāṇiṣu sattveṣu sarvadā sarvasmin kāle kartavyaṃ yatinā śrāmaṇereṇeti | evamuktamabhihitaṃ | yasmāt yataḥ kāraṇāt | asmādanantaroktāddhetoḥ kimityāha | na sattvān pīḍayediti ślokaḥ | sattvānāṃ pīḍāṃ na kuryāt | kairityāha | dārurajjvayaścarmabandhanaiḥ | tatra dāru kāṣṭhaṃ | rajju guṇamayī kriyā | ayo lohaḥ | carma vadadhrī | teṣāṃ bandhanāni atastaiḥ | analo 'gniḥ | jalañcānalaśca jalānalau | tatra nimajjajjalaṃ jalānalapraveśaḥ | anu tyaktaṃtasya tyajanaṃ anutyāgaḥ | ādiśabdena viṣabhakṣaṇādikaṃ grāhayati | jalānalapraveśaścānutyāgaśceti dvandvaḥ | tasminna niyojayet ||
body.translated_text: He states the reason for [the prohibition of] harming beings, saying 'bodily, etc.' '<s>Karuṇā</s>' (compassion) is that which obstructs [suffering] (<s>ka</s>). Those who possess it are '<s>kāruṇikas</s>' (compassionate ones). For thus the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, suffer at the suffering of others. By those compassionate ones — friendly bodily action, friendly verbal action, and friendly mental action toward living beings should be performed at all times, in every circumstance, by the ascetic (<s>yati</s>), by the <s>śrāmaṇera</s>. Thus has it been said. Since, for what reason? — from the cause just stated, what [follows]? He says: 'One should not harm beings' — this is the verse. One should not inflict harm on beings. By what means? He says: by wood, rope, iron, and leather bindings. Therein, 'wood' means a stick (<s>kāṣṭha</s>); 'rope' means a cord made of fiber; 'iron' means metal; 'leather' means a hide-strap. Their bindings, therefore by those. 'Fire' means flame. Water and fire — immersion in water and entering into fire. 'Abandonment' (<s>anutyāga</s>) means the forsaking of [a being in distress]. The word 'etc.' includes the eating of poison and the like. 'Immersion in water and fire, and abandonment' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound). One should not subject [beings] to these.

body.text: kṛmigorūpetyādi | kṛmigīrūpādīnāṃ vihiṃsanaṃ mithyājīvaśca karṣaṇe sati yasmāt kāraṇāt bhavati tasmāddhetoḥ karṣaṇa dūrādeva tyajet ||
body.translated_text: 'Worms, cows, etc.' Since the harming of worms, cows, and similar creatures, as well as wrong livelihood (<s>mithyājīva</s>), arise from plowing — for that reason, one should abandon plowing from afar [i.e., completely avoid it].

body.text: nāṅkayedomahiṣyādi | gomahiṣyādirnāṅkayitavyo, na cāsya gomahiṣyādernāsikāṃ vedhayet, na ca vetrādinā tāḍayet ||
body.translated_text: 'One should not brand cows, buffaloes, etc.' Cows, buffaloes, and similar [animals] should not be branded, nor should their noses be pierced, nor should they be beaten with a rod (<s>vetra</s>) or the like.

body.text: uddiśyetyādi | śrāmaṇeramuddiśya matsyādikaṃ jīvitādvyaparopayet | vyaparopya tasya māṃsena yadvyañjanaṃ kṛtaṃ tat bhakṣayato yateḥ śrāmaṇerasya yasmānnighṛṇaṃ niṣkṛpaṃ cittaṃ jāyate | ataḥ kadācit uddiśya kṛtaṃ bhakṣayan lobhānalenāpūryamāṇaḥ prāṇivadhamapi kuryāt iti hiṃsā yasya saṃbhāvyate | tasmāduddiśya kṛtaṃ na bhakṣaṇīyamityabhiprāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Specifically, etc.' [If] fish and the like are killed specifically for a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, deprived of life, and a dish (<s>vyañjana</s>) is prepared from that meat — when the ascetic, the <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, eats it, a merciless (<s>nighṛṇa</s>), pitiless (<s>niṣkṛpa</s>) mind arises. Therefore, at some point, eating what was specifically prepared, being filled with the fire of greed, he might even commit the killing of living beings — thus violence is to be expected of him. Therefore, what is specifically prepared should not be eaten — this is the intended meaning.

body.text: taduddiśya kṛtaṃ kathaṃ boddhavyamityāha | jñeyaṃ tu tribhirākārairityādi | abhrāntimatā nirīkṣitena śrutena śaṅkitena vā taduddiśya kṛtaṃ boddhavyaṃ | eṣāmeva padānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ cikīrṣurāha | īkṣitaṃ yat svayaṃ dṛṣṭamityādi | ātmanāyaddṛṣṭaṃ tadīkṣitamucyate | pratyāyitenāvisaṃvādakena tu yaduktaṃ tat śrutamucyate ||
body.translated_text: He says how one should know that something was specifically prepared, with 'It should be known by three signs, etc.' By one who is not confused — by seeing (<s>nirīkṣita</s>), hearing (<s>śruta</s>), or suspecting (<s>śaṅkita</s>) — one should know that it was specifically prepared. Wishing to define these very terms, he says: 'What is seen by oneself, etc.' What is seen by oneself — that is called 'seen' (<s>īkṣita</s>). What is reported by a trustworthy person, one who does not deceive — that is called 'heard' (<s>śruta</s>).

body.text: āśaṅkāmadhikṛtyāha | gṛhābaddhetyādi | gṛhābaddhā ye pakṣimṛgaśūkarādayaḥ teṣāṃ yat pakṣaśṛṅgādi [tad]darśanāt- kimete mṛgapakṣiśūkarādayo mamoddiśya hatā na veti āśaṅkā utpadyate | satyāmāśaṅkāyāṃ dānapatiḥ praṣṭavyaḥ- kimete mamoddiśya hatā na veti | pṛṣṭo dātetyādi | yadidaṃ dānapatiḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sannevaṃ vadet- tvannimittaṃ tavārthe 'mī mṛgādayo hatā iti | evaṃ sati tasmin gṛhe na bhuñjīta | uddiśya kṛtatvāttasyeti bhāvaḥ | virataḥ prāṇināṃ vadhādityanena gṛhītaśikṣasyāyaṃ pratiṣedho netarasyeti darśayati | śyenakādihatā vetyādi | atha sa dānapatirevaṃ (

children.text: ) kuryāt | śyenakādibhiramī hatā mṛtāḥ pakṣiṇo hatāḥ | śāliyavamudbhakṣaṇādvā mṛtāḥ | mātāpitroryajñasya kṛte hatā ityevaṃ sati doṣāsti nāśnatāṃ | evaṃ dātari bruvāṇe sati bhuñjānānāṃ na kaściddoṣo bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'These birds were killed by hawks and the like, or died from eating rice and barley, or were killed for the sacrifice of the parents' — in such a case, there is no fault for those who eat. When the donor speaks thus, there is no fault whatsoever for those who eat — this is the meaning.

body.translated_text: Addressing suspicion, he says 'bound in a household, etc.' Those birds, deer, boars, and the like that are bound in a household — from seeing their wings, horns, and the like, the suspicion arises: 'Were these deer, birds, boars, etc. killed specifically for me or not?' When such suspicion arises, the donor (<s>dānapati</s>) should be asked: 'Were these killed specifically for me or not?' 'When asked, [the donor] gives, etc.' — if the donor, when asked, says thus: 'On your account, for your sake, these deer and the like were killed' — in that case, one should not eat in that household, because it was specifically prepared — this is the meaning. By [the phrase] 'one who has ceased from the killing of living beings,' he shows that this prohibition applies to one who has undertaken the training, not to others. 'Killed by hawks, etc.' — now, if that donor should say thus:

body.text: ekaṃ śrīghanamuddiśyetyādi | yadyekaṃ śrāmaṇeramārabhya kṛtaṃ matsyādikaṃ māsaṃ vyañjanaṃ tadanyeṣāmapi śrāmaṇerāṇāṃ yatīnāṃ bhogāya na kalpate | bhikṣubhikṣuṇyopāsakopāsikānāṃ samuddiśya kṛtañca yattadapi paribhogāya na kalpate |
body.translated_text: 'Specifically for one <s>Śrīghana</s> [monk], etc.' If fish and the like — meat as a dish — is prepared for one <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, that is not suitable for the enjoyment of other <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> and ascetics (<s>yatis</s>) either. And what is prepared specifically for <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers) — that too is not suitable for consumption.

body.text: nādeyādi jalamityādi | nadyāmbhavaṃ nādeyaṃ | kiṃ tat? jalaṃ | ādiśabdena tāḍāgādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ | kīdṛśaṃ? sajantukaṃ saprāṇakaṃ | tat saprāṇakamiti jānannapi na pibet | ko na pibedityāha | vratī | jānanniti vacanāt | ajñāne na doṣaḥ | nātra jantuśabdena matsyādayaḥ parigṛhyante teṣāṃ vivecanakṣamatvāt | kintu jantavo 'tra matāḥ sūkṣmāḥ | jantavaḥ prāṇinaḥ | sūkṣmāḥ adṛśyāḥ | atrāsmin śikṣāpadematāḥ abhipretāḥ | yathā katama ityāha | trasikormiṅkarādayaḥ | urmikara ityevamādaya iti yāvat | atha kimarthamiyaṃ kārikā pṛthak vyavasthāpyate? yāvatā vṛkṣasekagurusnānaṃ kuryānnāśuddhavāriṇā ityasyāṃ kārikāyāṃ saprāṇakena vṛkṣasekādipratiṣedhādayamapi kāryo 'vagata eva | yatra hi sekaḥ pratiṣidhyate sutarāṃ tatra pānapratiṣedhaḥ | satyametadanusaṅgato na mukhyataḥ | na atra mukhākāreṇa māraṇābhiprāyo 'sti pātukāmatāyāḥ prādhānyāt | ataḥ pṛthageva sthāpitā iyaṃ kārikā | kiñcārthotpattivaśānna (

children.translated_text: because the <s>Vinaya</s> operates through the arising of circumstances.

body.translated_text: 'River water,' etc. '<s>Nādeya</s>' means 'belonging to a river.' What is that? Water. By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), water from ponds and the like is included. Of what kind? Containing living beings (<s>sajantuka</s>), containing life (<s>saprāṇaka</s>). That water which contains living beings — even knowing it, one should not drink it. Who should not drink? [The text] says: 'one who has vows' (<s>vratī</s>). By the statement 'knowingly,' there is no fault in [drinking] unknowingly. Here, the word 'living beings' (<s>jantu</s>) does not include fish and the like, since they can be distinguished [by the eye]. Rather, the 'living beings' meant here are minute ones. 'Living beings' means sentient creatures. 'Minute' means invisible. 'Meant here' means intended in this training precept. What kinds are they? [The text] says: 'moving creatures such as <s>ūrmikara</s> and the like' — meaning '<s>ūrmikara</s>' and others. Now, for what purpose is this verse (<s>kārikā</s>) set up separately? Since in the verse 'one should water trees and bathe the teacher, but not with impure water,' the prohibition of watering trees and the like with water containing living beings already implies this [prohibition of drinking]. For where even watering is prohibited, drinking is all the more so prohibited. That is true, [but the prohibition of watering] is incidental, not primary. Here the intention of killing through the mouth is not present, since the desire for drinking is predominant. Therefore this verse is established separately. Moreover, due to the arising of the subject matter, there is no fault [in not writing it],

body.text: vārītyādi | jalaṃ pāvayituṃ dharmakaraṅkaṃ khallakasahitaṃ sthāpayet | antaśo 'gatyā kośo 'pyadhiṣṭheya iti adhiṣṭhātavya ityarthaḥ | kasya kośo 'dhiṣṭhātavyaḥ ityāha | suvāsasaḥ | satpaṭasyetyarthaḥ | kimartha? vighātaparihārārtha | duṣkṛtaparihāraṃ cetyadhyāhāryaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Water,' etc. To purify the water, one should set up a <s>dharmakaraṅka</s> (water-strainer) together with a <s>khallaka</s> (filtering cloth). At the very least, in case of necessity, even the hem of a robe (<s>kośa</s>) should be used to consecrate [the water] — that is the meaning. Whose robe-hem should be used? [The text] says: 'of one with clean garments' (<s>suvāsas</s>) — meaning 'of fine cloth.' For what purpose? For the avoidance of harm. 'And to avoid a transgression' — this is to be supplied.

body.text: divyanetretyādi | divi bhavaṃ divyaṃ | kiṃ tat? netraṃ cakṣuḥ | divye netre yasya sa divyanetraḥ | andhaḥ cakṣurindriyarahitaḥ | divyanetrasyāndhasya śrāmaṇerasya neṣṭaṃ nābhihitaṃ | kiṃ tanneṣṭamityāha | jalapratyavekṣaṇaṃ | yuktaṃ tāvat andhasya jalapratyavekṣaṇapratiṣedhaḥ sāmarthyābhāvāt | atha divyanetrasya kasmāt pratiṣedhaḥ? sa hi pṛthivyāśritānapi prāṇakān sūkṣmāntarakārūpikān paśyati | ata āha śaṅkāparihārārthadivyacakṣuṣaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ | bhadantaḥ prajñāsiṃha āha- divyacakṣuṣaḥ kumataya ityucyante | tathāvidharūpatvāt | pṛthagjanānāṃ pratyavekṣaṇaṃ na syāt | ataḥ pratiṣedhakaraṇamiti | nanu cāndhasya jalapratyavekṣā sāmarthyābhāvādeva na bhaviṣyati, kimanena pratiṣedhena prayojanaṃ? prasannākṣasya darśanasaṃbhavāt pratiṣedhamiti vinayavido varṇayanti ||
body.translated_text: 'One with divine eyes,' etc. 'Divine' (<s>divya</s>) means 'existing in heaven.' What is that? The eye (<s>netra</s>), vision. One who has divine eyes is '<s>divyanetra</s>.' 'Blind' (<s>andha</s>) means devoid of the sense-faculty of sight. For a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> who has divine eyes or who is blind, [water-inspection] is not prescribed, not recommended. What is not prescribed? [The text] says: the inspection of water (<s>jalapratyavekṣaṇa</s>). It is reasonable that the prohibition of water-inspection applies to a blind person, due to the absence of capability. But why the prohibition for one with divine eyes? For he sees even the beings dwelling in the earth, the minute and formless ones. Therefore [the text] says: the prohibition regarding one with divine eyes is for the purpose of removing doubt. The venerable <s>Prajñāsiṃha</s> says: 'Those with divine eyes are called those of wrong understanding,' because of their being of such a form. Ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjanas</s>) should not have [such] inspection. Therefore the prohibition is made. Now, since a blind person will not be able to inspect water due to lack of capability, what purpose does this prohibition serve? The <s>Vinaya</s>-knowers explain that the prohibition is for one with clear eyes, since seeing is possible [for such a person].

body.text: kena tarhi jalaṃ pratyavekṣaṇīyamityāha | hastetyādi | hastasyāṅguṣṭhāgre āvartā sūkṣmarekhā tāṃ draṣṭuṃ śīlaṃ yasya sa [ta]thoktaḥ, tasya na nivāryate | anivāryamiti yāvat | anenaiva timirikāṇāṃ pratiṣe[dha]yanti ||
body.translated_text: By whom, then, should water be inspected? [The text] says: 'with the hand,' etc. One whose habit is to see the fine lines (<s>āvartā</s>) — the subtle marks — at the tip of the thumb of the hand, for him it is not prohibited — that is, it is permitted. By this very [statement], those with blurred vision (<s>timirikās</s>) are also prohibited.

body.text: tena hastapaścimakāvartadarśinā kiyantaṃ kālaṃ pratyavekṣaṇīyamiti āha | (

children.text: ) locanasyetyādi | locanasyākṣṇorvibhramo mā bhūditi kṛtvā ciraṃ bahukālaṃ na [pa]śyet na nirīkṣayet | neti pratiṣedhaḥ | taditi jalaṃ | cirapratiṣedhādeva pratyavekṣaṇī[yaṃ] ityāha | kalpamātraṃ na vai kuryādityādi | māyā paravañcanā | śāṭhayañcittakauṭilyaṃ yena tathābhūtaṃ nāviṣkaroti asphuṭaṃ pratipadya | māyā ca śāṭhayañca māyāśāṭhaye | ataḥ tābhyāṃ samanvitaḥ | saṃkalpamātrakaraṇāya nāsyaivaṃ pratyavekṣaṇīyaṃ | kālaniyamastarhi kartavyaḥ ityāha | yenāntareṇetyādi | yāvat kālāntareṇa ṣaṣṭyabdaḥ ṣaṣṭivarṣaḥ kuñjaro hastī paribhramyate | śakaṭaṃ vā vaṃśapūrṇaṃ yāvatā kālena kālāntareṇa bhramati, sa īdṛgvidhakāla ityarthaḥ | salilekṣaṇe jalapratyavekṣaṇe veditavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Of the eye,' etc. [The text says:] thinking 'let there not be strain (<s>vibhrama</s>) on the eye,' one should not look at the water (<s>tat</s>) for a long time (<s>ciraṃ</s>), one should not gaze at it. 'Na' is the prohibitive particle. 'Tat' means 'the water.' Since prolonged [gazing] is prohibited, [the text] states it should be inspected [only briefly]: 'one should not engage in mere deliberation,' etc. '<s>Māyā</s>' is deception of others. '<s>Śāṭhya</s>' is crookedness of mind, by which one does not reveal things as they truly are, apprehending them unclearly. <s>Māyā</s> and <s>śāṭhya</s> [together are] <s>māyāśāṭhya</s>. Therefore, one endowed with these two [should not inspect] merely for the sake of a formality. Then a time-limit must be established, [the text] says: 'In the interval by which,' etc. The duration is: the time-interval (<s>kālāntareṇa</s>) by which a sixty-year-old elephant is turned around, or by which a cart full of bamboo revolves — such a time-interval is to be understood as applying to the inspection of water (<s>salilekṣaṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: For how long should one who can see the fine marks on the back of the hand inspect [the water]? [The text] says:

body.text: ūrdhvetyādi | ūrdhvā ca adharā ca madhyamā ca ūrdhvādhomadhyamāḥ | tistraḥ kiṃ? bhūmayaḥ | kasya? salilasya | śuddhimāyāti yā yā bhūriti | āsāṃ tisṛṇāmapi bhūmīnāṃ madhye yā yā bhūḥ śuddhimāyāti niḥ prāṇakā bhavati, kāryaṃ kuryāttayā | tayā bhūmyeti saṃbandhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Upper,' etc. The upper, the lower, and the middle — these three. What [three]? Layers (<s>bhūmis</s>). Of what? Of the water. Whichever layer attains purity — that is, becomes free of living creatures — one should use that layer for one's purpose. The connection is: 'with that layer.'

body.text: yatra ityādi | yasyāṃ nadyāṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ vā, sthūlā mahāntaḥ prāṇakā karatalahatāḥ hastena hatāḥ santaḥ adhaḥ sthalaṃ yānti tatra jalaṃ grahītavyaṃ, na cet srāvayitavyamiti | cecchabdo yadyarthe | yadi karatalāhatāḥ santaḥ prāṇino 'dho [na] yānti tadā srāvayitavyaṃ tadudakaṃ | kayā? pañcāṅgulikayā | pañcabhiraṅgulībhiḥ ityarthaḥ | bhaveyuru[da]kamityādi | yasminnudake prāṇinaḥ kare lagnā uttiṣṭhanti na tatra pāṇipādāsyavastrādikaṃ kṣālayedyatiriti | āsyaṃ mukhaṃ | sugamatvānna vibhaktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Where,' etc. In whatever river or pool there are large (<s>sthūla</s>), big living creatures which, when struck with the palm of the hand, go down to the bottom — there the water may be taken. If not, it should be filtered. The word 'if' (<s>cet</s>) means 'in the case that.' If, when struck with the palm, the living creatures do not go down, then that water should be filtered. By what? 'By the five fingers' (<s>pañcāṅgulikayā</s>) — that is, with the five fingers. 'If there should be water,' etc. In water where living creatures, clinging to the hand, rise up — there one should not wash hands, feet, mouth, cloth, or the like — [so says] one who holds vows. '<s>Āsya</s>' means 'mouth.' It is not separated [further] because the meaning is easy to understand.

body.text: kule ityādi || kule yaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ bhojanāya nimantritaḥ, tena tatra gatvā praṣṭavyaṃ- kimatra jalaṃ srāvitaṃ na veti | neti cet, saṃjñiko (

children.text: ) vācyaḥ- srāvayeti | yadi pṛṣṭaḥ san dānapatiḥ bravīti na srāvitamiti, tadā saṃjñiko vācyaḥ | saṃjñāsyāstīti saṃjñikaḥ, sa viśiṣṭa eva gṛhyate | yaḥ srāvaṇāya kuśalaḥ sa vaktavyaḥ | kimiti | etatsaprāṇakaṃ jalaṃ srāvayeti | itaro na tu | yaḥ stha[vi]rataraḥ parisrāvayituṃ na jānāti, sa srāvayeti na vaktavyaḥ | yaḥ vakti, tasya duṣkṛtaṃ syāt |
children.translated_text: the one who knows [the procedure] (<s>saṃjñika</s>) should be told: 'Filter it!' If the donor (<s>dānapati</s>), when asked, says 'It has not been filtered,' then the one who knows [the procedure] should be told. '<s>Saṃjñika</s>' means 'one who has knowledge' — and he is to be understood as one who is skilled [in the matter]. One who is skilled in filtering should be told. [Told] what? 'Filter this water containing living beings.' But not the other [kind of person] — one who is more senior but does not know how to filter should not be told 'filter it.' If he does tell [such a person to do it], there would be a transgression (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) for that one.

body.translated_text: 'In a household,' etc. A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> who has been invited to a household for a meal, having gone there, should ask: 'Has the water here been filtered or not?' If not,

body.text: yadi tathaiko 'pi srāvaṇāya kuśalo na bhavati, tadā kiṃ kartavyaṃ ityāha | kintu snāvyamiti vistaraḥ | srāvyāt parisrāvaṇāt | sajantukajalamātmīyapātre muktvā kutaḥ punaretadudakamānītamiti pṛṣṭaṃ yataḥ puṣkariṇyāderānītaṃ tatraiva muñcetsvayamiti | mā bhūdanyatra kṣāraṃ nīramupaghātakṛtaṃ prāṇināmiti tatraivetyāha | saptāhaṃ vetyādi | athavā yatra sapta divasān pānīyamavatiṣṭhati tatra tat saprāṇakamudakaṃ moktavyaṃ | athavā vihāre kaṭāhādau tatra sthāpayet | kīdṛgvidha ityāha | tadaśuṣyati | tat pānīyaṃ tatra śoṣaṃ nopaiti | tasminnaśuṣyati kaṭāhādau sthāpayet | kecittadaśuṣyati tatra pānīyāśoṣaṇaṃ nimittamiti nimittasaptamīṃ varṇayanti | pravṛṣṭetyādi | athavā sutarāṃ deve vṛṣṭe | kīdṛśe? svacchanīraughavāhini | svacchamanāvilaṃ, nīraughaṃ jalaughaṃ voḍhuṃ śīlaṃ yasyeti bhāvaḥ | svacchanīraughavāhī | tasminnīdṛgvidhe vṛṣṭe sati tāni [sa]prāṇakāni jalāni nimnagānāṃ patiṃ mahāsamudrapātaṅgacchateti uktvā visarjayet | athaitat sarva na bhavati | dūragatodakamudakapānamasti | tadā tat saprāṇakaṃ jalaṃ kiṃ kartavyamityāha | sudīrghaityādi | dīrghātipramāṇatalikādhobhāgaḥ | vaktraṃ mukhaṃ dīrghaṃ yasyā rajjudvayena ca (

children.text: ) baddhā ghaṭikā sā evamucyate | tayā dūragatādhvagena udake kūpe adhastāttadudakaṃ muñcet ||
children.translated_text: With that [pot], a traveler who has come a long distance should release that water downward into a well.

body.translated_text: If, however, there is not a single person skilled in filtering, then what should be done? [The text] says: 'But [it should be strained],' and so forth in detail. [The word] '<s>srāvyāt</s>' means 'through a strainer' (<s>parisrāvaṇa</s>). Having put the water with living beings into one's own vessel, [one should ask] 'From where was this water brought?' Having been told it was brought from such-and-such a pond and the like, one should release it there by oneself. [The text says] 'there itself' so that alkaline water, which is harmful to living beings, may not be released elsewhere. 'Seven days,' etc. Alternatively, where water remains for seven days, there that water containing living beings should be released. Alternatively, in the monastery, in a cauldron or the like, there one should store it. Of what kind? [The text] says: 'where it does not dry up.' That water does not undergo evaporation there. In that [vessel] where it does not dry up — in a cauldron or the like — one should store it. Some explain 'where it does not dry up' as a locative of cause, meaning the reason is that the water does not dry up there. 'When it rains,' etc. Alternatively, especially when it rains heavily. Of what kind? 'Bearing a stream of clear water' — 'clear' means 'not turbid'; 'water-stream' means 'a flood of water'; the meaning is: whose nature is to bear [such]. When it rains in such a manner, those waters containing living beings [should be released, saying:] 'Go to the lord of rivers, the great ocean' — having thus spoken, one should release them. Now, if none of this is possible and there is only water from a distant source for drinking, then what should be done with the water containing living beings? [The text] says: 'Very long,' etc. The lower part of a very long, excessively large earthen pot — the mouth is long — bound with two cords is such a pot (<s>ghaṭikā</s>). It is thus called.
