body.text: adhvagena kathaṃ jale pratipattavyaṃ ityāha | ghaṭikātritayamiti | tisro ghaṭikāḥ pratyavekṣya mārgageṇa udapānataḥ kūpāt jalaṃ pātavyaṃ | kiṃ pariśuddhāsvapi? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi sarvāstāḥ pariśuddhāścet peyaṃ? cecchabdo yadyarthe | yadi tāstisro ghaṭikāḥ pariśuddhā bhavanti, pratyavekṣamāṇāstadānena mārgageṇa pātavyaṃ | tat srāvyamanyatheti | kathamanyathā? yadi tāstisro ghaṭikā na śudhyanti, tadā sajantukaṃ jalaṃ srāvayitavyamiti | ghaṭikātritayaṃ vīkṣyeti | ghaṭikā tritayasthamudakaṃ | stokastokena salilaṃ pratyavekṣyetyeke | sakṛdeka eva | ekaikasyāḥ stokastokaṃ pratyavekṣyetyapare | etadeva tu yujyate, yatopyūrdhvādhomadhyamāstisraḥ salilasyāpi bhūmayaḥ iti kārikāyāṃ stokaṃ pratyavekṣitavyamiti yuktaṃ na ca tatra sarvaṃ śikṣāpadañcedaṃ, nādeyādi jalaṃ jānanniti vacanāt | tasmāt ghaṭikāpi stokameva pratyavekṣitumanujñāyate | tadvadihāpi | atha tamaśakyatvāt tatra stokaṃ | iha tu śakyatvāt sarvamiti | evaṃ tarhyaśakyatvāt tatrāpratyavekṣaṇamevāstu | athāśakyaṃ stokena cittaviśuddhirvidhīyate, śakye 'pi kasmānnaivaṃ sarvaṃ śikṣāpadaṃ cedaṃ, nādeyādijalaṃ jānanniti vacanāt | tasmāt pṛṣṭe 'pi stokameva pratyavekṣaṇīyaṃ | ghaṭipañcaghaṭikāṃ vīkṣyeti kecit paṭhanti | teṣāmanyārthatvāt pāṭho nābhyupeyaḥ | amutra tu vidhiḥ |
body.translated_text: How should a traveler handle water? He says: "Three vessels" — having examined three vessels, a traveler should drink water from a well or cistern. [Should one drink] even if [all three are] pure? He says no. Then what? "If all of them are pure, one may drink." The word "if" (<s>cet</s>) is used in the sense of "if." If those three vessels are pure, then, upon examination, the traveler may drink. "Otherwise it should be strained" — how otherwise? If those three vessels are not pure, then water containing living beings should be strained. "Having examined three vessels" — the water standing in three vessels. Some say: "One should examine a small amount at a time of each." Once, [meaning] just one [examination]. Others say: "A small amount from each one should be examined." But this alone is correct, because the verse states "above, below, and middle are three levels of water" — it is proper that a small amount should be examined, and moreover this is the entire training precept: "knowing that river-water and other [types of] water" — from this statement. Therefore, even a vessel is permitted to be examined in only a small amount. So too here. [Objection:] "There [it is] a small amount because of impossibility [of examining all]; but here, because it is possible, [one should examine] all." If so, then because of impossibility there, let there be no examination at all! But if, when it is impossible, purity of mind is prescribed [even] with a small amount, then why not the same when it is possible? "This is the entire training precept: knowing that river-water and other [types of] water" — from this statement. Therefore, even when asked, only a small amount should be examined. Some read "five-vessel" for "vessel." Since their meaning differs, that reading is not accepted. But the procedure there is [as follows]:

children.translated_text: Apart from a traveler, six or five vessels
should be examined before consuming; otherwise one would commit a transgression.

body.text: na rajjughaṭiketyādi | rajjuśca ghaṭikā ca rajjughaṭike tayo rdānaṃ parityāgaḥ | tanna śastaṃ nābhimataṃ | kutretyāha | saprāṇake jale | saha prāṇakena vartata iti saprāṇakaṃ jalaṃ, tasmin | kiṃ tadeva na śastaṃ? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi? pibeti vaktumityādi | tatsaprāṇakamudakaṃ parasmai pibeti vaktuṃ dātuṃ vā na jātu kadācit yatiḥ kṣamate | yathā yatinānantaranirdiṣṭametat na kāryaṃ | kiṃ tena saprāṇakamidaṃ taḍāgādi ityapi na vaktavyamityāha | sajantukamityādi | iyaṃ puṣkariṇī sarittaḍāgādi saprāṇakamiti pareṣāmuccaiḥ śabdairna vadet | atha yadi kaścit pṛcchati, kimidaṃ, prativacanaṃ dadyāt, saprāṇakamiti, taḍāgādi | tadā kuru kāryaṃ na veti samīkṣyeti | pṛṣṭaḥ prativadet parān pratyavekṣya jala kṛtyaṃ kuru | ityevaṃ sati pṛṣṭaḥ san paraṃ yatirvadet | na tu saprāṇakamiti vadedityarthaḥ | lokāvadhyānaparihārārthami[ti] bhāvaḥ | yathā ca pareṣāmevaṃ na vaktavyaṃ | kimevamupādhyāyācāryāṇāmapi? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi upādhyāya ityādi | saprāṇakamidaṃ taḍāgādi na veti sphuṭaṃ vaktavyaṃ | svakīyāṇāmupādhyāyācāryāṇāṃ vaktavyaṃ na śāṭhyaṃ kartavyaṃ |
body.translated_text: "Not a rope-and-vessel" and so forth — a rope and a vessel together are a rope-vessel; their giving means their handing over. That is not recommended, not approved. Where? He says: in water containing living beings (<s>saprāṇaka</s>). Water that exists together with living creatures is water containing living beings — in that [water]. Is only that not recommended? He says no. Then what? "To say 'drink'" and so forth — to tell another "drink" regarding that water containing living creatures is also to be given [as a prohibition].

body.text: evaṃ tarhyātmanaḥ saprāṇakajalapānapratiṣedhāt pareṣāñca dānapratiṣedhāt vṛkṣādīnāmacetanānāṃ saprāṇakenodakena sekānnadānaṃ na nirudhyate | bāhyaparibhogyāścet tadāśaṅkāṃ nivṛtyarthamāha | vṛkṣasekamityādi | apariśuddhena jalena vṛkṣaseko na dātavyaḥ | (

children.text: ) upādhyāyācāryāṇāmapi snānaṃ na kāryamiti anena bāhyabhogo nivāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) "Bathing of preceptors and teachers also should not be done" — by this, external use is prohibited.

body.translated_text: If so, then from the prohibition on drinking water with living beings for oneself and from the prohibition on giving to others, the watering of trees and other inanimate things or the giving of food with water containing living beings is not prohibited. [Objection:] If external objects of use [are permitted], then to remove that doubt he says: "Watering of trees" and so forth — watering of trees with impure water should not be done.

body.text: kiṃ punarjalameva saprāṇakamokṛtaṃ dātraṃ vakraṃ na kuryāt, āhosvidanyadapi? anyadapītyāha | mastukāñjika iti vistaraḥ | mastuśabdena dadhimastūcyate | kāñjiko dhānyāmburityeko 'rthaḥ | sauvīraṃ bahubhirauṣadhidravyaiḥ kriyate ambuviśeṣaiḥ | maṇḍo 'nnavikāraḥ | daṇḍāhataṃ mathitaṃ | tadevamādikaṃ saprāṇakaṃ yatirna pibet, na parasmai dadyāt, bhuvi pṛthivyāṃ na tyajet |
body.translated_text: Is it only water that, when containing living beings, should not be made into a gift or a curved [vessel-full]? Or other things too? He says: other things too. "Whey, fermented gruel" and so forth — this is the elaboration. By the word "whey" (<s>mastu</s>), curd-whey is meant. "<s>Kāñjika</s>" means one kind of grain-water. "<s>Sauvīra</s>" is a special type of liquid made with many medicinal substances. "<s>Maṇḍa</s>" is a rice preparation. "<s>Daṇḍāhata</s>" means churned. Such things and the like, when containing [creatures]

body.text: samatkuṇa ityādi | saha matkuṇairvattate yacchayanaṃ tadātape na śoṣa yat | hime kardame śotavāriṇi uṣṇavāriṇi vā [na] kṣipet | anena sattvapīḍākaraṇamātramapi pratiṣedhayati ||
body.translated_text: "With bedbugs" and so forth — bedding that exists together with bedbugs should not be dried in the sun. One should not throw [it] in frost, mud, cold water, or hot water. By this, he prohibits even the mere causing of pain to living beings.

body.text: navakarmetyādi | caityārāmavihārādīnāṃ navakarma sajantukenodakena na yatiḥ kuryāt | sāmarthyāt srāvayitvā kāryamityuktaṃ bhavati | srāvayitvā tadudakaṃ dināntaṃ na sakalaṃ divasaṃ trikoṇakaṃ khallakaṃ dhāryaṃ dhārayitavyamityarthaḥ | kintu kālena kālaṃ parisrāvaṇaṃ moktavyaṃ prāṇakānāṃ pīḍāparihārārthaṃ duṣkṛtaparihārārthañceti ||
body.translated_text: "New construction" and so forth — an ascetic (<s>yati</s>) should not perform new construction of <s>caitya</s>s, parks, monasteries, and the like with water containing living creatures. By implication, it is stated that [such work] should be done after straining. Having strained, that water — the triangular straining cloth (<s>trikoṇaka</s>) or filtering vessel (<s>khallaka</s>) should not be kept for the entire day; rather, the strainer should be released from time to time, to avoid harm to the living creatures.

body.text: atha pareṇa srāvayatā kathaṃ pratipattavyamityāha | bhṛtakaṃ śikṣayedevamityādi | yatiḥ karmakaramevaṃ śikṣayet | kimiti | vadhāna tvaṃ trikoṇakamiti | bhṛtaka, khallakaṃ bandha, kūpādevamudakamutkṣipya evaṃ srāvaya, evaṃ vimocaya khallakamiti ||
body.translated_text: Now, how should one conduct oneself when another person is doing the straining? He says: "One should instruct the laborer" and so forth. The ascetic should instruct the worker thus: for what purpose? "Bind the straining cloth" — "Laborer, bind the filtering vessel; draw up water from the well in this manner; strain it thus; release the filtering vessel thus."

body.text: yadi srāvyamāṇamapi tadudakaṃ saprāṇakaṃ bhavati, tadā kiṃ kartavyamityāha | (

children.text: ) trikoṇasaptakenetyādi | yadyekapuṭakhallakena srāvyamāṇaṃ tadudakaṃ na śudhyati, tadā yāvatsaptapuṭake[na] khallakena srāvyaṃ tadambhaḥ pānīyaṃ | athaivamapi na śudhyati, tadā pratikūpikā kāryā | yadi sā na śudhyeta, tadā navakarma tyaktvā deśāntaraṃ gantavya | tasmāt pradeśādanyasmin pradeśe gantavyamiti yāvat |
children.translated_text: ) "With seven triangular [cloths]" and so forth — if, when strained through a single-layered filtering vessel, that water is not purified, then it should be strained through a seven-layered filtering vessel. If even then it is not purified, then a counter-well (<s>pratikūpīkā</s>) should be made. If that too does not purify [the water], then the construction work should be abandoned and one should go to another place — from that location, one should go to another location.

body.translated_text: If even after being strained, that water [still] contains living beings, then what should be done? He says:

body.text: kadā tarhi navakarma kārayitavyamityāha | abhūtvā saṃbhavantīti vistaraḥ | ete hi kuṇarūpiṇaḥ prāṇakāḥ abhūtvā saṃbhavanti, bhūtvā ca paścādvinaśyanti | yadā tāvadamī prāṇakā bhūtvā bhavāntaraṃ janmāntaraṃ yānti, tadā navakarma kārayitavyaṃ | kena? yathokta vidhikāriṇā | yathoktamācāravidhiṃ kartuṃ śīlamasyeti yathoktavidhikārī | teneti saṃbandhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When, then, should construction work be done? He says: "Not having existed, they come into being" — this is the elaboration. For these insect-formed creatures, not having existed, come into being; and having existed, they subsequently perish. When these creatures, having existed, pass on to another existence, another birth, then construction work should be done. By whom? By one who is authorized by the prescribed procedure — one who is qualified to perform the prescribed rules of conduct.

body.text: satpaṭetyādi | śobhanaḥ paṭaḥ satpaṭaḥ | tenābaddhaṃ yanmañcapīṭhasaṃsthānaṃ dhāraṇapātrakaṃ, tasmāt | kīdṛśāt? ucchīdañcaturāṅgulāt | ucchīdanti uchrayeṇa catvāryaṅgulāni yasya mañcādeḥ tasmāt nadyādau salilaṃ grahītavyaṃ | ālokya pratyavekṣya | navakarmaṇi navakarmanimittaṃ | etaduktaṃ bhavati- nadītaḍāgādiṣu mañcapīṭhasaṃsthānaṃ dhāraṇapātraṃ ghanena paṭenāveṣṭaya madhye tu upalādikaṃ datvā udake nimajya caturāṅgulamucchritaṃ kṛtvā tadantargatamudakaṃ pratyavekṣya jalakāryaṃ kāryamiti ||
body.translated_text: "Fine cloth" and so forth — a good cloth is a fine cloth (<s>satpaṭa</s>). That which is bound with it and has the form of a platform-seat, a filtering vessel — from that. Of what kind? "Four fingers in height" — a platform and the like that is four fingers high in elevation — from that, water should be drawn in a river and the like. "Having examined" means having inspected. "For new construction" means for the purpose of new construction. What is stated is:

body.text: chidrakarṇadvayetyādi | chidrite kāṣṭhamaye karṇadvaye āsaktaṃ baddhaṃ yatsūtraṃ, tacchidrakarṇadvayāsaktasūtraṃ | tena baddhaṃ dvidaṇḍake daṇḍakadvaye yaddhāraṇapātrakaṃ tattathoktaṃ | (

children.text: ) tadīdṛgvidhaṃ dhāraṇapātrakaṃ trikoṇakasya khallakasya bahirheṣṭhaṃ dadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: ) Such a filtering vessel should be placed outside and below the triangular straining cloth (<s>trikoṇaka</s>).

body.translated_text: "Two pierced ears" and so forth — a string attached to two pierced wooden ears, bound [thereby] — that is the string attached to the two pierced ears. A filtering vessel bound with that to a pair of sticks — that is described thus.

body.text: kṛpāparītacitteneti vistaraḥ | kṛpayā karuṇayā parītaḥ samantāt idaṃ gṛhīta cittaṃ yasya yateḥ sa tathoktaḥ | tena kṛpāvatā śrīghanena svādu mṛṣṭaṃ vāri pānīyaṃ sajantukaṃ saprāṇakaṃ kṣārembhasi kṣārīye jale na moktavyaṃ notsraṣṭavyaṃ | yastu niṣkṛpo muñcati tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati | anāpatmṛṣṭasaṃjñinaḥ | yastu kṣārīye jale mṛṣṭasaṃjñī mṛṣṭābhiprāyastasya anāpat | na āpadanāpat | duṣkṛtaṃ na bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "With a mind pervaded by compassion" — this is the elaboration. One whose mind is encompassed on all sides by compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), that ascetic is described thus. By that compassionate one, <s>Śrīghana</s>, sweet and pure water that contains living beings should not be released, should not be discharged, into alkaline water (<s>kṣārīya</s>). But one who, lacking compassion, releases [it] commits a transgression. [The phrase] "considering it to be without fault and pure"

body.text: tatra sakalena śarīreṇetyārabhya yāvadavakrītādirityetaiḥ kārikāntarairduṣkṛta pūrvakaḥ saṃvaratyāga uktaḥ | śeṣaistu duṣkṛtānyudāhṛtāni |
body.translated_text: From "with the entire body" up to "purchased" and the like — through these intervening verses, the abandonment of restraint preceded by transgression is stated. By the remaining [verses], individual transgressions are illustrated.

children.translated_text: In a human body, endowed with consciousness, here resides the intention to kill.
One who has the knowledge of killing an executioner — how can restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) not be abandoned?

body.text: iti prahelikā ||
body.translated_text: Thus the riddle (<s>prahelikā</s>).

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śroghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ prāṇivadhaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāma prathamaṃ samāptaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the first [section], the precept of abstaining from killing living beings (<s>prāṇivadhaviratiśikṣāpada</s>), is completed.

body.text: uktaṃ prāṇivadhaviratiśikṣāpadalakṣaṇaṃ | adattādānaviratiśikṣāpadamidānīṃ vaktavyaṃ | yato yasya kasyacidvastumātrasyāpahāraṇādaśrāmaṇeratvamiṣyate | ato uccāvacatāṃ nirdiśannāha | kālikamityādi | kālaśabdenātra prayuktaṃ | mabhyavahāraparibhoge na kṣamate vratīti, kālikamannapānādi | kālaścātra rātreḥ tṛtīyo bhāgaḥ | yāvajjīvamarhatīti yāvajjīvikaṃ pippalyādi | sakṛtparigṛhītaṃ saptāhaṃ kṣamate śrī[gha]nasya bhikṣoriti sāptāhikaṃ ghṛtādi | sāptāhikamiti vakṣyatā sarpirādikamityuktaṃ ślokabandhānuguṇyāt | parihāramarhati pārihāryaṃ yateścīvarādi, udvahanakṣamamityarthaḥ | anādhānīyasyetyādinā gurubhūta tvādgurudravyaṃ sāṃghikameva | anyadgurudravyaṃ na bhavati sāṃghikasyaiva gurudravyatvena vivakṣitatvāt | spraṣṭuṃ kṣamate parihartuñca, na tu punaḥ pinvitumiti | ataḥ kalpyākalpyaṃ muktāphalādi | spraṣṭumapya'kṣamatvādakalpikaṃ suvarṇādi | tadevaṃ kālikaṃ yāvadakalpikaṃ dravyaṃ nādadīta parasvakamiti vakṣyate ||
body.translated_text: The definition of the precept of abstaining from killing living beings has been stated. Now the precept of abstaining from taking what is not given (<s>adattādānaviratiśikṣāpada</s>) is to be explained. Since the taking of even the slightest object belonging to anyone entails the loss of novice-status (<s>aśrāmaṇeratva</s>), therefore, indicating the gradations [of property], he says '<s>kālika</s>' and so forth. By the word '<s>kāla</s>' (time) is meant here: 'the vow-observer is not permitted to use [it] for consumption beyond [the proper time]' — <s>kālika</s> (time-bound) [requisites] are food, drink, and the like. The 'time' here is the third portion of the night. 'That which is suitable for a lifetime' (<s>yāvajjīvika</s>) is long pepper and the like. 'Once accepted, it is suitable for seven days for the <s>bhikṣu</s> of <s>Śrīghana</s>' — <s>sāptāhika</s> (seven-day) [requisites] are ghee and the like. By the one who will say '<s>sāptāhika</s>,' 'butter and the like' is stated in accordance with the verse-structure. 'That which merits carrying' (<s>pārihārya</s>) — robes and the like of the renunciant, meaning that which can be borne. By [the phrase] 'of what cannot be deposited' and so forth — because it is weighty, weighty property (<s>gurudravya</s>) is exclusively communal (<s>sāṃghika</s>). There is no other weighty property, because only communal [property] is intended by the term 'weighty property.' 'It is permissible to touch and to handle, but not to hoard' — therefore <s>kalpyākalpya</s> (permissible-impermissible) [property] is pearls and the like. Because it is impermissible even to touch, <s>akalpika</s> (wholly impermissible) [property] is gold and the like. Thus, it will be stated: 'From <s>kālika</s> up to <s>akalpika</s> property, one should not take what belongs to another.'

body.text:
uktā aṣṭau pariṣkārāḥ | ṣoḍaśamidānīmucyante | pṛthivyudaketi vistaraḥ | pṛthivī codakaṃ cetyādi dvandvaḥ | tatra pṛthivīdravyaṃ su[va]rṇādyutpattisthānaṃ | dvipadadravyaṃ puruṣādi | catuṣpādadravyaṃ mahiṣyādi | apādakadravyamuragādi |
pādapadravyaṃ paṇaśavṛkṣādi | tadataṃ ceti pṛthivyādipādapaparyantāvasthitamityarthaḥ | tatra pṛthivyādipādapaparyantā aṣṭau pariṣkārāḥ | tadatāścāpare 'ṣṭāviti ṣoḍaśa bhavanti | (

children.text: ) ca samuccaya iti yathoktārthapratipādanārtha | nādadīteti na gṛhṇīyāt | parasvakamiti paradravyaṃ | ebhiraṣṭābhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiśca dravyaiḥ sarvadravyasaṃgrahaḥ kṛto bhavati | yadevaṃ ṣoḍaśabhireva dravyaiḥ sarvadravyasaṃgrahe siddhe kimarthamaṣṭau pariṣkārāḥ pṛthagucyante kālikādīni? satyametat | kintu tebhya eva ṣoḍaśebhyo dravyebhyo niṣkṛṣya kālikāditvamasāṃkaryeṇa pratipādanārthamaṣṭau pariṣkārāḥ pṛthaṅnirdiśyante | avaśyaṃ ca kālikādinirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ | saṃmukhībhūtaḥ varṣoṣitacāturdiśasaṃghānāṃ yathāyogaṃ bhajamānatvakhyāpanārthaḥ | ataśca pṛthagaṣṭau nirdiṣṭāḥ | evaṃ kuḍayādau ṣoḍaśa pariṣkārā vaktavyāḥ | yathodaṣṭau? satyametat | kintu aṣṭau ṣoḍaśeti saṃkhyānupaurvavidhānārthamaṣṭau pūrvamuktāḥ | ayaṃ saṃkṣepārthaḥ | pṛthivyādīnaṣṭau pariṣkārān nādadīta na gṛhṇīyāditi |
children.translated_text: ) And the conjunction [particle] serves to establish the meaning as stated. 'Should not take' means should not seize. 'Belonging to another' (<s>parasvaka</s>) means another's property. By these eight and sixteen categories of property, the inclusion of all property is accomplished. 'If all property is already included by the sixteen categories, then for what purpose are the eight requisites — <s>kālika</s> and the others — separately stated?' True. But from those very sixteen categories, the <s>kālika</s> nature and so forth is extracted and stated separately without confusion. And the specification of <s>kālika</s> and the rest must necessarily be made, for the purpose of indicating the [rules of] distribution to the <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four directions who have spent the rains, as applicable. Therefore the eight are stated separately. Thus in <s>Kuḍaya</s> and elsewhere, the sixteen requisites are to be explained. 'Just as the eight?' True. But 'eight, sixteen' — for the purpose of prescribing the sequence of enumeration, the eight are stated first. This is the summary meaning: 'One should not take, should not seize, the eight requisites beginning with earth and the rest.'

body.translated_text: The eight requisites have been stated. Now the sixteen are explained. 'Earth, water' and so forth in detail. 'Earth and water' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. There, 'earth-property' is the place of origin of gold and the like. 'Biped-property' is human beings and the like. 'Quadruped-property' is buffalo and the like. 'Footless-property' is serpents and the like. 'Plant-property' is <s>paṇaśa</s> trees and the like. 'And that beyond' means up to and including the range from earth to plants. Of those, from earth up to plants there are eight requisites. 'And beyond those, another eight' — thus there are sixteen.

body.text: uktāḥ ṣoḍaśāṣṭau pariṣkārāḥ | kiyatpramāṇa[ma]sya punaḥ dravyasyāpaharaṇātsaṃvaratyāgo bhavatītyāha | kārṣāpaṇacaturbhāgamiti vistaraḥ | kārṣāpaṇaśabdenātra ekonnaviṃśatiḥ kapardakapaṇāḥ parigṛhyante | tasya yaścaturtho bhāgaḥ kākinīnyūnāḥ pañca māṣakāḥ, tān haran | athavā tadarghaṃ tanmūlyaṃ dhanaṃ śāṭakādi[s]teyacittaḥ cauryābhiprāyaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ haran sthānāt cyāvayan svīkurvan anyairyatibhirlaghu (

children.translated_text: ) [and] quickly expelled — meaning, having seized [him], he is to be dismissed.

body.translated_text: The sixteen and eight requisites have been stated. Now, 'Of what quantity of property does taking result in loss of restraint?' He says: 'one-quarter of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>' and so forth in detail. By the word '<s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>' here, nineteen <s>kapardaka</s>-coins are meant. Its fourth part is five <s>māṣakas</s> less one <s>kākinī</s>. One who takes that [amount], or its equivalent in value — cloth and other goods — with a thieving mind, with the intention of stealing, a novice who takes [it], displacing [it] from its place, appropriating [it] — [is to be dealt with] by the other renunciants swiftly

body.text: uktaṃ dravyasya pramāṇaṃ | kutaḥ punaḥ sthānāttaddravyamapaharannaśrāmaṇero bhavatītyāha | yadi vāṭeti vistaraḥ | caturvāṭāntarāvasthite hastini hriyamāṇe yadi tatra vṛhaddvārā vāṭā bhavanti, tadā caturbhiḥ pādaiścyute gaje ayatiḥ bhavati | atha saṃvṛtā dvārā, tadā niṣkrānte sati dvipahṛtsyāt | dvābhyāṃ pibatīti dvipo hastī | taṃ haratīti dvipahṛt, hasticauro bhavedityarthaḥ | evamanayā kārikayā sthānadvayaṃ pratipādita vistīrṇadvāre pādau sthānamityekaṃ, saṃvṛtadvāre vāṭeti dvitīyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: The measure of property has been stated. Now, 'From what kind of location does one who takes that property lose novice-status?' He says: 'if an enclosure' and so forth in detail. When an elephant standing within four enclosures is being stolen — if the enclosures there have wide gates, then when the elephant has moved [even] with four feet [still inside], [the thief] loses his status. But if the gates are narrow, then only when [the elephant] has exited does he become an elephant-thief. '<s>Dvipa</s>' — 'one who drinks with two [trunks]' — is an elephant; one who steals it is a '<s>dvipahṛt</s>' — elephant-thief, is the meaning. Thus by this verse, two types of location are demonstrated: in a wide-gated [enclosure], the feet are the criterion of location; in a narrow-gated [enclosure], the enclosure [exit] is the second.

body.text: gulphetyādi | gulphaṃ pādasya parva | tatrābaddhaṃ yadikṣudaṇḍādi, tasmin | kīdṛgvidhe? dūrākṛṣṭe dūranīte | tadutkṣipte uddhṛte | kutaḥ? mahītalāt pṛthivītaḥ | kiṃ saṃvarabhaṅgaḥ, saṃvaratyāgo bhavatīti yāvat | pañjarād gajavadvije iti | yathā vṛhaddvāravāṭāyāṃ gajasya pādacyutimātreṇa saṃvaratyāga uktaḥ svalpadvārāyāñca niṣkrānte sati, evaṃ pañjare 'pi vṛhaddvāre pādacyutimātreṇa svalpadvāre niṣkrānte pakṣiṇi sati yatiḥ dvijahṛtsyāditi | asyāñca kārikāyāṃ sthānacatuṣṭayaṃ nirdiṣṭaṃ | gulphopanibandhanaṃ sthānaṃ, vṛhaddvāre pañjare pādau sthānaṃ, svalpadvāre pañjaraḥ, ubhayāpaharaṇe saṃyogasthānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Ankle' and so forth. '<s>Gulpha</s>' is the joint of the foot. What is bound there — a small stick and the like — in that [case]. Of what kind? 'Drawn far away' — taken far. 'Lifted up from it' — raised. From where? 'From the surface of the earth.' What [is the result]? 'There is breaking of restraint' — meaning, loss of restraint occurs. 'As with an elephant from a cage, so with a bird' — just as in a wide-gated enclosure, loss of restraint was stated for the mere movement of an elephant's feet, and in a narrow-gated one only when it has exited, so too in a cage: in a wide-gated [cage], by the mere movement of the bird's feet; in a narrow-gated cage, only when the bird has exited — 'one becomes a bird-thief.' In this verse, four types of location are specified: the ankle-binding as a location; in a wide-gated cage, the feet as a location; in a narrow-gated cage, the cage [exit]; and in the case of taking both [elephant and bird], the junction-location.

body.text: deśādityādi | kaścidyatirito deśādanyaddeśāntaraṃ gacchati, saṃdeśaṃ kasyacinnayati | tatra yadyekasmādaṅgādanyasminnaṅge śirasi vā tatsaṃdeśadraviṇaṃ (

children.text: ) dravyaṃ sañcārayet stainyacittena saṃvaradhūtaṃ samāpnute, ayatirbhavatītyarthaḥ | tadevamanayā kārikayā śarīrāṅgāni sthānamuktaṃ ||
children.translated_text: ) — if one transfers that property with a thieving mind, one's restraint is destroyed — meaning one loses one's status as a renunciant. Thus by this verse, the body-parts are stated as the [criterion of] location.

body.translated_text: 'From a region' and so forth. A certain renunciant goes from one region to another, carrying a message for someone. There, if from one part of the body to another part or to the head, that message-property

body.text: mṛto 'sau yasyetyādi | yasmin pudgalāyaṇādhitame dravyamamukena pudgalenāsau mṛta ityevaṃ manyatānyasmādadhvagāt brahmacāriṇaḥ sakāśācchratvā sīmānte sthātuṃ śīlaṃ yasya tasmai bhāgamadatvā gṛhṇan yatirayatirbhavet, aśrāmaṇero bhavatīti yāvat | atrāpi śarīrāṅgameva sthānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'He is dead, of whom' and so forth. In [the case of] a certain deceased person — when, having heard from a traveler or fellow celibate that 'such-and-such a person has died,' one who is accustomed to standing at the boundary [of the village], without giving [the deceased's] share, takes [it] — the renunciant becomes a non-renunciant, loses novice-status. Here too, the body-parts themselves are the [criterion of] location.

body.text: atha mṛtasya śrāmaṇerasya taddravyaṃ tatkasya prāpnotītyāha | yadvittamityādi || mṛtasya yaterathavārhataḥ parinirvṛtasya yaddravyaṃ tatsarvamupādhyāyasya prāpnotītyevaṃ jagaumuniḥ, bhagavānāhetyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Now, 'To whom does the property of a deceased novice belong?' He says: 'Whatever wealth' and so forth. Whatever property belongs to the deceased renunciant, or to an <s>Arhat</s> who has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, all that goes to the preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) — thus spoke the sage, meaning the Blessed One said.

body.text: harturityādi | ete hastino vistīrṇapradeśe caranti | tattu kaścidvratī hastinaṃ haret | tatra harturiṣṭāmabhipretāṃ diśaṃ yadi hastī yāyāt, tasmin harturneturabhipretāṃ diśaṃ yāte hastini | vratinaśca svakaṃ ruddhāṃ satyāṃ | kariṇaṃ hastinaṃ pātīti karipo hastya'varohakaḥ | tasmin karipe | kīdṛgvidhe? hṛtasaṃjñini | hṛto hastī mameti saṃjñā yasya tasmin hṛtasaṃjñini karipe sati asau hartā vratī cauraḥ syādaśrāmaṇero bhavatīti | anayā kārikayā pādacatuṣṭayaṃ (

children.text: ) sthānaṃ | anabhimatā dik, upacāraḥ, paripanthi cittaṃ ceti catvāri sthānāni nirdiṣṭāni ||
children.translated_text: ) of location [are specified]: an undesired direction, approach, the intention to waylay — these four locations are indicated.

body.translated_text: 'Of the taker' and so forth. These elephants roam in an extensive area. Suppose a vow-observer were to steal an elephant. If the elephant goes in the direction desired and intended by the taker, and when the elephant has gone in the direction intended by the taker and guide, and the vow-observer's own [path] is blocked — '<s>karipa</s>' — 'one who protects elephants' (<s>kariṇaṃ pāti</s>) — is the elephant-keeper; in that elephant-keeper — of what kind? 'One who has the awareness that [his elephant] has been taken' — when the elephant-keeper who has the awareness 'my elephant has been taken' [notices], then that taker, the vow-observer, becomes a thief, loses novice-status. By this verse, four [criteria]

body.text: pūjācīvaretyādi | pūjārtha cīvaramālā pūjācīvaramālā | tasyā antadvayaṃ, tasya mocanaṃ muktirapanayanaṃ | tayā antadvayaṃ muktvā cīvaramālāyāḥ | avanau pṛthivyāṃ yā cyutiḥ pātaḥ asyāḥ cyutau satyāṃ bhraśyate | kutaḥ? saṃvarāt | saṃvarīti śeṣaḥ | bodhivṛkṣādapi aṃśukaṃ vastraṃ gṛhṇan ayatirbhavati | anena ślokena sthānatrayaṃ pratipāditaṃ | ubhayānta[yo]rbandhaḥ, manasā paraparigraho, vastraṃ ceti | tatra kīlakabaddhāyāṃ cīvaramālāyāṃ ubhayāntasthānaṃ | yadā anyonyāparijñānādubhau corayataścīvaramālāyā antadvayaṃ muñcatastadā parasparaparigrahaḥ sthānaṃ | khaṇḍacchede tu tadeva vastraṃ sthānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Worship-robe' and so forth. A robe-garland for the purpose of worship is a 'worship-robe-garland.' Its two ends — their releasing, loosening, untying. Having released the two ends of the robe-garland — 'upon the ground' means on the earth — whatever 'falling' is its descent; when it falls, one loses — from what? From restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). 'Even one who takes cloth from the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree becomes a non-renunciant.' By this verse, three types of location are demonstrated: binding at both ends, mentally [considering it as] another's possession, and the cloth [itself]. There, when the robe-garland is fastened with pegs, the two ends are the criterion of location. When two [thieves], without knowing each other, both steal and release the two ends of the robe-garland, then mutual possession is the criterion. But in the case of cutting a piece, that very cloth is the criterion of location.

body.text: kṣiptetyādi || kṣiptāni prakīrṇāni mauktikahārādīni yasmin mahākule tadevamucyate | tatra gato yatiḥ sahāye jāte sati tasyaiva sahāyasya hastāyāṃ prasevikāyāṃ tataḥ kulāt prakīrṇamauktikahārādi gṛhītvā nyasati | tannyastaṃ tenaiva sahāyena hārayan kiṃ saṃvaracyutiriti vakṣyate | jaṭālenetyādi | athavā jaṭālena lomaśena śunā kurkureṇa tanmahākulāt taṃ mauktikahārādikaṃ hārayan upalāpya vatsaṃ tṛṇādinā gokāyapotakaṃ haran kiṃ saṃvaracyutiḥ? kiṃ punaḥ (

children.text: ) pādacyutimātreṇaiva saṃvaratyāgo bhavati? netyāha | upacārastaistyaktaścet saṃvaracyutiḥ | yadi taiḥ sahāyakurkuravatsairupacārastyakto bhavet, tadā yateḥ saṃvaratyāgo bhavati | upacāravyatikramaścātra darśanaśravaṇavyatikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Does loss of <s>saṃvara</s> occur merely by the [object's] displacement from [its] position? No, he says — 'If the approach through those [agents] is abandoned, [then] loss of <s>saṃvara</s>.' If the approach is abandoned by those — the accomplice, the dog, the calf — then the ascetic's abandonment of <s>saṃvara</s> occurs. And the violation of approach here means the transgression of seeing [the object taken] and hearing [about it being taken].

body.translated_text: 'Scattered, etc.' A great household in which pearl necklaces and the like are scattered about is described thus. An ascetic (<s>yati</s>) who goes there, when an accomplice (<s>sahāya</s>) has been secured, places the scattered pearl necklace etc. taken from that household in that very accomplice's hand, in [his] sleeve. Having that accomplice carry away what was thus placed — is it a loss of <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic vow)? This will be stated. 'By a shaggy [dog], etc.' Or alternatively, using a shaggy dog (<s>kurkura</s>), having it carry from that great household that pearl necklace etc., or enticing a calf with grass and the like, having it carry from a cow household — is it a loss of <s>saṃvara</s>?

body.text: rātrāvityādi | yatiḥ kaścinniśi gośakaṭāśvādīnbadhnāti | etān ete gāvo hariṣyantīti atra pūrvavadādiśet, yaduta cyutasaṃvaro bhavatīti | tadevamādibhistisṛbhiḥ kārikābhirupacāraścittaṃ ca śakaṭādiṣu tatsaṃjñitvaṃ mamatvalābhaśca sthānamuktaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'At night, etc.' A certain ascetic at night ties up cows, carts, horses, and the like. [Thinking:] 'These cows will carry them away' — here one should instruct as before, namely that he becomes one whose <s>saṃvara</s> has fallen. Thus, by these three verses beginning with the foregoing, the approach (<s>upacāra</s>), the mental intention, the cognition [of the object] as pertaining to carts and the like, and the acquisition of [the sense of] 'mine' in connection with the place have been stated.

body.text: ṛjuka ityādi | eṣa kaścidyatiḥ hāramapaharati | tatra yadi praguṇaḥ kīlako bhavati, kaṭhinañca bandhanaṃ bhavati, tadā utkṣipyamāṇameva [ba]ndhanaṃ kīlakasthānaṃ muñcatīti niranubandhasthānāccyāvitamityāha | utkṣepaṇe ca cauraḥ syāditi | atha kuṭilaḥ kīlako bhavatīti bandhanañca śithilaṃ bhavati, na tāvat aśrāmaṇero bhavati | vakratvena kīlakasya śithilatvena bandhasya kīlakasthānānatikramaṃ darśayati | tataśca niranubandhasthānāt cyāvitamiti nāśrāmaṇeraḥ | yadā tu sarveṇa sarvaṃ bandhanamuktaṃ bhavati, tadā ayatirbhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'Straight, etc.' This is a certain ascetic who steals a necklace (<s>hāra</s>). In that case, if the peg (<s>kīlaka</s>) is straight and the bond (<s>bandhana</s>) is hard, then the bond, when being lifted, releases from the peg-position — thus he says 'it is displaced from the place without further attachment.' 'And in the lifting, he becomes a thief.' Now, if the peg is crooked and the bond is loose, he does not immediately become a non-<s>śrāmaṇera</s>. He shows that, due to the crookedness of the peg and the looseness of the bond, the peg-position has not been transgressed. Therefore, [the object] not being displaced from the place without further attachment, he is not a non-<s>śrāmaṇera</s>. But when the bond is completely and entirely released, then he becomes a non-ascetic.

body.text: chidrayitvetyādi | ghaṭasya chidraṃ kṛtvā sarpirghṛtaṃ, kṣaudraṃ madhu, tailaṃ tilatailādi, jalaṃ nādeyādi haran yatiryadi pūrārpyataṅgataṃ bhavet, dhārā ca vicchinnā bhavettadā saṃvarakṣobhamāpnute, ayatirbhavatītyarthaḥ | avicchinnāyāṃ tu dhārāyāṃ yadi śrāmaṇyāpekṣayā nivartate, tadā na bhavatīti vinayavido varṇayanti |
body.translated_text: 'Making a hole, etc.' Having made a hole in a pot, if [the ascetic], stealing ghee (<s>sarpis</s>), honey (<s>kṣaudra</s>), oil (<s>taila</s> — sesame oil etc.), or water (<s>jala</s> — river water etc.), [causes] the [stream] to reach the designated place, and the stream is broken [i.e., detached from the original container] — then he incurs the disturbance of <s>saṃvara</s>.

body.text: vaṇṭayamāṇa ityādi | dvayorbhrātroḥ gṛhe vibhajyamāne, labdhumicchā lipsālābhābhilāṣaḥ, tayā lipsayā ekasya bhrāturbhāgāt yadi bālamātramapi bhūmi haret tadā kṣatasaṃvarī bhavati | tadatrāśayaḥ sthānamuktaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'Dividing, etc.' When a household is being divided between two brothers, the desire to obtain — the wish for acquisition — [arises]. Through that desire, if [an ascetic] takes even the smallest amount of land from one brother's share, then he becomes one whose <s>saṃvara</s> is damaged. The intention here, and the [matter of] the place,

body.text: atha kiṃ cauragṛhītaṃ pātrādi tyaktāśayasya śanaiḥ punargṛhītuṃ labhyate? netyāha taskaretyādi | taskareṇa caureṇa upāttaṃ gṛhītaṃ yatpātrādi taṃ nirāśaḥ san yatiḥ punarbhūyaḥ ādadat gṛhṇan saṃvarād bhraśyata iti | saṃvaraṇaṃ savaraḥ | akuśalaśrotasa āvaraṇaṃ | tato hīyate | itarastu anyaktāśaḥ punargṛhṇan nāpadaṃ prāpnoti, ayatirnabhavatītyarthaḥ | kiṃ punastattaskaropāttaṃ pātrādi gopālādidattaṃ gṛhītuṃ labhyate? temityāha | mitretyādi | yadi taccauragṛhītaṃ pātraṃ mitrabhāvena labdhaṃ bhavet mahatā vā kārpaṇyena gopālādibhirvā dattaṃ syāt, tadā ādadānasya yaternāpattiriṣyate, duṣkṛtamapi na bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, can a bowl etc. seized by a thief be slowly taken back by one who has abandoned [the sense of] ownership? No, he says, 'by a thief, etc.' That which has been taken — seized — by a thief (<s>taskara</s>), namely a bowl and the like — an ascetic who is without hope (<s>nirāśa</s>), if he again takes it, seizes it — he falls from <s>saṃvara</s>.

body.text: yadi caurāḥ pātracīvaraṃ gṛhītvā na dadate, tadā kathaṃ pratipattavyamityāha | bhayetyādi | pātrasya cīvarasya ca muktaye teṣāṃ caurāṇāṃ bhayopadarśanaṃ kārya | yatra tu rājani teṣāṃ malimlucāṃ bandhanādikaṃ bhavati, tatra gatvā na vaktavya mebhiścauraiḥ vayaṃ muṣitā iti ||
body.translated_text: If thieves, having taken the bowl and robe, do not return them, then how should one proceed? He says, 'by fear, etc.' For the release of the bowl and the robe, the showing of fear (<s>bhayopadarśana</s>) should be done to those thieves. Or where [there is recourse to] the king — the binding of those criminals,

body.text: niṣkāsayasītyādi | etau yatī kriyākāraṃ kurvāṇāvanyonyaṃ prayājayataḥ | upādhyāyācāryāṇāṃ yatpātracīvaraṃ tvaṃ niṣkāsayasi tadāvayostava ca mama ca | tadityevamuktvā yadyeko 'pi yatistatpātracīvaramapaharet, tadā dvāvapi tau vratinau taskarau bhavataḥ | svadravyetyādi | etau yatī svadravyaṃ stainyacittenāpaharataḥ | tatra ubhayabhāgādekasya yateḥ bhāgārdhena ekopya'yatirbhavati, dvitīyopītarapudgalaniṣkāsitārdheneti ||
body.translated_text: 'You are causing [items] to be expelled, etc.' These two ascetics, engaging in a business affair (<s>kriyākāra</s>), provoke each other. 'Whatever bowl and robe of the teachers (<s>upādhyāya-ācārya</s>) that you are causing to be expelled — that belongs to both of us, to you and to me.' Having spoken thus, if even one ascetic should take that bowl and robe,

body.text: atha yadā bahavaḥ śrāmaṇerāḥ saṃbhūya kākinīnyūnān pañca māṣakānapahareyustadā kiṃ te saṃvariṇo bhavantyuta neti? asaṃvariṇa eva bhavantyekābhiprāyatvāt (

children.text: ) sarve dvāri sthitacellakavat | dāsyāma ityādi | ete yataya ekābhiprāyā mahallakena saha kriyākāraṃ kurvata | mahallaka, samaṃ tava bhāgaṃ dāsyāmaḥ, kevalaṃ dvāre tiṣṭha vaya caurikāṃ kariṣyāma iti | evaṃ pratijānanāsya | uktaṃ karotītyuktakṛt | tasyoktakṛto mahallakasya tulyāpattiḥ | kaiḥ sahetyāha | cauracellakaṃḥ | sāpi cauro bhavedityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: All [are guilty], like the attendant (<s>cellaka</s>) standing at the door. 'We shall give [you your share], etc.' These ascetics, of one purpose, conspire with the elder (<s>mahallaka</s>): 'Elder, we shall give you an equal share; just stand at the door while we commit the theft.'

body.translated_text: Now, when many <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> together steal five <s>māṣakas</s> minus a <s>kākinī</s>, do they retain their <s>saṃvara</s> or not? They become non-<s>saṃvarins</s> (losers of vows), because of their shared intention (<s>ekābhiprāyatva</s>).

body.text: uṣitvetyādi | kaścidāgantuko yatiḥ uṣitvā, nivāsaṃ kalpayitvā pātracīvaraṃ vismṛtya gacchati | tasminnāgantuke gate āgatyāgatya yo yatiḥ tatpātracīvara gāpayetsa caurā bhavati | evamāvāsikāḥ sarvetyādi | amunānantaroktena prayogeṇa yadi sarve āvāsikāstadāgantukasya pātramapa[ha]reyustadā sava kṣatasaṃvarā bhavanti | yasya tu tatpātracīvaraṃ, sa yadi saṃsmṛtya nayati na kilviṣī | kilviṣamucyate pāpaṃ | tadasyāstī[ti] kilviṣo | na kilviṣī anāpattikaḥ syāditi yāvat |
body.translated_text: 'Having stayed, etc.' A certain visiting ascetic (<s>āgantuka</s>), having stayed, having settled in his lodging, forgets his bowl and robe and departs. After that visiting [monk] has left, whichever ascetic causes that bowl and robe to be taken away, coming and going — he is a thief. 'Likewise all the resident [monks], etc.'

body.text: anyasyetyādi | yaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ steyacittenānyasya yateḥ pātramanyena yatinā ānāyayati, sa doṣavān bhavati, ayatirbhavatītyarthaḥ | yastvānetā tasyaivaṃvidhā buddhiretatpātraṃ asyaivānāyayituryaterityevaṃ sati na doṣo, [a]yaṃ na doṣabhāg bhavati stainyacittābhāvāt | ye tu sahānīya yatirvratīti paṭhanti, teṣāṃ vinā sahaśabdena (

children.text: ) tṛtīyaryava sahārthasya dyātitatvāt sahaśabdagrahaṇamatiricyate | na vā sahārtha iyaṃ tṛtīyā kartari vighānāt | yattadośca saṃbandhitvāt tacchabdaprayogo hīyate | tasmādya anī[ya] yatirvratītyeva pāṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The third [case-ending, i.e., instrumental] — because of the meaning of 'together with' (<s>sahārtha</s>), the inclusion of the word '<s>saha</s>' is redundant. Or this instrumental is not in the sense of 'together with' but in the agent [sense], due to its being blocked [by a grammatical rule]. And because of the word's relation to that [referent], the use of the word '<s>tat</s>' is omitted. Therefore, the reading is simply 'the ascetic who brings, the <s>vratin</s> (vow-holder).'

body.translated_text: 'Of another, etc.' Whichever <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, with thieving intent (<s>steyacitta</s>), has another ascetic's bowl brought by yet another ascetic — he is culpable, meaning he becomes a non-ascetic. But as for the one who brings [it], if he has this kind of understanding — 'this bowl [I bring] for this very requesting ascetic' —

body.text: yāvata pūjetyādi | yāvat munerbuddhasya bhagavataḥ pūjā kriyate tāvat saṃghasyāpi pūjāsatkāraḥ pravartate ityevaṃ matvā yaḥ sāṃghikaṃ lābhaṃ stainyacittena stūpāya dadāti, staupikaṃ vā lābhaṃ saṃghāya dadāti sa kṣatasaṃvaro bhavatyayatirbhavatītyarthaḥ | nanu ca yāḥ kāścitsaṃpadaḥ sarvāstā bhagavantamāgamyati | yonisomanasikāreṇa stainyacittāsaṃbhavaḥ | naitadasti | etadeva hi vidāraṇaṃ stainyacittasyotthāpakaṃ yathā kāruṇyena salilamapaharata iti | kutastasyādattādānaṃ siddhyate?
body.translated_text: 'As far as worship, etc.' As far as worship of the sage (<s>muni</s>), the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, is performed, so far does worship and honor of the <s>Saṃgha</s> also continue — thinking thus, whoever gives <s>Saṃgha</s> property to a <s>stūpa</s> with thieving intent, or <s>stūpa</s> property to the <s>Saṃgha</s>,

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sāṃghikātkośāt stūpasyoddhārakaṃ gṛhītuṃ labhyate? nemityāha | likhitveti vistaraḥ | savārikairvā pakṣavārike māsavārāvārikairvā sāṃghikātkośāt likhitvoddhārakaṃ grahītavyaṃ | mithaḥ parasparaṃ | stūpāt saṃghasya grahītavyaṃ | saṃghācca stūpasyetyarthaḥ | taiśca vārikaiḥ karmādānaparisamāptau vaktavyaṃ- iyat hiraṇyaṃ suvarṇādi staupikāt kāśādagṛhītaṃ sāṃghikācca iyaditi | noktakṛto 'nyatheti | kathamanyathā? yadi vinā likhitvoddhārakaṃ gṛhṇanti, māsaniṣkāse ca na vadanti, tadā noktakṛto bhavanti | uktaṃ na kurvantīti noktakṛto, duṣkṛte prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, may one take a loan (<s>uddhāraka</s>) from the <s>Saṃgha</s> treasury for a <s>stūpa</s>? No, he says — 'having written, etc.' is the elaboration. By weekly, fortnightly, or monthly trustees, having written [an agreement], the loan should be taken from the <s>Saṃgha</s> treasury. Mutually, between each other,

body.text: svāṃśetyādi | tatrāṃśo bhāgo 'vayava ityanarthāntaraṃ | svakīryo 'śaḥ svāṃśaḥ | tena mukto yaḥ parakīryo 'śaḥ taṃ haratīti svāṃśamuktaharaḥ, ātmabhāgavyatiriktabhāgahara ityarthaḥ | etau yatī ekatra kule lābhaṃ labhete | tayordvayormadhye yaḥ parabhāgaharaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ sa cauro bhavati | viśvāsaṃ tu punardāsyāmīti ca kṛtvā gṛhṇan nāpadaṃ prāpnoti | labhase tvamityādi | etau yatī kriyākāra kurvāte | yaṃ tvaṃ lābhaṃ labhase ahañca yaṃ lābha labhe tadāvayostava ca mama ca vaditvaivaṃ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā samutpanne lābhe sati yastaṃ kriyākāraṃ bhinati tatordhena taskaro bhavati, dvitīyasya yaterbhāgeṇāśrāmaṇero bhavatītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One's own share,' etc. Therein, 'share' (<s>aṃśa</s>), 'portion' (<s>bhāga</s>), and 'part' (<s>avayava</s>) are synonyms. 'One's own share' (<s>svāṃśa</s>) is one's own portion. One who, having been freed from that [his own share], takes another's share — he is called '<s>svāṃśamuktahara</s>' (one who takes [another's share] after being freed from his own); the meaning is: one who takes a portion other than his own portion. These two ascetics (<s>yatīs</s>) obtain gain in a single household. Among those two, whichever <s>śrāmaṇera</s> takes the other's portion becomes a thief. However, one who takes [the other's share] with trust, saying 'I will give it back,' does not incur an offense. 'What you receive,' etc. These two ascetics make an agreement. 'What gain you receive and what gain I receive — that belongs to both of us, to you and to me' — having spoken thus and having made such an agreement, when gain arises and one breaks that agreement, he becomes thereby a thief; the meaning is: he ceases to be a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> with respect to the second ascetic's portion.

body.text: dakṣiṇādeśanepyevamityādi | yathā dvayoḥ kulopakayorekasya kriyākāraṃ bhindataḥ saṃvaracyutiruktā, eva dakṣiṇādeśane 'pi draṣṭavya | dakṣiṇādeśanañca dānagāthāpāṭhaḥ | dvayośca pāṃśukūlikayormadhye pāṃśukūle samutpanne sati yaḥ kriyākāraṃ bhinatti sa cyutasaṃvaro bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'In the dedication of merit too, likewise,' etc. Just as in the case of two household-supporters, when one breaks the agreement, the loss of restraint (<s>saṃvaracyuti</s>) has been stated, so too it should be seen in the dedication of merit (<s>dakṣiṇādeśana</s>). And the dedication of merit is the recitation of the gift-verse (<s>dānagāthā</s>). Among two rag-robe wearers (<s>pāṃśukūlikas</s>), when a rag-robe is obtained, whoever breaks the agreement — he becomes one whose restraint has lapsed.

body.text: prāṅnirdiṣṭaḥ sāṃghiko lābhaḥ stūpāya na dātavyaḥ staupikaśca saṃghāyeti | anyasmai sutarāṃ dātuṃ na labhyata ityabhiniveśatyājanārthaṃ vidhiṃ darśayannāha | upakārītyādi | upakartu śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te upakāriṇo, viparyayādanupakāriṇaḥ | tebhyaḥ sāṃghikamannapānādi dātavyaṃ | ke punaste ityāha | vihārasvāmi rājādayaḥ upakāriṇaḥ, caurādayo 'nupakāriṇa iti yathākramaṃ ubhau boddhavyo ||
body.translated_text: The previously indicated <s>Saṅgha</s> property (<s>sāṃghika lābha</s>) should not be given to a <s>stūpa</s>, and <s>stūpa</s> property should not [be given] to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. To show the rule for the purpose of abandoning the insistence that it cannot be given to anyone else at all, [the text] says: 'Benefactors,' etc. Those whose nature is to render service are 'benefactors' (<s>upakāriṇas</s>); by contrast, 'non-benefactors' (<s>anupakāriṇas</s>). To them, <s>Saṅgha</s> food, drink, and the like should be given. Who are they? [The text] says: the monastery owner, the king, and the like are benefactors; thieves and the like are non-benefactors. Both are to be understood in order.

body.text: śrīghanebhyopītyādi | yadi cellakāḥ sāṃghike vihāre ālepanaṃ saṃmārja[nā]dikaṃ kurvanti tadā tebhyaḥ saṃghataḥ pādāsyaṅsa pūrvāhṇikādi dātavyamanyathā neti | apiśabdena na kevalamupakāryapakāriṇo jñātavyāḥ śrīghanebhyo 'pyevaṃvidhakarmakāribhya iti (

children.text: ) darśayati | nanu ca śrāmaṇerasya pravraji[ta]tvādvināpi vihāralepanādikaraṇena sāṃghikānnapānaparibhogo labhyata eva | tatkimarthamucyate śrīghanebhyo 'pīti | idameva āśaṃvayamāne kṛte tricīvareṇa vibhūṣitasya hi bhikṣoḥ sāṃghikānnapānaparibhogo 'nujñāto bhagavatā sūtre, na śrāmaṇarasya ato vighā[nā]ntaramāha bhagavān- śrīghanebhyo 'pīti | na vā vinaye tarko 'vatārayitavyaḥ yatkiñcidetaditi ||
children.translated_text: [The text] demonstrates. Now, since the <s>śrāmaṇera</s> is ordained, even without performing monastery plastering and the like, the consumption of <s>Saṅgha</s> food and drink is obtained [by him] as a matter of course. Then why is it stated 'to the <s>śrīghanas</s> too'? When this very doubt arises, [the answer is:] the consumption of <s>Saṅgha</s> food and drink for a <s>bhikṣu</s> adorned with the three robes has been authorized by the Blessed One in the <s>Sūtra</s>, but not for a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>. Therefore the Blessed One states an additional provision: 'to the <s>śrīghanas</s> too.' Or, reasoning should not be applied in the <s>Vinaya</s> — whatever this may be.

body.translated_text: 'To the <s>śrīghanas</s> (lay servants) too,' etc. If lay servants (<s>cellakas</s>) perform plastering, sweeping, and the like in a <s>Saṅgha</s> monastery, then from the <s>Saṅgha</s>, foot-washing [water], mouthwash, morning [food], and the like should be given to them; otherwise not. By the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), it is to be known that not only benefactors and non-benefactors [are relevant], but also to <s>śrīghanas</s> who perform such work.

body.text: sīmāntasthāyina ityādi | sīmāntarāle syātuṃ śolaṃ yasya yatestasmai bhikṣusahitāya bhikṣūṇāyupasyātakāriṇe taṇḍulādikaṃ datvā dārakaprasyavyājena taṇḍulādikaṃ yatirgṛhṇīyāt | kecitugṛhṇāyāttaṇḍulādi netyante nakāraṃ paṭhanti | sīmāntasthāyine adatveti vātrākāraḥ praśliṣṭāstāti matvaivaṃ vyāvakṣate | sīmāntapātine yataye taṇḍulādikamadatvā dārakaprasthavyapadeśena taṇḍulādi na grāhyamiti tadatrobhayasmin pāṭhe na doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'One dwelling at the boundary,' etc. An ascetic who has the habit of dwelling in the boundary-interval (<s>sīmāntarāla</s>) — to that ascetic, who is accompanied by <s>bhikṣus</s> and who is a server of <s>bhikṣus</s>, having given rice and the like, [another] ascetic should accept rice and the like under the pretext of sending a boy. Some read the text with the negative particle: one should not accept rice and the like without giving to the ascetic dwelling at the boundary. [Another reading:] the boundary-dweller [reads the <s>sandhi</s>] as fused. One should understand it thus: without giving to the ascetic who dwells at the boundary, rice and the like should not be taken under the pretext of sending a boy. In both readings there is no fault.

body.text: atyaktāśa ityādi | atyaktā pātrādi pratyāśā yena sa tathoktaḥ | svapātracīvaraṃ naṣṭamiti | na kenacidapahṛtaṃ kintu kathañcit pramādācchoritaṃ | taddṛṣṭvāyatirutpādayedgṛhṇoyāt | matvaivamiti | kathamevaṃ matvā? atyaktāśasya matvā naṣṭaṃ pātracīvaraṃ gṛhītuṃ labhyate, netarasya | evaṃ gṛddho yatiḥ kīdṛśa ityāha naṣṭapātrādiḥ | naṣṭāni pātrādīni yasya sa evamucyate | āśāṃ naiva tyajediti | (

children.text: ) yatraiva naṣṭapātrādi lapsye, tatraiva grahīṣyāmītyevaṃ prajño bhavedityarthaḥ | yastu nirāśībhūtaḥ pātra cīvaraṃ naṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāti, tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati, na saṃvaratyāgo | na hi tena caurāt praticaurikā kṛtānapahṛtatvāddravyasya |
children.translated_text: 'Wherever I may find my lost bowl and the like, there I shall take it' — the meaning is: he should be wise in this way. But one who, having become hopeless, takes a lost bowl or robe — for him there is a transgression (<s>duṣkṛta</s>), but not a loss of restraint. For he has not committed counter-theft against a thief, since the property was not [originally] stolen.

body.translated_text: 'One whose hope is not abandoned,' etc. One whose expectation of [recovering] his bowl and the like is not abandoned — he is so called. 'His own bowl and robe are lost' — not taken by anyone, but somehow abandoned through negligence. Having seen that [lost property], an ascetic should generate the expectation and take it. 'Having thought thus' — how [should one think] thus? Having thought that one whose hope is not abandoned [may take it], it is permissible for him to take the lost bowl and robe, but not for another. Such an eager ascetic — of what kind is he? [The text] says: 'one whose bowl and the like are lost.' One whose bowl and the like are lost is so called. 'He should never abandon hope.'

body.text: lābhārthaṃ kriyākāraprasaṃgenoddeśādikriyākārātikrame 'pi duṣkṛtaṃ darśayitumāha | svādhyāyetyādi | ete śrāmaṇerā saṃghaśīlakaṃ kṛtvā kriyākāraṃ kurvanti | svādhyāyamadhyayanamuddeśaṃ vā kariṣyāma ityevaṃ kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā ye kriyākāraṃ na pratipālayanti, te jinoditalaṃghinaḥ | jinena buddhena bhagavatā ya uditaḥ ukto vinayastaṃ laṃghituṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te jinoditalaṃghino, duṣkṛtaṃ prāpnuvantītyarthaḥ | tadanena sarvatraivaṃ dhārmika kriyākārātikrame duṣkṛtaṃ bhavatītyākhyātaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: To show that there is a transgression even when one violates the agreement of recitation and the like, in connection with an agreement for obtaining gains, [the text] says: 'Study,' etc. These <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, having formed a communal practice (<s>saṃghaśīlaka</s>), make an agreement. 'We shall do study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), learning (<s>adhyayana</s>), or recitation (<s>uddeśa</s>)' — having thus made the agreement, those who do not uphold the agreement are 'transgressors of what was uttered by the <s>Jina</s>' (<s>jinoditalaṅghinas</s>). One who has the habit of transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s> that was uttered, spoken by the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One — they incur a transgression. By this, it is declared that everywhere, in any violation of a legitimate agreement, a transgression occurs.

body.text: patāketyādi | yatinā dhvajāpatākādilakṣaṇaḥ stūpato na grahītavyaḥ | nirgranthastūpagrahaṇaṃ copalakṣaṇārthaṃ | tena paṇḍarabhikṣustūpāderapi gṛhṇataḥ syādeva duṣkṛtaṃ, na tu saṃvaratyāgaḥ svāmino 'bhāvāt | yatra tu stūpe devalakaḥ āste tasmādgṛhṇataḥ syādeva saṃvaratyāgaḥ | anilena vātena tu uddhṛtaṃ kaṃpitaṃ pātitaṃ ca yatpatākādi tatpāṃśukalamiti kṛtvā gahītavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Flags,' etc. An ascetic should not take from a <s>stūpa</s> [items] characterized as banners, flags, and the like. The mention of a <s>Nirgrantha</s> <s>stūpa</s> is for the purpose of implying [all types]. Thus, even for a <s>Paṇḍarabhikṣu</s> (white-robed monk), taking from a <s>stūpa</s> and the like would indeed be a transgression, but not a loss of restraint, due to the absence of an owner. But where a <s>stūpa</s> has a temple-keeper (<s>devalaka</s>), taking from that [stūpa] would indeed involve a loss of restraint. However, what is lifted, shaken, and felled by wind — such flags and the like — should be taken as a rag-cloth (<s>pāṃśukūla</s>).

body.text: śulkakṛtyamityādi | śulkaśabdena rājakulapratyāyotpattisthānamucyate | yasya ghaṭṭa iti prākṛtajanapratītiḥ | tatra kṛtya prayojanaṃ | kintu tasmāt sthānāducitadānāpradānārtha yatparadravyanayanaṃ tadarthaṃ pareṣāṃ dravyaṃ yatiḥ svayaṃ na nayet, nāpi pareṇa nāyayet | śulkaṃ yatpradānaṃ tasya ca mokṣārthamupāyaṃ nopadiśet- amunā mārgeṇa gaccha, tataste śulkapradānaṃ na bhavati | ratnaṃ datvetyādi | kaścicchaṭhakajātīyo vaṇi[ja]kaḥ śulkapradānamuktaye śulkātprāgyatibhyo yathāvṛddhikayā ratnaṃ datvā paścāt (

children.text: ) śulkakarayayativāhyakṛtākaṇḍikayā tadratnaṃ mārgayatoti ca | yatayaḥ prāktasyābhiprāyaṃ na jānantīti bāddhavyaṃ, anyathā hi saṃvaratyāgaḥ syāt | tasmin aparijñāte tairyatibhiḥ- evaṃ nāma tvaṃ mohapuruṣa, asmākaṃ visaṃvādayasītyevaṃ suṣṭhuparibhāṣya tadratnaṃ tasyaiva vaṇijā dātavyaṃ | nāsti śulkamityādi | munerbuddhasya bhagavataḥ śulkaṃ nāsti | vratamasti yeṣāṃ te vratinaḥ | paribhogāyedaṃ pāribhogikaṃ | tasmin pāribhogike dravye muneriva vratināṃ śulka nāsti | anyatrāstītyuktaṃ bhavati | ata evāha | krayavikrayakṛddadyāditi | krayavikrayaṃ karotīti krayavikrayakṛdyatiḥ śulkaṃ prayacchet |
children.translated_text: by means of a basket purportedly [containing goods] made into a conveyance by the ascetics for the customs-levy, he searches for that jewel. It should be understood that the ascetics did not previously know his intention; otherwise there would be a loss of restraint. When that [intention] is not recognized by those ascetics, [they should say]: 'Such indeed are you, deluded man! You deceive us!' — having thus severely rebuked him, that jewel should be given back to that very merchant. 'There is no customs duty,' etc. For the Sage (<s>Muni</s>), the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, there is no customs duty. Those who have vows are 'vow-holders' (<s>vratinaḥ</s>). 'For consumption' — what is for personal use is '<s>pāribhogika</s>' (for use). On that property for personal use, just as for the Sage, so too for vow-holders there is no customs duty. It is stated that it exists for other [goods]. Therefore [the text] says: 'One who engages in buying and selling should pay' — an ascetic who engages in buying and selling should pay the customs duty.

body.translated_text: 'Customs duty,' etc. By the word '<s>śulka</s>' (customs/toll), the place of generating revenue for the royal court is denoted — what common people know as '<s>ghaṭṭa</s>' (customs-post) in the vernacular. There, the 'duty' is the purpose. However, for the purpose of avoiding the proper payment at that post, an ascetic should not himself transport others' goods, nor should he have them transported by another. And for the purpose of exemption from customs payment, he should not advise a stratagem — '[go by] such-and-such a road, and then you will not have to pay customs.' 'Having given a jewel,' etc. A certain deceitful merchant, for exemption from customs payment, before [reaching] the customs-post, gives a jewel to the ascetics according to their seniority, and then afterward

body.text: varṣāvāsiketyādi | yatra grāme nagare vā yaḥ śrāmaṇero varṣāmupagataḥ, tasya tatra varṣāvāsikalābho dātavyaḥ | jīvitasya brahmacaryasya ca yayoḥ śrāmaṇerayornāśaḥ tayorapi varṣāvāsikalābhā dātavyaḥ | tenaitaduktaṃ bhavati- jīvitāntarāyabhayabhītaṃ brahmacaryāntarāyabhayabhītaṃ muktvā anyeṣāmavarṣoṣitānāṃ varṣāvāsikalābho na dātavyaḥ | prākprāgupagatairityādi | ye śrāmaṇerāḥ prāk śrāvaṇamāsasya pratipadi varṣāmupagatāstaiḥ prāgevāśvinamāsasya pratipadamārabhya varṣāvāsikayācanā kartavyā | ye tu paścāt bhādrapadamāsasya pratipadi varṣāmupagatāstaiḥ paścādeva kārtikamāse | yadi sarvaḥ saṃvaḥ prayamāyāmupagacchati tadā saṃghavaśena paścādupagatairapi yugapadeva varṣāvāsikalābho yācanīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Rains-retreat [share],' etc. In whatever village or city a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> has entered the rains retreat, the rains-retreat gain (<s>varṣāvāsika lābha</s>) should be given to him there. Even for those two <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> whose life or whose holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) is in danger, the rains-retreat gains should be given. By this, the following is stated: except for one frightened by danger to life and one frightened by danger to the holy life, the rains-retreat gain should not be given to others who have not completed the rains [retreat]. 'By those who entered earlier,' etc. Those <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> who entered the rains before the first day of the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> should request the rains-retreat [share] from the first day of the month of <s>Āśvina</s> onward. But those who entered the rains later, on the first day of the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, [should request] later, in the month of <s>Kārtika</s>. If the entire <s>Saṅgha</s> enters on the first day, then by the will of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, even those who entered later should request the rains-retreat gain simultaneously.

body.text: punargṛhṇātītyādi | tatra vastu pūrṇaviśavaṣatvaṃ | vākpravyāhāro viśiṣṭārthadyotakaḥ | karma kriyā karmeti kṛtvā, kriyate vā aneneti | karmaśabdenopasaṃpatkarmaivābhidhīyate | tena hi karmaṇā sa pudgalo bhikṣuḥ kriyate | vastu karma ca vastukarmaṇo, (

children.text: ) tayorjugupsā nindā, tayā yaḥ pudgalo bhikṣubhāvaṃ parityajya punardīkṣāṃ pravrajyāṃ gṛhṇāti, tasmai api yataye varṣoṣitaiḥ saha samo lābho dātavyaḥ | anye tvanyathā vyācakṣante | triśaraṇayācanāmārabhya yāvata kāṣāyaparidhānamidaṃ vastu, buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pravrajitamanupravrajāmīti idaṃ karma viśiṣṭārthadyotakatvātkriyākarmeti kṛtvā | vastu ca karma ca vastukarmaṇī, tayorjugupsā nindā, tayā yaḥ pudgalaḥ śrāmaṇerabhāvaṃ parityajya punardīkṣāṃ pravrajyāṃ gṛhṇāti, tasmai api yataye varṣoṣitaiḥ saha samo lābho dātavyaḥ | ka evamāhetyato bravīti ityāha sarvavit, bhagavānāhetyarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) their reproach is censure. One who, through that [censure], having abandoned the state of being a <s>bhikṣu</s>, again takes ordination and goes forth — to that ascetic too, an equal share of gains should be given along with those who have spent the rains. But others explain it differently: from the requesting of the Three Refuges up to the donning of the ochre robe — this is the substance (<s>vastu</s>); "I go forth following the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, who has gone forth" — this is the act (<s>karma</s>), being called an action-object because it illuminates a special meaning. The substance and the act together are the substance-act; their reproach is censure. One who, through that [censure], having abandoned the state of being a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, again takes ordination and goes forth — to that ascetic too, an equal share of gains should be given along with those who have spent the rains. "Who says this?" — therefore he says: "the Omniscient One" — meaning the Blessed One has said.

body.translated_text: 'Takes again,' etc. Therein, 'thing' (<s>vastu</s>) means complete full ordination. 'Verbal utterance' means what indicates a specific meaning. 'Action' (<s>karma</s>) means activity — because it is done, or because by it [something is done]. By the word '<s>karma</s>,' the ordination ceremony (<s>upasaṃpat-karma</s>) itself is denoted. For by that action (<s>karma</s>), that individual is made a <s>bhikṣu</s>. 'Thing and action' — of thing and action,

body.text: avarṣoṣitetyādi | tatra traimāsānadhiṣṭhānādavarṣoṣitaḥ | vibhrānto yaḥ pravrajyāpapravrajitaḥ | kutsitā dṛṣṭiryasyeti kudṛṣṭiḥ, mithyādṛṣṭika ityarthaḥ | mithyādṛṣṭiśca nāstikapravṛttiḥ- nāsti mātā, nāsti pitā, nāsti sukṛtaduṣkṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipāka iti | jīvitendriyanirodhāt mṛtakaḥ | deśāntaragato 'nyadyatra deśagamanāt | ityete pañca pudgalāḥ lābhaṃ nārhanti ||
body.translated_text: "One who has not spent the rains" and so forth. Therein, one who has not resided for the three months is "one who has not spent the rains" (<s>avarṣoṣita</s>). One who is confused (<s>vibhrānta</s>) is one who has gone forth and then disrobed. One whose view is base is "of wrong view" (<s>kudṛṣṭi</s>), meaning a holder of wrong views (<s>mithyādṛṣṭika</s>). Wrong view is the nihilist disposition: "There is no mother, there is no father, there is no fruit or ripening of good and evil <s>karma</s>s." One who is dead (<s>mṛtaka</s>), from the cessation of the life-faculty. One who has gone to another region — from having gone to a different place. These five types of persons do not deserve a share of gains.

body.text: amuṣmai deyamityādi | amukasmai bhikṣave dātavyoyaṃ madīyo lābha ityevaṃ lābhe samutpanne sati yadi kaścidyatiḥ mriyate tadā niyatamavaśyaṃ tasmai vikalpitabhikṣave sa lābho deya iti bhagavatoktaṃ | deśāntaretyādi | ito deśāttraimāsamadhiṣṭhāyānyatra deśāntaragatasya yateḥ lābhaḥ kalpe mandire kalpakuṭayāṃ sthāpayitabyaḥ | yadā cāvarṣoṣitavibhrāntakudṛṣṭayastrayaḥ pudgalāḥ saṃghasyānartha kurvanti, tadā tebhyaḥ prāśyādi na sāṃghikamannapānādi dātavyaṃ budhaiḥ | nanuca lābhaṃ nārhanti pañcaketyuktaṃ (

children.text: ) tatkimarthamidamucyate- amuṣmai deyamityādi kārikādvayaṃ? satyametat | kintu yadā avikalpo mriyate, anutpanne ca lābhe gacchati, avarṣoṣitavibhrāntakudṛṣṭayaśca trayaḥ pudgalāḥ yadānarthaṃ vā kurvanti, tadaite pañca pudgalā lābhaṃ nārhanti, viparyayādarhantīti vyabhicārasaṃbhavādadoṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) Then why is this stated — the two verses beginning with "to so-and-so it should be given"? This is true. However, when one who is not designated dies, and when one departs before gains have arisen, and when the three persons — those who have not spent the rains, the confused, and those of wrong views — cause harm, then these five persons do not deserve gains; in the opposite case, they do deserve [them]. Since deviation is possible, there is no fault.

body.translated_text: "To so-and-so it should be given" and so forth. "To such-and-such a <s>bhikṣu</s>, this gain of mine should be given" — when a gain has arisen in this manner, if some ascetic dies, then the Blessed One has said that the gain must certainly be given to that designated <s>bhikṣu</s>. "In another region" and so forth: the gains of an ascetic who, having undertaken the three-month [rains retreat] from this region, has gone to another region, should be kept in the <s>kalpa</s>-hall, in the <s>kalpa</s>-hut of the monastery. When the three persons — one who has not spent the rains, the confused one, and one of wrong views — cause harm to the <s>Saṃgha</s>, then food, drink, and other communal <s>Saṃgha</s> provisions should not be given to them by the wise. [Objection:] But it was stated that "five [types] do not deserve gains"

body.text: ācchādamityādi | ete yatayaḥ kule varṣāmupagatā bhavanti | tatra yadi dānapati sāmānyenaivaṃ vadet- ācchādaṃ dāsyāmi, cīvaraṃ dāsyāmi, cīvaramūlyaṃ dāsyāmi, ācchādamūlyaṃ dāsyāmītyebhiścaturbhiḥ śabdairutpadyate yo lābhaḥ sa samukhībhūtānāṃ prāpnoti, netareṣāṃ | varṣāvāsiketyādi | varṣoṣitānāmācchādaṃ dāsyā[mi], cīvaraṃ, ācchādakrayaṃ, cīvarakrayaṃ caitaiścaturbhiśca śabdairyo lābhaḥ samupajāyate, sa varṣoṣitānāṃ prāpnoti | yadi dāyakastadvarṣāvāsikaṃ lābha avarṣoṣitānāmapi dadāti, tadā dāyakasyecchayā gṛhṇato na doṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "A covering" and so forth. These ascetics spend the rains in a household. There, if a donor generally says: "I shall give a covering," "I shall give a robe," "I shall give the price of a robe," "I shall give the price of a covering" — the gain that arises through these four words accrues to those present, not to the others. "Of the rains-dwellers" and so forth: "I shall give a covering to the rains-dwellers," "a robe," "the price of a covering," "the price of a robe"

body.text: yāmika ityādi | yasmin divase bhagavānutpannaḥ anuttarāñca samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ tatra yo maho yā pūjā, sa jātisaṃbodhyādimahaḥ | tata utpanno yo lābhaḥ saṃghasya sa evamucyate | mṛtapariṣkāraśca kṣudrapariṣkāraścetyādi dvandvaḥ | kālikaḥ yāmikaḥ yāvajjīvikaḥ sāptāhikaḥ mṛtapariṣkāraḥ kṣudrapariṣkāraḥ naityakaḥ akālacīvaraṃ kuṭīpratiṣṭhā jātisaṃbodhyādimahodbhavaśceti yo 'yaṃ daśaprakāro lābhaḥ sa saṃmukhībhūtānāṃ prāpnoti ||
body.translated_text: "Of the watch-period" and so forth. On the day when the Blessed One was born and attained unsurpassed perfect awakening — the festival and worship [held] on that [occasion] is the birth-and-awakening festival and so forth. The gain that arises from it belongs to the <s>Saṃgha</s> and is designated thus. "The goods of the deceased and minor goods" and so forth — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Temporal (<s>kālika</s>), of the watch-period (<s>yāmika</s>), lifelong (<s>yāvajjīvika</s>), weekly (<s>sāptāhika</s>), goods of the deceased, minor goods, regular (<s>naityaka</s>), unseasonable robes, hut-establishment, birth[-festival]

body.text: anādheyamityādi | sāṃghikaṃ yacchayanāsanaṃ tadanādheyaṃ, pratibandhatvena na dātavyamityarthaḥ | na vikretavyaṃ, na ca paudvalikaṃ kṛtvā paribhoktavyaṃ | ye tu śrāmaṇerāḥ (

children.text: ) sāṃghikaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratibandhakatvena dadati, vikrīṇīte, paudgalikatvena vā paribhuñjateraṃ teṣāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: ) give <s>Saṃgha</s> sleeping-quarters as security, sell [them], or use [them] as personal property — they commit a transgression.

body.translated_text: "Not to be pledged" and so forth. That which is <s>Saṃgha</s> property — sleeping-quarters — is not to be pledged, meaning it should not be given as security. It should not be sold, nor should it be used after making it personal property. Those <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s who

body.text: cāturdiśāyetyādi | kaściddānapatiḥ kiñciddravyānta, kadāciccāturdiśāyāryasaghāya dadāti, buddhāya vā bhagavate, saṃmukhībhūtāya vā saṃghāya tatsarvaṃ yatistatra tatropanāmayet | yaccāturdiśāya dattaṃ taccāturdiśāyaivopanāmayitavyamityeṣā dik ||
body.translated_text: "Of the four quarters" and so forth. A certain donor at some time gives some property to the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> of the four quarters, or to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, or to the <s>Saṃgha</s> present [before him]. The ascetic should direct all of that to [the appropriate recipient] in each case. What is given to the [<s>Saṃgha</s>] of the four quarters should be directed to the [<s>Saṃgha</s>] of the four quarters alone — this is the principle.

body.text: tūṣṇīṃ datvetyādi | kaściddānapatiḥ vihāramāgatya muktāphalādika datvā tūṣṇīṃ bhūto gacchet | tasmin tūṣṇīṃ datvā gate dānapatau sati buddhāya bhagavate muktā phalādi dātavyaṃ, yacchayanāsanaṃ taccāturdiśāya | saṃmukhībhūtāya tu saṃghāya vastrādikaṃ dātavyamiti ||
body.translated_text: "Having given silently" and so forth. A certain donor, having come to the monastery and given pearls, fruits, and the like, departs silently. When the donor has gone after giving silently, pearls, fruits, and the like should be offered to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One; sleeping-quarters [should be directed] to the [<s>Saṃgha</s>] of the four quarters; and cloth and the like should be given to the <s>Saṃgha</s> present [before one].

body.text: katibhiraṅgaiḥ samanvāgato 'dattādānaṃ gṛhṇan aśrāmaṇero bhavati? āha | pṛthudravyamityādi | pṛthuvistīrṇaṃ | kiṃ taddravyaṃ? kākinīnyūnaṃ māṣakapañcakaṃ | svakīyamapi kadācittadbhavatītyāha | paropāttamiti | kadāciddravyaṃ paropāttamapi sat yatiḥ paropāttasaṃjñā na bhavatītyata āha | tatsaṃjñī paropāttasaṃjñītyarthaḥ | kadācidetatsarvaṃ bhava[ti], na tu steyacetanetyataḥ steyacetaneti vacanaṃ | stainyacittaṃ copasthitaṃ bhavatātyarthaḥ | kadācidetadaṅgacatuṣṭayaṃ saṃbhavadapi sat taddravya sthānānna cyāvitaṃ syādityata āha | sthānacyutiśceti |
body.translated_text: Endowed with how many factors does one who takes what is not given become a non-<s>śrāmaṇera</s>? He says: "Substantial property" and so forth. "Substantial" means extensive. What is that property? Five <s>māṣaka</s>s, less than a <s>kākinī</s>. "Even one’s own [property] sometimes becomes that" — he says: "taken by another." Sometimes property, even though taken by another, the ascetic does not perceive it as "taken by another" — therefore he says: "having the perception of it [as taken by another]" — meaning having the perception of it being taken by another. Sometimes all this exists, but

body.text: pañcabhiraṅgaiḥ samanvāgato yatiradattamādadāno 'pi na cyutasaṃvaro bhavati | katamaiḥ pañcabhirityāha | dattasvaketyādi | dattasaṃjñā svakasaṃjñā aparopāttasaṃjñā ca vidyate yasya yateḥ sa yathokto yatiḥ | anyo 'pi ca svāṃśāttāvatkālikatvena ca gṛhṇan na saṃvaraṃ saṃvarī jahāti |
body.translated_text: An ascetic endowed with five factors, even when taking what is not given, does not lose his restraint. Which five? He says: "The perception of being given, one’s own" and so forth. An ascetic who has the perception that it was given, the perception that it is his own, and the perception that it is not taken by another — that ascetic is described thus. Moreover, one who takes from one’s own share and only temporarily does not abandon the restraint of a restrained one.

body.text: ādāyādattamityādi | ādāyeti gṛhītvā | adattaṃ pu[naḥ] dravyaṃ utpluyedvadhvā khamākāśaṃ gatvā | diśānāṃ catuṣṭayaṃ dikcatuṣṭayamityarthaḥ | āśāśabdasya dikparyāyatvāt | tatraiveti | yasmāt pratyāgataḥ punarbhūyastatropaviṣṭaḥ | san kṣatasaṃvaro bhavati, ayatirbhavatītyarthaḥ |
body.translated_text: "Having taken what is not given" and so forth. "Having taken" means having seized. "Not given" — then that property, having leapt up, going into the sky. "A group of four directions" means the four cardinal directions — since the word "<s>āśā</s>" is a synonym for "direction." "In that very [place]" means having returned to the place from which [he left], he sits down there again. Being [thus], he becomes one of damaged restraint, meaning he becomes a non-ascetic.

body.text: avakrītādiriti vistaraḥ | kaścidyatiḥ kenacitkrīto bhavati, bhṛtako vā sa ajñānāt smṛtisaṃpramoṣātkalpikasaṃjñayā vā paradravyaṃ gṛhṇan kṣatasaṃvaro bhavati | unmattavikṣiptacetasastu yatayaḥ parasvamādadānā api santonāpattibhājo bhavanti stainyacittābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: "Purchased" and the like — this is the elaboration. A certain ascetic is purchased by someone, or is a hired servant. He, out of ignorance, loss of mindfulness, or with the perception that it is permissible, taking another’s property, becomes one of damaged restraint. But ascetics who are insane or whose minds are disturbed (<s>vikṣiptacitta</s>), even when taking others’ property, being [of such mental state], do not incur an offense, due to the absence of a thieving intention.

body.text: tatra kālikamityārabhya yāvaddakṣiṇādeśanepyevamityebhirvākyaiḥ saṃvaratyāga uktaḥ | upakāryapakārimya ityārabhya yāvat tūṣṇīṃ datvetyādibhirvākyaiḥ duṣkṛtānyudāhṛtāni | śeṣaistu pāñcāṅganiyama iti |
body.translated_text: From "temporal" up to "and in the dedication of merit to the south" — through these statements, the abandonment of restraint is stated. From "benefactor and malefactor" up to "having given silently" and so forth — through these statements, transgressions are illustrated. By the remaining [statements], the five-factored rule [is presented].

children.translated_text: An ascetic who, with a thieving intention, carries away substantial goods placed in a vessel,
[traveling] eleven <s>yojana</s>s — may or may not [lose his status], [says] <s>Śrīghana</s>.

body.text:
sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ adattādānaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ
dvitīyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>: the second training precept, on refraining from taking what is not given, [is complete].

body.text: maithunaviratiśikṣāpadalakṣaṇaṃ labdhvāvakāśamadhikṛtyāha | nṛstrītyādi | nā ca strī ca paṇḍakaśceti nṛstrīpaṇḍakāsteṣāṃ yāni viṇmūtravaktrāṇi, teṣāṃ yat randhraṃ vivaraṃ chidraṃ, tasmin aṅgajātaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ tilamātramapi prakṣipya yaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ svādaṃ nigamayet sa kṣatasaṃvarā bhavati, ayatibhavatītyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having obtained the opportunity to address the characteristic of the training precept on refraining from sexual misconduct, he says: "A man, a woman" and so forth. A man, a woman, and a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (person of ambiguous sex) — these are the man-woman-<s>paṇḍaka</s>s. Their orifices of excrement, urine, and mouth — their opening, gap, or hole. A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> who, having inserted even a sesame-seed’s measure of the male organ into that [orifice], derives pleasure — he becomes one of damaged restraint, meaning he becomes a non-ascetic.

body.text: manuṣyagativyatirikteṣvapi strīpuruṣapaṇḍakeṣu maithunamadhyācarataḥ saṃvaratyāgo bhavatīti darśayannāha | mānuṣāmānuṣāste tviti vistaraḥ | atra kārikāpāṭhe vivādaḥ | tatraike mānuṣāmānuṣāste tu tiryañca[śca] narādaya iti pāṭha matvaivaṃ vyācakṣate | āha | narādaya ityādiśabdena strīpaṇḍakayorgrahaṇaṃ | tena narādaya iti | nṛstrīpaṇḍakā ityarthaḥ | manuṣyagatiparyāpannāḥ, amanuṣyagatiparyāpannāstiryaggatiparyāpannāśca nṛstrīpaṇḍakā jāgranto mṛtāḥ suptāśca maithunāśrayā avagantavyā iti | apare punarmānuṣā[mānuṣā]ste tu tiryañcaścāmarādaya iti pāṭhaṃ matvaivaṃ bruva[te] | mānuṣāmānuṣāste tviti | tacchabdenānantaraprayuktā nṛstrīpaṇḍakāḥ parigṛhyante tacchabdasyānantarābhidhāyitvāt | tu śabda evakārārthe | ta eva nṛstrīpaṇḍakā manuṣyagatiparigṛhītāḥ amanuṣyagatiparigṛhītāḥ tiryaggatiparigṛhītāśca pratyekaṃ jāgranto mṛtāḥ suptāśca maithunāśrayā jñeyāḥ | amarādaya ityamarā devāḥ ādiśabdenānyāmapi gati grāhayati | ato devāsuranarakapretagatisaṃgṛhīteṣvapi strīpuruṣapaṇḍakeṣu maithunamadhyācarataḥ saṃvaratyāgo bhavati | eta eva tu yujyate | anyathā hi narādaya ityanena nṛstrītareṣāṃ grahaṇe siddhe tviti tacchabdagrahaṇamatiricyate | (

children.text: ) atha mataṃ- tacchabdena ta eva mānuṣāmānuṣāḥ saṃbadhyanta ityasaṃbaddhametat | na hi pratyakṣāpātteṣu śabdeṣu tacchabdaḥ prayujyata sūribhiranavasthāprasaṅgāt | na cāpi tacchabdena viṇmūtravaktrarandhrasya saṃbandha iti pāryate vaktuṃ, randhraśabdasya napuṃsakaliṅgatvāt ekavacananirdeśāt, iha ca te tviti puṃliṅgena bahuvacanena nirdeśāt | atha mataṃ- viṇmatravaktrarandhraviśeṣā iti vyākhyāsyāma iti | yathā hi viṇmūtravaktrarandhraviśeṣāḥ strīpuruṣapaṇḍakāḥ manuṣyāmanuṣyatiryagga[ti]parigṛhītā maithunāśrayā jñeyā ityapūrvāyaṃ kriyākāra[ka]saṃbandhaḥ narādīnāmiti saṃbandhaṣaṣṭhayabhāvāt anyasyāśca gateḥ parigrahaṇāt | tasmādamarādaya ityeva pāṭhaḥ | evaṃ vicārite kecidatra bruvata narādaya ityapi pāṭhe ādiśabdena strīpaṇḍakayoranya[syā]śca gateḥ parigraho bhaviṣyati | ko 'tra virodha iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, if it is thought that by the word '<s>tat</s>' those very human and non-human [beings] are connected — this is incoherent. For the word '<s>tat</s>' is not used by the learned in reference to words that are directly apparent, because of the unwanted consequence of infinite regress. Nor can it be said that the word '<s>tat</s>' connects with 'the opening of the excretory, urinary, and oral [passages],' because the word '<s>randhra</s>' (opening) is of neuter gender and singular, whereas here '<s>te tu</s>' is in the masculine and plural. Now, if it is thought: 'We shall explain [them as] specific types of openings — excretory, urinary, and oral' — [this would mean] that those types of openings — the excretory, urinary, and oral — [pertaining to] women, men, and <s>paṇḍakas</s>, included in the human, non-human, and animal realms, should be known as objects of sexual intercourse. But this is an unprecedented relation of action and agent, there being no genitive relation with 'man and so forth,' and because another realm is included. Therefore, the reading '<s>amarādayaḥ</s>' (gods and so forth) alone [is correct]. When thus examined, some say: even with the reading '<s>narādayaḥ</s>' (man and so forth), by the word 'etc.,' the inclusion of women, <s>paṇḍakas</s>, and other realms will be accomplished. What is the contradiction here?

body.translated_text: Showing that loss of <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic vow) occurs even when one engages in sexual intercourse with women, men, and <s>paṇḍakas</s> (eunuchs/intersex persons) in realms other than the human realm, he says: 'Human and non-human, those, etc.' — this is the elaboration. Here there is a dispute regarding the verse reading. Some, taking the reading 'human and non-human, those, and animal, and man and so forth (<s>narādayaḥ</s>),' explain it thus: He says — by the word 'etc.' in '<s>narādayaḥ</s>' (man and so forth), women and <s>paṇḍakas</s> are included. Thus '<s>narādayaḥ</s>' means men, women, and <s>paṇḍakas</s>. Those belonging to the human realm, those belonging to the non-human realm, and those belonging to the animal realm — men, women, and <s>paṇḍakas</s>, whether awake, dead, or asleep, should be understood as objects of sexual intercourse. Others, however, taking the reading 'human and non-human, those, and animal, and gods (<s>amarādayaḥ</s>) and so forth,' say thus: 'Human and non-human, those' — by the word 'those' (<s>tad</s>), the men, women, and <s>paṇḍakas</s> just previously mentioned are included, since the word '<s>tat</s>' refers to what was immediately stated. The word '<s>tu</s>' is in the sense of '<s>eva</s>' (emphasis). Those very men, women, and <s>paṇḍakas</s>, included in the human realm, the non-human realm, and the animal realm, should each be known as objects of sexual intercourse — whether awake, dead, or asleep. '<s>Amarādayaḥ</s>' — '<s>amaras</s>' means gods; the word 'etc.' includes other realms as well. Therefore, loss of <s>saṃvara</s> occurs even when one engages in sexual intercourse with women, men, and <s>paṇḍakas</s> included in the realms of gods, <s>asuras</s>, hell-beings, and <s>pretas</s>. This [reading] alone is correct. For otherwise, if 'man and so forth' (<s>narādayaḥ</s>) already includes others besides men, the words 'tu' and 'tat' would be redundant.

body.text: atra na sarvā tiryagyonirabhipretā sūkṣmaudārikatvena maithunākṣamatvāt | kintu viśiṣṭaiveti darśayannāha | hastinīmāditaḥ kṛtveti vistaraḥ | hastinījāteḥ prabhṛti yāvat kukkuṭā jātiḥ | atrāntarāle yānyonyāpekṣayākṣudrikā maṃhato jātiḥ tāṃ tāṃ gacchan tasyāṃ tasyā jātau maithunamācaran vratāccyavate, aśrāmaṇerā bhavatītyarthaḥ | ata evādinirdeśāt hastinījāteyānyā mahattarā jātiḥ, kukkuṭājāteśca yānyā (

children.text: ) svalpatarā tasyāṃ vipratipadyamānasya na saṃvaratyāgaḥ, kintu duṣkṛtaṃ syāditi ||
children.translated_text: smaller than the hen species — for one who transgresses with those, there is no loss of <s>saṃvara</s>, but there would be a transgression (<s>duṣkṛta</s>).

body.translated_text: Not all animal species are intended here, since the very small and the very large are incapable of sexual intercourse.
