Rather, only specific ones, as he shows by saying 'beginning with she-elephants, etc.' — this is the elaboration. From the she-elephant species up to the hen species — in the interval between these, whichever species are, relative to each other, not too small and of considerable size, going to each such species, engaging in sexual intercourse with each such species — one falls from the vow, meaning one becomes a non-<s>śrāmaṇera</s>. Therefore, by the specification 'beginning with,' [for] any species larger than the she-elephant species, or any species

body.text: yatirna kevalaṃ maithunamadhyācaritaṃ na kṣamate strīdarśanādyapi na kṣamata iti pratipāda[ya]nnāha | raktaḥ sanniti vistaraḥ | yatiḥ saṃraktaḥ san striyaṃ na paśyet, na ca tasyāḥ śabdamākarṇayet | nirvastraśca san nirvastrāṃ striyaṃ nopeyāt, na gacchet, na ca puruṣendriyaṃ nirbhujet | etasyātra vidhikaraṇātsarvatra duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Demonstrating that an ascetic should not only refrain from engaging in sexual intercourse but should also refrain from even seeing women and the like, he says: 'being impassioned, etc.' — this is the elaboration. An ascetic who is impassioned (<s>saṃrakta</s>) should not look at a woman, nor should he listen to her voice. And being unclothed, he should not approach or go to an unclothed woman, nor should he manipulate the male organ. Because this is prescribed as a rule, a transgression (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) occurs in every [such] case.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ pāṭitāyāmapi maithunamadhyācarataḥ saṃvaratyāgo bhavati? bhavatītyāha bhittidvayetyādi | strīndriyādhiṣṭhānasaṃjñitāṃ koṭarikāṃ vātātapādinā śuṣkāṃ śastreṇavā pṛthak pṛthak kṛtāṃ tattailādibhiḥ klinnāṃ saṃyojyaikīkṛtya yaḥ śrāmaṇero vipratipadyate sa nāśayitavyaḥ | saṃgrahe sati | yadi sā koṭarikā sagrahamupayāti, tadā doṣo 'nyadā neti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, does loss of <s>saṃvara</s> occur even when one engages in sexual intercourse with a severed [organ]? Yes, he says — 'the two walls, etc.' The cavity designated as the seat of the female organ — dried by wind, sun, and the like, or separated into parts by a blade — if that [cavity] is moistened with oil and the like and joined together, made into one, and a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> transgresses with it — he is to be expelled. When there is grasping (<s>saṃgraha</s>): if that cavity receives [the male organ] with a grip, then there is a fault; otherwise, not.

body.text: adha ūrdhvamityādi | kācitstrī trikhaṇḍīkṛtā bhavati | tasyā adhaḥ khaṇḍe upari khaṇḍe ca vinīlādhmātikāñcavratī na vrajet | yā cāsthisaṅkalā pūyarudhirādibhiramyaktā tāmapi na yāyāt | sitāsthisaṅkaleti vistaraḥ | sitā śuklā yā asthisaṅkalā, śailamayī yā śilāyāṃ nidhātā dārumayī yā kāṣṭhamayī, pustamayī yā lepakṛtā | tāṃ sitāsthisaṅkalāṃ yāvatpustamayīṃ striyaṃ na gacchet | mithunaṃ strīpuruṣayoryugmaṃ, tatra utpadyate yaḥ sukhaviśeṣaḥ tanmaithunaṃ | tasmātsadā sarvakālaṃ yo virata iti yativiśeṣaṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'Lower, upper, etc.' A certain woman's [body] has been cut into three sections. In the lower section and in the upper section, even if it is discolored and bloated, the vow-holder should not go [to it]. And the bone-chain (<s>asthisaṅkalā</s>) smeared with pus, blood, and the like — that too one should not go to. 'White bone-chain, etc.' — this is the elaboration. 'White' means bright — a white bone-chain; one made of stone, placed upon rock; one made of wood, made of timber; one made of plaster, made of coating. Such — from a white bone-chain up to one made of plaster — one should not go to [such a representation of] a woman. Sexual union (<s>mithuna</s>) is the coupling of a man and woman; the particular pleasure that arises therein is '<s>maithuna</s>' (sexual intercourse). 'One who is always, at all times, abstinent from that' — this is a qualification of the ascetic.

body.text: dhyānetyādi | gataḥ prāptaḥ | dhyānamiddhagatastaṃ dhyānasamāpannaṃ nidrayābhibhūtaṃ ca vibuddhamapi śayitaṃ surāpānādinā mattaṃ mahābhūtavaiṣamyādinā vā vikṣiptacittaṃ rukṣayā vā vedanayā tunnaṃ vyathitaṃ yati yā kācitstrī balādgṛhītvā yateraṅgajātaṃ ātmīye 'ṅgajāte prakṣipet | tasmin balato 'bhiniṣīdati mātṛgrāme kimityāha | ādimadhyetyādi | ādāvaṃgajātapraveśakāle, madhye paryavasāne ca ya āsvāda nigamayet | yatiḥ kīdṛkṣaḥ? tato dhyānāvyutyitaḥ | sa vihārād ghaṭṭayitavyaḥ | āsvādanābhāve tu neti | etaccādhimātramadhyamṛdurāgiṇaṃ pudgalamadhikṛtyoktamityavaseyaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'In <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), etc.' 'Gone' means 'attained.' One who has attained <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>middha</s> (torpor) — one absorbed in meditation, one overpowered by sleep, or even one who is awakened but lying down, one intoxicated by liquor-drinking and the like, or one whose mind is deranged by the imbalance of the great elements and the like, or one who is afflicted, tormented by harsh pain — if any woman forcibly seizes such an ascetic's generative organ and inserts it into her own generative organ — when that woman forcibly sits upon [him], what [is the result]? He says: 'At the beginning, middle, etc.' At the beginning — at the time of the insertion of the generative organ; in the middle; and at the conclusion — whoever savors [the pleasure]. An ascetic of what kind? One who has emerged from <s>dhyāna</s>. He is to be expelled from the monastery. But in the absence of savoring — no [offense]. And this should be understood as stated with reference to a person of intense, moderate, or mild passion.

body.text: yaduktamādimadhyāvasāneṣa svādayediti tatra keyamāsvādanā nāmetyāha | nānetyādi | nānā prakārāṇāṃ vyañjanānāṃ rasānāṃ nānāvidhena yadupetaṃ samanvitaṃ śāliḥbhaktaṃ tasya paribhogaḥ tadvadāsvādanā draṣṭavyā | yathā śauṇḍasya mattavālakasya tailava[t] svacchasyānnāsavasya surāyāḥ pānāsvādastadvat maithunāsvādo 'vaseyaḥ | anye anyathā vyācakṣate śuṇḍiṣu bhavaḥ śauṇḍaḥ | kaḥ punarasau? annāsavaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ? tailācchaḥ | tailava[t] svaccho yaḥ śoṇḍo 'nnāsavaḥ, tasya pānamabhyavaharaṇaṃ | tadvat kiṃ? āsvādanā jñeyeti | anāsvādaḥ punaḥ kīdṛśa ityāha | anāsvādā yuvagrīvetyādi | yathā yūnastaruṇasya grīvāyāṃ mṛtakukkurabandhaḥ | yathā ca sukumārasya puṃsaḥ (

children.text: ) pradīptalohasparśastadvadanāsvādo vijñeyaḥ | dhyāyantyaneneti dhyānaṃ, prajñānaṃtītyarthaḥ | taccāṅgabhedāccaturvidhaṃ bhavati | prathamadvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānabhedena | siddhaṃ kāyasaṃdhāraṇāsamarthaścittābhisaṃkṣepo, nidreti yo 'rthaḥ | te dhyānamiddhe iti |
children.translated_text: the touch of blazing metal — such should non-savoring be known. '<s>Dhyāna</s>' — 'that by which one meditates' — means 'discernment' (<s>prajñāna</s>). That, due to the division of its constituents, is of four kinds — by the division into first, second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. 'Established' — the contraction of the mind that is incapable of maintaining the body, that is sleep (<s>nidrā</s>) — this is the meaning. These [two] are '<s>dhyāna-middha</s>' (meditation and torpor).

body.translated_text: As to what was said — 'whoever savors at the beginning, middle, and conclusion' — what, then, is this 'savoring'? He says: 'various, etc.' The enjoyment (<s>paribhoga</s>) of rice-food that is accompanied by various condiments and flavors in various ways — like that should savoring (<s>āsvādanā</s>) be understood. Just as the pleasure of drinking for a drunkard — a liquor-intoxicated person — [who drinks] liquor (<s>annāsava</s>) that is clear like oil — such is sexual savoring to be understood. Others explain differently: one who frequents taverns (<s>śauṇḍa</s>) is a '<s>śauṇḍa</s>.' Who is that? One [who drinks] grain-liquor (<s>annāsava</s>). Of what kind? Clear like oil — one who is a tavern-goer, [drinking] grain-liquor that is clear like oil — its drinking, its consumption. Like that — what? Savoring (<s>āsvādanā</s>) should be known. Now, what is non-savoring like? He says: 'non-savoring [is like that] of a young person's neck, etc.' Just as on the neck of a young man, the binding of a dead dog. And just as for a delicate person,

body.text: avakrītetyādi | asyārthaḥ pūrvaśikṣāpadānusāreṇāvaseyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Hired, etc.' The meaning of this should be understood following the earlier training rules.

body.text: rāgāmanuṣyetyādi | rañjanaṃ rāgaḥ, rañjayate vāneneti cittamiti rāgaḥ | tena rāgādinā praguṇībhūtaṃ yadaṃgajātaṃ tacchukranirmokṣārthaṃ na kadācidapi spṛśet | kairna spṛśedityāha | pṛthivyādidhātubhiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Passion, non-human, etc.' Passion (<s>rāga</s>) is that which colors [the mind], or 'that which colors is the mind' — thus it is passion. The generative organ that has become erect (<s>praguṇībhūta</s>) through passion and the like — that should never be touched for the purpose of releasing semen (<s>śukranirmokṣa</s>). By what [means] should one not touch it? He says: by the elements (<s>dhātus</s>) beginning with earth.

body.text: tiryaksaṃyogetyādi | tiryakmaithunādhyācāradarśanāt prāmādikaḥ strīpuruṣa darśanācca, tīvrarāgāditayā yadi śukrasya muktirbhavet tadā yatirmānasaṃ vigarhedvirūpakaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ na punarevaṃ kariṣyāmīti |
body.translated_text: 'Animal coupling, etc.' From seeing the sexual intercourse of animals, [one becomes] inadvertent; and from seeing a man and woman — if, due to intense passion and the like, there should be a release of semen, then the ascetic should mentally reproach himself [thinking:] 'I have done something disgraceful; I shall never do this again.'

body.text: majjetyādi | majjājātaṃ majjajaṃ śukraṃ, tasya kṣaraṇamapagamaḥ | yasya yateḥ svapne śukravinirmuktirbhavati, tasya doṣo na bhavati | kathaṃ punarbhavatītyāha | kāraṇamāha | svapnetyādi | pañcasvapnā vinaye uktāḥ | satyasvapno yathā bodhisattvena dṛṣṭaḥ, alīkasvapno yathā dṛṣṭaḥ tathā na bhavatya'līkaṃ mṛṣeti kṛtvā, acīrṇasvapno yatsatatakaraṇīyaṃ vastu dṛśyate, anantasvapno yaḥ sakalāṃrātriṃ dṛśyatena paricchidyate, svapnasvapno yaḥ svapna evānyaḥ svapno dṛśyate | tadukta bhavati- yasya yateḥ svapne śukranirmokṣo bhavati, tasya manāgapi doṣo na bhavatyalīkatvātsvapnasya | anyathā hya'nāśvāsikaṃ brahmacaryaṃ syāt svapne 'pi maithunādhyācāreṇāpattiprasaṅgāt ||
body.translated_text: 'Marrow' (<s>majja</s>) and so forth. Born from marrow (<s>majjāja</s>) is semen (<s>śukra</s>); its 'flowing out' (<s>kṣaraṇa</s>) means its discharge. For a renunciant who experiences an emission of semen during sleep, there is no fault. 'But how is this so?' He gives the reason: 'In sleep' and so forth. Five types of dreams are mentioned in the <s>Vinaya</s>: a true dream (<s>satyasvapna</s>), such as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw; a false dream (<s>alīkasvapna</s>), where what is seen does not [actually] occur, since 'false' means untrue; a dream of habitual action (<s>acīrṇasvapna</s>), where something constantly done is seen; an endless dream (<s>anantasvapna</s>), which continues throughout the entire night without being bounded; and a dream within a dream (<s>svapnasvapna</s>), where another dream is seen within a dream. Thus it is stated: for a renunciant who has an emission of semen in a dream, there is not even the slightest fault, because of the illusory nature of dreams. Otherwise, the celibate life would be unreliable, since there would be the undesirable consequence of an offense even through sexual misconduct in a dream.

body.text: rāgetyādi | rāgeṇāviṣṭaṃ parigṛhītaṃ yaccittaṃ tena rāgāviṣṭena cetasā yatirnārīṃ striyaṃ śrīghano na spṛśet | puṃnapuṃsakamiti | puruṣaṃ paṇḍakaṃ cetyarthaḥ | śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ |
body.translated_text: 'With passion' (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth. The mind that is possessed and seized by passion — with such a passion-possessed mind, the renunciant of <s>Śrīghana</s> should not touch a woman. 'A man or a eunuch' — meaning a male or a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch). The rest is easy to understand.

body.text: stanakakṣetyādi | stanau kakṣe ca oṣṭhau ca nābhiśca ūrū ca pārśve ca kukṣiśca malabhramaśceti dvandvaḥ | atastān stanakakṣauṣṭhanābhyūrupārśvakukṣimalabhramān yatiḥ saṃraktaḥ san na nindet, na nindāṃ kuryāt | na ca saṃstuyānna ca praśaṃsedityarthaḥ, aśobhanau tava payodharau śobhanau vā yāvadaṅgajāta iti | katamāsāṃ tu tān stanakakṣādīnna ninde[di]tyāha | strīṇāmiti | malabhramaśabdenātra strīṇāmaṅgajātamucyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Breasts, armpits' and so forth. 'Breasts and armpits and lips and navel and thighs and sides and belly and genitals' — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. Therefore, a renunciant, being passionate, should not criticize — should not censure — those [body parts]: breasts, armpits, lips, navel, thighs, sides, belly, and genitals. Nor should he praise them — meaning he should not extol them [with words like] 'Your breasts are ugly' or 'beautiful,' and so on up to the genitals. 'But of whom should one not criticize those breasts, armpits, and so forth?' He says: 'of women.' By the word '<s>malabhrama</s>' (genitals), the private parts of women are meant here.

body.text: yadyadvadedityādi | yat yadvacanaṃ striyāḥ antike striyaṃ śrīghanaḥ maithunādhyācāraṃ kartukāmaḥ puruṣo bravroti yathā yatheti yena yena prakāreṇa [tat]tadvacanaṃ yatiḥ striyaṃ na vadet tathā tatheti tena tena prakāreṇetyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Whatever one would say' and so forth. Whatever words a man who desires to commit sexual misconduct with a woman speaks in the presence of a woman, in whatever manner — such words, in such a manner, the renunciant should not speak to a woman.

body.text: agretyādi | yoṣicchabdena mātṛgrāmo vidhīyate | yā strī māṃ paricarenmama paricaryāṃ kuryāt | kutaḥ? rahaḥ, rahasītyarthaḥ | sā agrā bhavati, śreṣṭhā bhavati | vyādhihīneti vyādhirahitā | yaśasvinīti yaśaḥ samanvitā, kīrtiyuktā | lābhinī ca bhavati | keṣāmityāha | āyurādīnāṃ | ādiśabdena varṇabalasaukhyādīnāṃ grahaṇaṃ | ityādi na vaco brūyādityādi | agrā bhavati sā yoṣidityevamādikaṃ vācaṃ na vadet | ka ityāha | śrīghanaḥ | kīdṛkṣa ityāha | rāgāgnipluṣṭamānasaḥ | rāga evāgniḥ rāgāgnirdahanātmakatvāt, tena pluṣṭaṃ dagdhaṃ mānasaṃ ceto yasya sa evamucyate | kasyāgrato na vade[di]tyāha | purastācchrīghanaḥ strīṇāmityādi | strīṇāmagnataḥ, puruṣasya paṇḍakasya cetyarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Foremost' and so forth. By the word '<s>yoṣit</s>' (woman), 'womanhood' (<s>mātṛgrāma</s>) is indicated. 'Whatever woman were to attend upon me, were to render service to me' — where? 'In private' (<s>rahas</s>). 'She is the foremost' — she is the best. 'Free from disease' means without illness. 'Renowned' (<s>yaśasvinī</s>) means endowed with fame, possessing renown. 'And she gains' — of what? 'Of long life and the rest.' The word 'and the rest' includes complexion, strength, happiness, and so forth. 'Such speech one should not utter' and so forth — one should not speak words such as 'She is the foremost woman who [attends to me]' and so forth. Who [should not]? 'The <s>Śrīghana</s>.' Of what kind? 'One whose mind is burnt by the fire of passion.' Passion itself is the fire — '<s>rāgāgni</s>' — because of its nature of burning; by that [fire], the mind (<s>mānasa</s>) is burnt (<s>pluṣṭa</s>) — one who is thus [described] is so called. 'Before whom should he not speak?' He says: 'before women, the <s>Śrīghana</s>' and so forth — before women, and before men and <s>paṇḍakas</s>.

body.text: strīpuruṣayoḥ saṃyogārthaṃ dautyaṃ kartuṃ na labhyata iti darśayitumāha | vivāhāvāhayorityādi | tatra vivāho dārikāparigrahaḥ | anyena paribhuktasya mātṛgna masya saṃgrahaṇamāvāhaḥ vivāhaścāvāhaśca vivāhāvāhau | atastayorvivāhāvāhayoḥ | vivāhanimittaṃ saṃgrahanimittañca dautyakarma na kuryāt | ka ityāha | śrāmaṇerakaḥ | śrāmaṇera eva śrāmaṇerakaḥ | kecittu kutsāyāṃ kanaṃ vidadhati | kutsitaḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ śrāmaṇeraka iti | taiḥ kutsārtho darśanīyaḥ- kathaṃ kutsitosau yatiriti? dautyakarmakaraṇāditi cet, na pratiṣedho 'yaṃ vartate- na kuryāditi | yaśca na kurute, sa kathaṃ kutsāmāsādayati | tasmātsvārtha evāyaṃ kaneṣṭavyaḥ | na kevalaṃ vivāhāvāhanimittaṃ dautyaṃ na kuryāttatkṣaṇamaithunādhyācāranimittamapi na kurvātāpiśabdaḥ sūcayati | dāpayeyamityādi | tatra samutpannakarmaphalasatyaratnādisaṃpratyayaḥ śrāddhaḥ | tasmai śrāddhāyopāsakadārakāya imāṃ śrāddhāṃ upāsakadārikāṃ dāpayeyamiti | evamarthasaṃsyandanāsūtraṃ yatirbhāṣittuṃ na ghaṭate ||
body.translated_text: To show that acting as a go-between for the union of a man and woman is impermissible, he says: 'for marriage and taking [a wife]' and so forth. There, '<s>vivāha</s>' is the taking of a maiden. The taking of a woman who has been enjoyed by another is '<s>āvāha</s>.' 'Marriage and wife-taking' — <s>vivāha</s> and <s>āvāha</s>. Therefore, for the purpose of marriage and taking a wife, one should not perform the work of a go-between. Who? 'A novice' (<s>śrāmaṇeraka</s>). A novice is simply called <s>śrāmaṇeraka</s>. Some, however, assign the [diminutive] suffix <s>ka</s> in the sense of contempt — 'a contemptible novice is a <s>śrāmaṇeraka</s>.' Those [who hold this view] should demonstrate the contempt-meaning: 'How is this renunciant contemptible?' 'Because of performing the work of a go-between,' if that is the answer — [but] this is a prohibition that is currently operative: 'he should not do [it].' And one who does not do [it] — how does he incur contempt? Therefore, the suffix <s>ka</s> should be understood in its own [ordinary] sense. Not only should one not act as a go-between for marriage, but also the word '<s>api</s>' (also) indicates that one should not do so even for the purpose of a single act of sexual misconduct at that moment. '[Thinking:] "I shall give [in marriage]"' and so forth. There, one who has conviction in the reality of the fruits of <s>karma</s> and the three jewels is 'faithful' (<s>śrāddha</s>). 'I would give this faithful lay-follower's daughter to this faithful lay-follower's son' — such speech of the nature of arranging a match, the renunciant is not able to utter.

body.text: bījārthamityādi | garbhotpādanimittaṃ vratī gavādikaṃ na dadyāt | etānevāśvādīn bījārthaṃ parebhyaḥ kadācidapi na prārthayet ||
body.translated_text: 'For the purpose of seed' and so forth. For the purpose of producing an embryo, the vow-observer should not give away cattle and the like. And these same horses and the like — one should never request them from others for the purpose of breeding.

body.text: tulyametāsvityādi | bahavaḥ striyo yasya taṃ bahustrīkaṃ puruṣaṃ yatiḥ naivaṃ vadet- kimiti ekayā striyā sārdhaṃ mā tvaṃ tiṣṭha, kintu paripāṭayā sarvāḥ striyo vaseti ||
body.translated_text: 'Equally among these' and so forth. A man who has many wives — to such a man with many wives, the renunciant should not say: 'Why do you stay with just one wife? Rather, live with all the wives in rotation.'

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ maithunaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the third [section], the precept of abstaining from sexual misconduct (<s>maithunaviratiśikṣāpada</s>) [is completed].

body.text: mṛṣāvādaviratiśikṣāpadamadhikṛtyāha | pratyekabuddhetyādi | tatrātmārthaṃmekaṃ prati buddha iti pratyekabuddhaḥ | samyagaviparītaṃ samantāt jñeyaṃ buddhā iti saṃbuddhāḥ | teṣāṃ śiṣyāstacchiṣyāḥ | tacchabdenātra saṃbuddhā eva parigṛhyante, na pratyekabuddhā tacchabdasyānantarābhidhāyitvāt | pratyeka buddhāśca saṃbuddhāśca tacchiṣyāśceti vigrahaḥ | teṣāṃ yat jñānaṃ darśanañca tat mamāsti, mama saṃvidyata iti | asaṃvidyamānamapi santaṃ yaḥ śrāmaṇero mṛṣā vakti sa nāśanīyo 'śrāmaṇeratvena dhārayitavya ityarthaḥ | kiṃ punarabhimānādapi yo bravīti so 'pi nāśyaḥ? netyāha | anyatrābhimānataḥ | anyatraśabdo varjanārthe vartate | anyatra bhīṣmadroṇābhyāṃ sarve yodhāḥ parāṅmukhā iti anyatraśabdasya varjanārthe prayogadarśanāt | aprāpte uttaraviśeṣādhigame prāpto mayeti manyamānasya yā cittasyonnatiḥ sobhimānaḥ | tasmādabhimānādyo jñānaṃ darśanañca pra[ti]jānīte tasya saṃvaratyāgo na bhavati prāptasaṃjñitvāt |
body.translated_text: With regard to the precept of abstaining from false speech (<s>mṛṣāvādaviratiśikṣāpada</s>), he says: '<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>' and so forth. There, 'one who is awakened for his own sake, in respect of one [thing at a time]' is a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. 'Those who have understood correctly and non-erroneously all that is to be known in every respect' are the '<s>Saṃbuddhas</s>' (Perfectly Awakened Ones). Their disciples are 'their disciples' (<s>tacchiṣya</s>). By the pronoun 'their' (<s>tat</s>), only the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> are meant here, not the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, because the pronoun refers to the immediately preceding [noun]. '<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Saṃbuddhas</s> and their disciples' — this is the analysis [of the compound]. 'Their knowledge and vision exists in me, is present in me' — a novice who falsely claims [to possess] what he does not possess is to be expelled and should be regarded as having lost novice-status. 'But is one who claims [it] out of mere conceit also to be expelled?' He says: 'No — except from conceit.' The word 'except' (<s>anyatra</s>) functions in the sense of exclusion, as the usage of <s>anyatra</s> in the sense of exclusion is seen in [the phrase] 'Except for <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>, all warriors turned their backs.' The elation of mind of one who thinks 'I have attained [something]' regarding a superior spiritual attainment that has not [actually] been attained — that is conceit (<s>abhimāna</s>). Therefore, for one who claims knowledge and vision out of conceit, there is no loss of restraint, because he has the perception of having attained [it].

body.text: yaduktaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ mamāstīti bruvan mithyā nāśya iti tatra katarajjñānaṃ katamacca darśanamiti na jñāyate | ato jñānadarśanaṃ tayorlakṣaṇamadhikṛtyāha | jñānaṃ satyābhisaṃbodhirityādi | satyāni catvāri duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgākhyāni | tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ pañcopādānaskandhāḥ | samudayasatyaṃ paunarbhavikī tṛṣṇā | nirodhasatyaṃ yadasyāḥ paunarbhavikyāḥ tṛṣṇāyāḥ prahāṇaṃ | mārgasatyaṃ ayamevāryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ tadyathā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ, samyaksaṃkalpaḥ, samyagvāk, samyakkarmāntaḥ, samyagājīvaḥ, samyagvyāyāmaḥ, samyaksmṛtiḥ, samyaksamādhiśca | tatra bodhanaṃ bodhiravagamaḥ avabodhaḥ parijñānaṃ bodhijñānārthatvāt | abhītyayamupasarga ābhimukhye (

children.text: ) vartate, samītya'viparītatve | tenāyaṃ vākyārtho jāyate- duḥkhādīnāmāryasatyānāṃ nirvāṇābhimukhā samyagaviparītā yā bodhistajjñānamucyate | abhijñāḥ pañca darśanamiti | abhijñānamabhijñājñānamityarthaḥ | tatra pañcābhijñāḥ | divyaṃ cakṣuryenātidūrasūkṣmavyavahitāni rūpāṇi paśyati karatalāvasthitamivāmalakaṃ, divyaṃ śroto yena dūrāsannāḥ śabdā śrūyante devamanuṣyāṇāmantaśaḥ kuntapipīlikasyāpi, paracittajñānaṃ yena parakīyān cittacaittān jānāti- sarāgaṃ cittaṃ sarāgamityādi, pūrvanivāsānusmṛtikṣānaṃ yenātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ cābhinivṛttajātiparaṃparāḥ smarati- amutrāhaṃ evannāmā evaṃgotrāka ityādi, āstravakṣayajñānaṃ yenātmano jānāti- kṣīṇā me jātiruṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ yāvannāparamitthatvamiti | etāḥ paṃcābhijñā darśanabhityucyante ||
children.translated_text: ) and '<s>samī</s>' in the sense of 'correctly, non-erroneously.' Therefore this sentence-meaning arises: the correct, non-erroneous awakening directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> regarding the Noble Truths of suffering and the rest — that is called 'knowledge' (<s>jñāna</s>). 'The five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) are vision (<s>darśana</s>).' '<s>Abhijñāna</s>' means the knowledge of superknowledge. There are five <s>abhijñās</s>: the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>), by which one sees forms that are extremely distant, minute, or concealed, as if [seeing] a myrobalan fruit placed on the palm of one's hand; the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), by which sounds both distant and near are heard, of gods and humans, and even of an ant or a small insect; the knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>), by which one knows others' minds and mental factors — 'a mind with passion is [known as] a mind with passion' and so forth; the knowledge of the recollection of former existences (<s>pūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñāna</s>), by which one remembers one's own and others' past successive births — 'There I was, of such a name, of such a clan' and so forth; and the knowledge of the destruction of the influxes (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>), by which one knows of oneself: 'Birth is exhausted, the holy life has been lived, there is no further existence beyond this.' These five <s>abhijñās</s> are called 'vision' (<s>darśana</s>).

body.translated_text: As stated: 'One who falsely says "I possess knowledge and vision" is to be expelled' — but what is this 'knowledge' and what is this 'vision'? This is not known. Therefore, regarding 'knowledge and vision,' he addresses their definitions: 'Knowledge is the awakening to the truths' and so forth. The truths are four, called suffering, origin, cessation, and path. There, the truth of suffering is the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandha</s>). The truth of origin is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) leading to renewed existence. The truth of cessation is the abandonment of that craving leading to renewed existence. The truth of the path is just this Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>), namely: right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). There, 'awakening' (<s>bodhi</s>) is comprehension, understanding, full knowledge — because <s>bodhi</s> has the meaning of knowledge. The prefix '<s>abhi</s>' functions in the sense of 'directed toward'

body.text: upalakṣaṇārthame[ta]jjñānadarśanagrahaṇamiti pratipādayannāha | dharmānvayādiketyādi | dharmatattvālambanaṃ jñānaṃ dharmajñānaṃ yena kleśān prajahāti | yatparasantānānugamaṃ jñānaṃ pratyātmavedyamutpadyate yairanyaiḥ kleśaprahāṇaṃ kṛtaṃ, ye pi sāṃprataṃ kurvanti kariṣyanti vā tepīdṛśameva jñānamadhigatavantau'dhigacchanti adhigamiṣyantītyetadanvayajñānaṃ | ādiśabdena saṃvṛtajñānādīn grāhayati |
body.translated_text: In order to demonstrate that the mention of '<s>jñānadarśana</s>' (knowledge and vision) is for the purpose of implication, [the text] says: '<s>Dharmānvaya</s> and so forth,' etc. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) that has the reality of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmatattva</s>) as its support is <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of <s>dharmas</s>), by which one abandons the defilements (<s>kleśas</s>). The knowledge that follows the continuum of others (<s>parasantānānugama</s>), which arises as personally experienced — that by which others have abandoned defilements, are abandoning them now, or will abandon them — [the knowledge that] they too have attained, are attaining, or will attain precisely such knowledge — this is <s>anvayajñāna</s> (inferential knowledge). By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), <s>saṃvṛtajñāna</s> (conventional knowledge) and the others are included.

children.translated_text: <s>Dharmajñāna</s>, <s>anvayajñāna</s>, <s>sāṃvṛta</s> (conventional [knowledge]), knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittavit</s>),
<s>sādhya</s> (that which is to be accomplished), <s>naimittika</s> (causal [knowledge]), and the seventh called <s>praṇidhā</s> (aspiration-knowledge).

body.text: iti saptānāṃ jñānānāṃ ślokaḥ | dharmajñānādīnāmaṅgīkaraṇe anyaṃ pūrvokto na yogya iti saṃvaratyāgo bhavatīti ||
body.translated_text: This is the verse of the seven knowledges. When accepting <s>dharmajñāna</s> and the rest [as one's own attainment], another [who is] as previously stated [i.e., one who hasn't actually attained them] is not fit — thus a loss of restraint (<s>saṃvaratyāga</s>) occurs.

body.text: āryamlecchetyādi | āryaśabdenātrāryadeśajāḥ puruṣāḥ parigṛhyante na prahīṇakleśāḥ mlecchaśabdena ca śavarādayaḥ | teṣāṃ yadvacanaṃ tena lekhena deśāntarasthasya lipyā saṃmukhameva likhitvā | hastamudrayeti aṅgulīvinyāsena | hastyavikāreṇetyabhinayena yaḥ śrāmaṇero jñānadarśanādikaṃ pratijānīte, tadapi [jñāna]darśanādikaṃ mṛṣeti boddhavyaṃ | lekhādiṣvaparān bodhayataḥ saṃvaratyāgo na bhavati vākpravyāhārābhāvāt ||
body.translated_text: '<s>Ārya</s> or <s>mleccha</s>,' etc. By the word '<s>ārya</s>' here, persons born in civilized (<s>ārya</s>) lands are included, not those who have abandoned defilements. By the word '<s>mleccha</s>' (barbarian), <s>Śabaras</s> and the like [are meant]. Whether by their speech, or by letter — having written to one in another region in script, face to face; 'by hand-gesture' (<s>hastamudrā</s>) means by arrangement of fingers; 'by bodily expression' (<s>hastyavikāra</s>) means by gesture — whatever <s>śrāmaṇera</s> claims <s>jñānadarśana</s> and the like [by these means], that too — the [claimed] knowledge-and-vision and the like — is to be understood as false. However, when informing others through letter and the like [without verbal utterance], there is no loss of restraint, due to the absence of verbal utterance.

body.text: vṛkṣamūletyādi || ahamekākyadvitīyo vṛkṣamūle viharāmi śūnye ca mandire gṛhe ahaṃ rame, mama ca yaccittaṃ tadekāgraṃ samāhitamityevamādi atīndriyaṃ vastu yatinā na vācyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: 'At the foot of a tree,' etc. 'I dwell alone, without a companion, at the foot of a tree; in an empty temple or house I delight; and my mind is one-pointed, concentrated' — such and similar supersensory matters (<s>atīndriya vastu</s>) should not be spoken by an ascetic.

body.text: atiprasaṅganivṛttyarthamāha || buddhādīnāmiti | varṇoguṇaḥ, sa bahudhā tathā gatasya loke khyāpayitavyaḥ svaparārthasaṃpādakatvāt | ityapi sa bhagavān daśabhirbalaiḥ samanvāgataścaturbhiḥ vaiśāradyaiḥ tribhiḥ smṛtyupasthānaiḥ mahākaruṇayā ceti | ādigrahaṇena dharmasaṃghayorapi | ātmanastu guṇaḥ kenacidapi prakāreṇa na vaktavyaḥ | kathañcaneti kathañcidityarthaḥ | pṛṣṭastu san yatiḥ parakīyaṃ guṇaṃ saṃvidyamānaṃ vadettatrāpi tasya guṇavataḥ pudgalasya saṃmukhaṃ na vadet ||
body.translated_text: To prevent overextension [of the rule], [the text] says: 'Of the <s>Buddhas</s> and others.' The 'praise' means 'quality.' That [quality] of the <s>Tathāgata</s> should be proclaimed in the world in many ways, because it accomplishes the benefit of self and others — namely, that the Blessed One is endowed with the ten powers (<s>bala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), the three special foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). By the word 'etc.' (<s>ādi</s>), the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s> are also included. But one's own qualities should not be spoken by any means whatsoever. 'In any way' means 'by whatever means.' However, when asked, an ascetic should speak of another's qualities that actually exist — but even then, he should not speak in the presence of that virtuous person.

body.text: yadāha brūyāttatsaṃmukhaṃ na tu [iti] vistareṇānadhigatasvabhāvamṛṣāvādalakṣaṇaṃ pratipādayitumanā cāryānāryavyavahārānupanyasati | dṛṣṭamityādinā | tatra dṛṣṭaṃ yaccakṣurvijñānenānubhūtaṃ śrutaṃ yacchotravijñātaṃ, mataṃ yadghrāṇajihvākāya vijñānaiḥ vijñātaṃ yanmanovijñānenetyeke | apare punarāhuḥ- dṛṣṭaṃ yat pañcabhirindriyaiḥ paricchinnaṃ, śrutaṃ yatparata āgamitaṃ, mataṃ yatsvayamupapattito 'vadhāritaṃ, vijñātaṃ yanmanasā pratyātmavedyenākāreṇa paricchannaṃ | tasmin dṛṣṭe dṛṣṭamiti vadet yāvadvijñātaṃmiti | vaiparītyena gadanmithyābhidhāyaka iti | viparītasya bhāvo vaiparītyaṃ tena anāryavyavahāreṇetyarthaḥ | anāryavyavahārāśca punaradṛṣṭe dṛṣṭavādikādayaḥ | gadanniti vadan | mithyābhidhāyaka iti mṛṣāvādī syādityartha ||
body.translated_text: 'What one would say, one should not [say] in [that person's] presence' — wishing to demonstrate at length the characteristic of false speech with respect to one who has not attained its nature, and presenting the customs of civilized and uncivilized behavior, [the text says:] 'seen,' etc. Therein, 'seen' (<s>dṛṣṭa</s>) is what is experienced through visual consciousness; 'heard' (<s>śruta</s>) is what is known through auditory consciousness; 'thought' (<s>mata</s>) is what is known through the consciousnesses of smell, taste, and touch; 'cognized' (<s>vijñāta</s>) is what is [known] through mental consciousness — according to some. Others, however, say: 'seen' is what is discerned by the five sense-faculties; 'heard' is what is received from others through scripture; 'thought' is what is ascertained by oneself through reasoning; 'cognized' is what is discerned by the mind through a personally experienced mode. Regarding the seen, one should say 'seen' — and so forth up to 'cognized.' Speaking in the opposite way, one is a false speaker — in an uncivilized manner, that is the meaning. The uncivilized behaviors are: claiming to have seen what was not seen, and so forth. 'Speaking' means 'saying.' 'A false speaker' means one who lies — that is the meaning.

body.text: katibhiḥ punaraṅgaiḥ mṛṣāvādī syādityāha | vastu cetyādi ślokaḥ | vastu ca bhavati, alīkasaṃjñī ca bhavati, vinihitaṃ cittaṃ bhavati, mṛṣāvādasaṃjño bhavati, vācaṃ ca bhāṣate | etāni pañcāṅgāni yasya santi sa pañcāṅgaḥ | kaḥ punarasāvityāha | anṛtavādikaḥ | anṛtaḥ vādaḥ yasyāstīti [sa] anṛtavādikaḥ mṛṣāvādīti yorthaḥ | tatra vastu ca bhavatīti- yathā paricchinnaṃ tathā tadastītyarthato na tu dravyatostīti, anyathā hyasaṃvidyamānaṃ vastva'stoti jñātvā nāstīti bruvato 'nāpattiḥ syāt | alīkasaṃjñī ca bhavatīti- yathā paricchinnādanyathā kathayāmītyeva saṃjñā ityarthaḥ | cittaṃ vinihitaṃ bhavatīti yathā paricchinnajñeyaviparītadyotinīvāksamutthāpakaṃ (

children.text: ) cittaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ | evamapi mṛṣāvādasaṃjñī ca bhavatīti atraivāntargatatvāt kasmāta pṛthagucyate | naitadasti | mṛṣāvādasajñitvena paravañcanābhiprāya ucyate | tasminstu satīda yathārtha paricchinnajñeyaviparītārthadyātinyā vācaḥ samutthāpakaṃ cittaṃ pṛthageva kāraṇatvenocyata iti naitasminnantarbhāvaḥ | tathā ca vinaye vinidhāya saṃjñāṃ vinidhāya citaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣata iti mṛṣāvādasaṃjñī ca bhavatīti paravañcanābhiprāya ityarthaḥ | vitathasaṃjñino 'nyaḥ ko viśeṣa iti cet vitathasaṃjñī hayanyathārthaṃ pratipādayati na tu paraṃ vañcayati | tathā ca mṛṣāvāda iṣyate yathā śnigdhaste mukhavarṇa ityādinā | naitaduktaṃ bhavati | yo vitathasaṃjñī sa nāvaśyaṃ mṛṣāvādasaṃjñī, yastu mṛṣāvādasaṃjñī so 'vaśyaṃ vitathasaṃjñīti yena dvābhyāmevāṅgābhyāṃ mṛṣāvāda iṣyata iti | vadedvācamiti | vākpravyāhāraṃ karotītyarthaḥ | etaduktaṃ bhavati | caturaṅgavanti yāni vacāṃsi tāni mṛṣāvādavyapadeśabhāñji bhavantīti | na kevalaṃ pañcabhiraṅgaiḥ saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo bhavati, kintu hyekenāpīti darśayannāha | catustrītyādi | pūrvamuktāni yānyaṅgāni te[bhyaḥ] varjitāni yānyaṅgāni taiḥ samanvāgato yo yatirmṛṣā vakti, so 'nyairyatibhirmṛṣāvādī jñeyaḥ | tatra caturbhiraṅgaiḥ mṛṣāvādī bhavati | alīkasaṃjñī cetyādi | alīkasajñitvena vastunaḥ parigrahānna pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ | tribhiraṅgairvinihitaṃ cetyādi | alīkasaṃjñāyā vinihitacitta evāntarbhāvāt | dvābhyāmevāṅgābhyāṃ mṛṣāvādasaṃjñī cetyādi | vinihitasya mṛṣāvāda evāntarbhāvāt | ekenāṅgena saṃprajānamṛṣāvādo bhavati, yadā vinidhāya cittaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate | atrāpi pūrvakāṇāmaṅgānāṃ na pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ sāmarthyalabdhatvāt | (
children.translated_text: — that is the meaning. [Objection:] Even so, since 'one has the cognition of false speech' is already included in this very [factor], why is it stated separately? This is not so. By 'having the cognition of false speech,' the intention to deceive others is denoted. When that [deceptive intention] is present, the mind that produces speech indicating the opposite of the knowable as properly discerned is stated separately as a cause — thus it is not subsumed within the other. And thus in the <s>Vinaya</s>: 'having directed the cognition, having directed the mind, one speaks speech' — thus 'one has the cognition of false speech' means the intention to deceive others. What difference is there from one who has a wrong cognition (<s>vitathasaṃjñin</s>)? The one with a wrong cognition conveys a different meaning but does not [intend to] deceive the other. And thus false speech is acknowledged [even] in statements like 'Your complexion is radiant' and the like. This does not mean the following: whoever has a wrong cognition necessarily has the cognition of false speech; but whoever has the cognition of false speech necessarily has a wrong cognition — [such] that false speech would be acknowledged by two factors alone. 'He utters speech' means: he produces a verbal utterance. This is what is stated: those utterances that possess four factors are designated as false speech. Not only with five factors does deliberate false speech occur, but even with a single one — demonstrating this, [the text] says: 'four, three,' etc. The factors that are excluded from the previously stated factors — an ascetic endowed with those [remaining factors] who speaks falsely is to be known by other ascetics as a false speaker. Therein, with four factors one is a false speaker: 'one has a false cognition,' etc. — by virtue of a false cognition, the taking up of a thing [is implied], so there is no separate mention. With three factors: 'the mind is directed,' etc. — because a false cognition is already subsumed in a directed mind. With two factors alone: 'one has the cognition of false speech,' etc. — because a directed [mind] is already subsumed in false speech itself. With a single factor, deliberate false speech occurs when, having directed the mind, one speaks speech. Here too, the previous factors are not separately mentioned because they are obtained by implication.

children.text: ) anyathā hi saṃkhyānupūrvī vidhānārthamekenāṅgena mṛṣāvādī bhavati, yāvat pañcabhirityuktaṃ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise, by an ordinal enumeration for the purpose of a rule, it would have been said: 'with one factor one is a false speaker, up to: with five [factors]' [which is not the case].

body.translated_text: By how many factors does one become a false speaker? [The text] says: 'A thing,' etc. — [this is] a verse. There is a thing (<s>vastu</s>); one has a false cognition (<s>alīkasaṃjñin</s>); the mind is directed (<s>vinihita citta</s>); one has the cognition of false speech (<s>mṛṣāvādasaṃjña</s>); and one utters speech. These are the five factors; one who possesses them is 'five-factored.' Who is that? [The text] says: a false speaker (<s>anṛtavādika</s>). One who has false speech — he is called a false speaker, i.e., a liar. Therein, 'there is a thing' means that as it is discerned, so it exists — in terms of meaning, but not [necessarily] in terms of substance; otherwise, knowing that a non-existent thing exists, if one says 'it does not exist,' there would be no offense. 'One has a false cognition' means: the cognition 'I shall speak otherwise than as it was discerned' — that is the meaning. 'The mind is directed' means: [there is] a mind that produces speech indicating the opposite of the knowable as discerned.

body.text: abhūtenetyādi | yatiḥ saṃmukhaṃ yati na codayet | kīdṛśo yatirityāha | dhvaṃsanacyāvanākūtaḥ | ākūto 'bhiprāyaḥ | tena dhvaṃsanābhiprāyaścodanābhiprāyaḥ yatiryati na cādayedityarthaḥ | doṣairabhyākhyānadānaṃ dhvaṃsanaṃ | brahmacaryāvasthitasyāvapravrājanaṃ cyāvanaṃ | kena na codayedityāha | prāṇātipātādattādānamṛṣāvādādinā | abhūtenetyādi | abhūtenetyasyāvidyamānena | anidāneneti niṣkāraṇenetyarthaḥ anidānaśabdasyākāraṇaparyāyatvāt | kṣudretyādi | kṣudrā laghīyasī sā āpattiḥ duṣkṛtasaṃjñitā saiva nimitta kāraṇaṃ codanāyāḥ tena kṣudrāpattinimittena | athavā leśamātreṇa duṣkṛtamātreṇa abhiprāyeṇa | tenaiveti pūrvoktena dhvaṃsanacyāvanābhiprāyeṇetyarthaḥ | pratyakṣaṃ śrāmaṇero parānna kṣipet, nāsvācakṣīteti yāvat | jātiliṅgetyādi | jātiranvayaḥ kulamityeko 'rthaḥ | liṅgaṃ dehacihnaṃ | kriyā karma jīvikopāyo vṛttirityanarthāntaraṃ | vādaśabdaḥ pratyekamabhisaṃbadhyate | jātivādaśca liṅgavādaścetyādi dvandvaḥ | taiḥ pratyekaṃ hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭaiḥ vratī prāṇān pudgalān jihmakaraṇārthaṃ niṣpratibhānakaraṇārthaṃ na jātu kadāciccodayet | upakleśetyādi | tatra upakleśo jaḍimatvādi | gado vyādhiḥ | ākrośo duścaritairgarhaṇaṃ | āpattiḥ kāyavāṅmanobhirbhagavadājñāvyatikramaḥ | upakleśādinā vratī vratinamāśayenābhiprāyeṇa puroktena jihmaniṣpratibhānakaraṇābhiprāyeṇa brūyānnaiva kadācaneti, kadācidapi na vadedityarthaḥ | atra ca hīnamadhyotkṛṣṭabhedo (

children.text: ) nāsti hīnatvādevopakleśādeḥ | anena ca ślokadvayena codyasya pudgalasya caturvidhānyūnatoktā- jātivādena kulanyūnatā, liṅgavādena dehanyūnatā, kriyāvādena vṛttinyūnatā, āpattyākrośasaṃkleśairguṇanyūnatābhihitā |
children.translated_text: ) does not apply, since defilement and the like are by nature inferior. And by these two verses, four types of deficiency of the accused person are stated: by birth-speech, deficiency of family; by mark-speech, deficiency of body; by action-speech, deficiency of livelihood; by offense, reproach, and defilement, deficiency of qualities is stated.

body.translated_text: "With something untrue" and so forth. An ascetic should not accuse an ascetic face to face. What kind of ascetic? He says: "with the intent to degrade and expel." "Intent" (<s>ākūta</s>) means intention. Thus, an ascetic whose intention is to degrade and whose intention is to accuse should not accuse an ascetic — this is the meaning. "Degradation" (<s>dhvaṃsana</s>) is the imputation of faults through false accusation. "Expulsion" (<s>cyāvana</s>) is causing one established in the holy life to be removed from ordination. With what should one not accuse? He says: with killing, taking what is not given, false speech, and the like. "With something untrue" and so forth — "untrue" means non-existent. "Without cause" means without reason, since the word "<s>nidāna</s>" is a synonym for "cause." "Minor" and so forth — a minor, i.e., lesser, offense designated as a transgression (<s>duṣkṛta</s>) — that itself being the ground, the cause of accusation, i.e., on the ground of a minor offense. Or, with a mere trifle, with a mere transgression, with intention. "With that very" means with the aforementioned intent to degrade and expel. A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> should not face to face cast [aspersions on] others, should not accuse, as it were. "Birth, marks" and so forth — "birth" (<s>jāti</s>) means lineage, family — this is one meaning. "Mark" (<s>liṅga</s>) means a bodily sign. "Action" (<s>kriyā</s>) means <s>karma</s>, means of livelihood, occupation — these are synonymous. The word "speech" connects with each: "birth-speech and mark-speech" and so forth is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. With those, individually, whether inferior, middling, or superior, the observant one should never at any time accuse living beings for the purpose of causing shame and confusion. "Defilement" and so forth — therein, "defilement" (<s>upakleśa</s>) is dullness and the like. "Disease" (<s>gada</s>) is illness. "Reproach" (<s>ākrośa</s>) is censure through misconduct. "Offense" (<s>āpatti</s>) is transgression of the Blessed One’s command through body, speech, and mind. The observant one should never at any time say to an observant one, with the aforementioned intent of causing shame and confusion, [anything] regarding defilement and the like — meaning one should never speak [thus]. And here, the distinction of inferior, middling, and superior

children.translated_text: By offense, reproach, and defilement, deficiency of qualities is declared;
by speeches about birth, marks, and actions — family, body, and livelihood [are impugned].

body.text: iti saṃgrahaślokaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the summary verse.

body.text: yaterapratirūpatvātprakṛtisāvadyatvācca paiśunyamācarituṃ na labhyata iti darśayannāha | bhedaṃ yāsyatītyādi | ayaṃ pudgalo anena pudgalena saha bhetsyati, mayā saha saṃvāsyatīti evaṃ matvā yatirjātyādivādena paiśunyaṃ na samācaret |
body.translated_text: To show that because it is unbecoming of an ascetic and because it is inherently blameworthy, slander (<s>paiśunya</s>) should not be practiced, he says: "He will become divided" and so forth. Thinking "this person will break with that person and will live with me," an ascetic should not practice slander through speech about birth and the like.

body.text: tatra kārikātrayeṇa saṃvaratyāga uktaḥ śeṣaistu ślokaiḥ pañcāṅgāni, yasmādaduṣkṛtāni codāhṛtāni |
body.translated_text: In that [section], by three verses the abandonment of restraint is stated; by the remaining verses, the five factors are [presented], since transgressions also are illustrated.

children.translated_text: One who, not having attained <s>dhyāna</s> and the like, makes wise persons hear [that he has] —
or alternatively, how does one who communicates [what he has attained] out of ignorance not lose his restraint?

body.text: iti prahelikā ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the riddle (<s>prahelīkā</s>).

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ mṛṣāvādaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ caturthaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>: the fourth training precept, on refraining from false speech, [is complete].

body.text:
avasaraprāptaṃ surāmaireyamadyapānaviratiśikṣāpadamadhikṛtyāha | madyamityādi |
yasmāt surāmaireyamadyapānaṃ pramādasya kuśaladharmānavahitatāyā āspadaṃ pratiṣṭhā, tasmātkāraṇādyatibhistatsurāmaireyamadyaṃ parasmai na deyaṃ na cātmanā pātavyaṃ | kiṃ vadityajñasaṃdigdhaviparyastānāmajñānasandehaviparyāsāpanayanārthaṃ dṛṣṭāntamāha | śvamūtravaditi | yathā śuno mūtraṃ parasmai na dīyate na cātmanā pīyate, tadvachrāmaṇereṇa surāmaireyamadyaṃ parasmai na deyaṃ, na cātmanāpi peya | svamūtravadityapi pāṭhaḥ | tatraitad vyākhyānaṃ- ātmīyaprasrāvavaditi |
body.translated_text: Having obtained the opportunity, he addresses the training precept on refraining from drinking <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor. He says: "Intoxicants" and so forth. Since the drinking of <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor is the basis and foundation of heedlessness, of inattentiveness to wholesome qualities, therefore ascetics should not give that <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor to another, nor should they drink it themselves. To remove the ignorance, doubt, and misunderstanding of the ignorant, doubting, and confused, he gives an illustration: "Like dog’s urine" —

body.text: tatra suretyāsava ucyate | annenānnavikāreṇa ca yā saṃcīyate, sā ca trividhāvagantavyā | kathaṃ kṛtvetyāha | valkalaiḥ saguḍairityādi | kācitsurā guḍasahitaiḥ valkalaiḥ saṃcīyate, aparā madhūnaiva kevalena | piṣṭo 'pūpaḥ, kiṇvaṃ surābījaṃ, jalaṃ toyaṃ | ebhirapi kācitsurā saṃcīyata ityetāḥ surā jñātavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, by the word "<s>surā</s>," fermented liquor is meant. That which is brewed from grain and grain-preparations is understood to be of three kinds. How is it made? He says: "With bark, together with molasses" and so forth. One kind of <s>surā</s> is brewed with bark mixed with molasses; another with honey alone. "<s>Piṣṭa</s>" means cake; "<s>kiṇva</s>" means yeast, the seed of <s>surā</s>; "<s>jala</s>" means water. With these too a certain <s>surā</s> is brewed — these [types of] <s>surā</s> should be known.

body.text: maireyamityādi | dhātrī āmalakīphalaṃ, ambu pānīyaṃ, dhātakī lokapratītyaiva kusumajātiḥ | guḍena dhātryā ambunā dhātakyā ca yatsaṃskṛtaṃ niṣpāditaṃ rasāntaraṃ tanmaireyamucyate | surāmaireyamadyaṃ tadyasmānmadanīyamataḥ kuśāgreṇāpi pātuṃ yatīnāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāṃ na prakalpate, na labhyate | na kevalaṃ jalādivattatpātuṃ na kalpate, kuśāgreṇāpītyapiśabdenāha ||
body.translated_text: "<s>Maireya</s>" and so forth. "<s>Dhātrī</s>" is the <s>āmalakī</s> fruit (emblic myrobalan); "<s>ambu</s>" is water; "<s>dhātakī</s>" is a species of flower known by common usage. That which is prepared, produced, as a different extract with molasses, <s>dhātrī</s>, water, and <s>dhātakī</s> — that is called <s>maireya</s>. <s>Surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor — since they cause intoxication, it is not permissible for ascetics, for <s>śrāmaṇera</s>s, to drink even with the tip of a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass. Not only is it not permissible to drink it like water and the like, but even with the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> blade — the word "even" (<s>api</s>)

body.text: surāmaireyavyatiriktamanyadapi madanīyaṃ vastu paribhoktuṃ na labhyata iti darśayannāha | kodravānnamityādi | kodravabhaktaṃ yatirnaṃ bhuñjīta, na ca tasya kodravasya (

children.text: ) palāle svapet | madayedityādi | yaccānyatsurāmaireyavyatiriktaṃ madyavarṇagandharasaṃ pītaṃ sanmadayenmadaṃ janayet, tadapi na pātavyaṃ | pibato duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati | ata eva madanīyaṃ pūgaphalādi jñātvā na bhakṣaṇīyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: ). "Would intoxicate" and so forth — whatever other [substance] apart from <s>surā</s> and <s>maireya</s>, having the color, smell, and taste of intoxicants, when drunk would intoxicate, would produce intoxication — that too should not be drunk. One who drinks commits a transgression. Therefore, knowing intoxicating [substances] such as betel-nut and the like, one should not consume them.

body.translated_text: To show that other intoxicating substances besides <s>surā</s> and <s>maireya</s> also should not be consumed, he says: "<s>Kodrava</s> food" and so forth. An ascetic should not eat <s>kodrava</s> grain, nor should he sleep on the husks of that <s>kodrava</s>

children.translated_text: If a novice (<s>cellaka</s>) were to drink <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor, and give it [to others],

children.text: kodravānnaṃ ca bhuñjīta na ca syāt duṣkṛtaṃ kathaṃ ||
children.translated_text: and eat <s>kodrava</s> food — how would there be no transgression?

body.text: iti prahelikā ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the riddle (<s>prahelīkā</s>).

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ surāmaireyamadyapānaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāma pañcamaṃ samāptaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>: the fifth [training precept], named the training precept on refraining from drinking <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor, is complete.

body.text: uktaṃ surāmaireyamadyapānaviratiśikṣāpadalakṣaṇaṃ | idānīmuccaśayanamahāśayanaviratiśikṣāpadalakṣaṇaṃ labdhvāvakāśamityāha | śayane yatirāsīta [i]tyādi | tatra jitakleśatvādbhagavān jinaḥ | tasyāṣṭau yānyaṅgulāni tatpramāṇaṃ pādakamasyeti jināṣṭāṅgulapādakaṃ śayanāsanaṃ | etacca jināṣṭāṅgulapramāṇaṃ sāmānyapuruṣāṣṭāṅgulapramāṇena triguṇaṃ bhavati | ataścaturviśatyaṅgulyo bhavanti | tena hastapramāṇamityākhyātaṃ bhavatīti | yacchayanāsanaṃ pramāṇapuruṣahastapramāṇapādakaṃ tasmin mañce pīṭhe vā yatiḥ śrāmaṇeraḥ āsīta [u]paviśedityarthaḥ | kiṃ saha śalyena? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi vinā śalye[na], śalyaṃ hitvetyarthaḥ | ataḥ pramāṇādhike mañce pīṭhe vā ya upaviśati, tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati | hemarūpyakṛte na tviti | suvarṇarūpyamaye tu mañce pīṭhe vā jināṣṭāṅgulapramāṇepyupaviṣṭuṃ [na] labhyata iti | atha kimarthamidamabhidhīyate- hemarūpyakṛte neti? yāvatā kāyena pāṇipādādyairvastracchatrādinetyādi vakṣyate | yatra ca vastrādinā sparśaḥ pratiṣidhyate, tatra sutarāmupabhogo [na] labhyata iti | satyametat | kintu kasyacidiyamāśaṅkā syāt sāṃghike rukmarūpyamaye śayanāsane upaviśato na kaściddoṣaḥ paudgalikasyaiva sparśapratiṣedhāditi | ata idamucyata iti | kecitparihāraṃ varṇayanti | tadetadasat, aviśeṣeṇa sāṃghikapaudgalikayorjātarūparajatayoḥ sparśapratiṣedhāt || tasmātparihārāya yatna āsteyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The characteristic of the training precept on refraining from drinking <s>surā</s>, <s>maireya</s>, and intoxicating liquor has been stated. Now, having obtained the opportunity, he states the characteristic of the training precept on refraining from high and luxurious beds. He says: "On a bed the ascetic should sit" and so forth. Therein, because he has conquered the afflictions, the Blessed One is the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>). A bed whose measure has his eight finger-breadths as a foot is a bed-and-seat measured by the Conqueror’s eight finger-breadths. And this measure of the Conqueror’s eight finger-breadths is three times the measure of an ordinary person’s eight finger-breadths.

body.text: tatrāpi jināṣṭāṅgulapramāṇe 'pi mañce pīṭhe vā vinā pratyāstaraṇenopaviṣṭuṃ [na] labhyata iti darśayitumāha | sāṃghike śayane dadyādityādi | saṃghasyeda sāṃghikaṃ śayanāsanaṃ | tatra pratyāstaraṇaṃ yatiḥ prayacchet | tacca pratyāstaraṇa na tṛṇapatrādika mabhipretaṃ, kintu viṣṭaretyāha | vastretyādi | sūkṣmasya vastrasya tripuṭaṃ ghanasya vastrasya dvipuṭaṃ kambalasya ekapuṭaṃ pratyāstaraṇamiṣṭaṃ, abhipretamityartha | kramāditi yathākramaṃ, pratyāstaraṇasya tridvayekapuṭabhedo 'vaseya ityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Even on a bed-or-seat measured by the Conqueror’s eight finger-breadths, one should not sit without a covering — to show this, he says: "On a communal bed one should place" and so forth. What belongs to the <s>Saṃgha</s> is a communal bed-and-seat. On that, an ascetic should place a covering. And that covering is not intended to be of grass, leaves, and the like; rather, "of cloth" — he says: "Cloth" and so forth — a triple fold of fine cloth, of thick cloth

body.text: atirekaprāmāṇike sāṃghike śayanāsane yathā pratipattavyaṃ tathā darśanannāha | nyasya garteṣu tatpādāniti vistaraḥ | tacchabdena sāṃghikaśayanāsana mabhisaṃvadhyate | tena tatpādāniti sāṃghikaśayanāsanapādān | kīdṛśān? atirekapramāṇakān, jināṣṭāṅgulapramāṇādadhikapramāṇānityarthaḥ | nyasya prakṣipya | kutretyāha | garteṣu | athavā suṣirapratipādeṣu prakṣipya | kiṃ evaṃ vratī niṣeveta sāṃghikaṃ śayanāsanaṃ? śayanāsanamiti vakṣyate | ṭaṃkitvā kīlakeṣu veti | athavā caturṣu kīlakeṣu tānatirekapramāṇakān pādān ṭaṃkitvā badhvā kiṃ kartavyamiti na jñāyate kriyākāra[ka]saṃbandhasya parisamāptatvāt | ata āha evaṃ vetyādi | amunānantaroktena krameṇa sāṃghikaṃ śayanāsanaṃ bhajeta | ikṣuyavagodhūmādīnāṃ (

children.text: ) rakṣārthaṃ yaddīrghapādaḥ mañcaḥ kriyate, tatrādhvago yatiḥ svapet | ādiśabdāt gṛhiśayyāsanasya grahaṇaṃ vedyaṃ | tatrāpi gṛhiṇāṃ śayanāsane yatinā na pādau lambīyayitavyau- mā bhūjjanāvadhyānamiti ||
children.translated_text: on that, a traveling ascetic may sleep. By the word 'etc.,' the inclusion of lay people's bedding and seating should be understood. Even there, on the bedding and seating of lay people, an ascetic should not let his feet dangle — lest there be contempt from people.

body.translated_text: Showing how one should deal with communal (<s>sāṃghika</s>) bedding and seating that is oversized, he says: 'having placed those legs in pits, etc.' — this is the elaboration. By the word 'those' (<s>tat</s>), communal bedding and seating is connected. Thus 'those legs' means the legs of the communal bedding and seating. Of what kind? Oversized — meaning exceeding the measure of eight finger-widths of the <s>Jina</s>. 'Having placed' means having inserted. Where? He says: 'in pits.' Or alternatively, having inserted them in hollow supports. What — should a vow-holder then use such communal bedding and seating? 'Bedding and seating' will be stated. 'Or having fastened to pegs' — or alternatively, having fastened and bound those oversized legs to four pegs — what should be done? This is not known, since the relation of action and agent is already completed. Therefore he says: 'thus, etc.' By the method just stated, one should use the communal bedding and seating. The long-legged bed that is made for the protection of sugarcane, barley, wheat, and the like —

body.text: pravrajyāṃ prasāṇīkṛtya yathāvṛddhikayā sāṃghikaṃ vihāramuddeṣṭavyamiti darśayannāha | alpaṃ ce[di]tyādi | yadi bahavaḥ śrāmaṇerā bhavanti vihārāśca stokāstadā ekaikaṃ vi[hā]raṃ dvādaśebhyaḥ śrāmaṇerebhyo dātavyaṃ | athaivamapi bahavoyatayo bhavanti, tadā antato 'gatyā nirmuṣṭakaṃ hastamekaikasmai śrāmaṇerāya dātavyaṃ | bahutve tu viparyayāditi | kathaṃ viparyayāt? yadi bahavo vihārā bhavanti yatayaśca [stokāḥ], tadā ekaismai api śrāmaṇerāya bahavo vihārā dātavyāḥ | tatra vihāraśabdena layanamevocyate viharantyasminniti kṛtvā ||
body.translated_text: Showing that communal monasteries should be assigned according to seniority, having given priority to ordination, he says: 'if few, etc.' If there are many <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> and the monasteries are few, then one monastery each should be given to twelve <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>. But if even so there are many ascetics, then ultimately, as a last resort, an unclenched hand's width of space should be given to each <s>śrāmaṇera</s>. 'But when there is abundance, the reverse' — how the reverse? If there are many monasteries and the ascetics are few, then even to a single <s>śrāmaṇera</s> many monasteries should be given. There, by the word 'monastery' (<s>vihāra</s>), a cell (<s>layana</s>) is meant, since one 'dwells' (<s>viharati</s>) in it.

body.text: stokaṃ cedityādi | yadi stokaṃ śayanāsanaṃ bhavati yatayaśca bahavaḥ, tadā tatra yo vṛddhaḥ sa mañce svapet | yastu navakaḥ sa pīṭhe svapet | athaivamapi sarveṣāṃ na bhavati, tadā yāvadvṛkṣamūle vṛddhena svaptavyaṃ, navakena tvabhyavakāśaka ityevaṃ yathāvṛddhikayā sāṃghikaṃ śayanāsanamuddeṣṭavyaṃ | kiṃ punaḥ sarvakālamebetyāha | antarvarṣāsu no sthāpya ityādi | antarvarṣākāle yatinā yathāvṛddhikayānyaḥ sabrahmacārī nopasthāpayitavyaḥ | ya upasthā[pa]yati tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'If the bedding is little, etc.' If the bedding and seating is scarce and the ascetics are many, then the elder (<s>vṛddha</s>) should sleep on the bed (<s>mañca</s>). But a junior (<s>navaka</s>) should sleep on a stool (<s>pīṭha</s>). If even so it does not suffice for all, then the elder should sleep at the foot of a tree, while the junior should [sleep] in the open (<s>abhyavakāśa</s>) — thus, communal bedding and seating should be assigned according to seniority.

body.text: atha kimarthaṃ śayanāsanamuddiśyata ityāha | saṃskāretyādi | chinnagranthyādikaraṇaṃ saṃskāraḥ | tatra svātmāvasthitiḥ paribhogaḥ | paripālanaṃ saṃrakṣaṇaṃ | evamarthaṃ sāṃghika śayanāsanamuddiśyate na vyasanitayeti darśayati ||
body.translated_text: Now, for what purpose is bedding and seating assigned? He says: 'repair, etc.' Repair (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is the mending of cut bindings and the like. Use (<s>paribhoga</s>) therein is one's own occupancy. Maintenance (<s>paripālana</s>) is preservation. For these purposes is communal bedding and seating assigned — not for the sake of indulgence — thus he shows.

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ sarvāṇyeva layanānyuddeṣṭavyāni? netyāha | kiṃ tarhi hīnamadhyetyādi | yadi bhūyāṃsi layanāni santi saṃvariṇaścālpīyānsastadā āgantukānāṃ bhikṣūṇāmavasthitaye layanatrayaṃ sthāpayitavyaṃ kīdṛśamityāha | hīnamadhyottamaṃ | yadyāgantukā āgacchanti, [ta]dā vṛddhādyāgantukebhyastaduddiśeddaharakramāt | teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ layanānāṃ madhye yaduttamaṃ layanaṃ tadvṛddhāyāgantukabhikṣave uddeṣṭavyaṃ yanmadhyaṃ tattato navakāya, yaddhīnaṃ tatsarvanavakāyeti ||
body.translated_text: Now, should all cells be assigned? No, he says. What then? 'Low, middle, etc.' If there are many cells and the <s>saṃvarins</s> (vow-holders) are few, then for the accommodation of visiting <s>bhikṣus</s>, three cells should be set aside. Of what kind? He says: 'low, middle, and excellent.' If visitors come, then to elder and other visitors one should assign those; to junior [visitors],

body.text: kimarthaṃ punarbhagavānuccaśayanamahāśayanapratiṣedhaṃ cakāretyāha | śayanāsanamatyucceti vistaraḥ | yasmādatīvoccaṃ śayanāsanaṃ yateḥ śrāmaṇerasya madakaraṃ, auddhatyakaraṃ, lākāvadhyānasya ca hetukāraṇaṃ, tasmātkāraṇād bhagavatoccaśayanamahāśayanaṃ pratiṣiddhamiti | jināṣṭāṅgulapramāṇādatirekapramāṇikatvāduccaśayanaṃ, mahāśayanañca rukmarūpyamayatvāditi ||
body.translated_text: For what purpose did the Blessed One make the prohibition against high beds and large beds? He says: 'the bedding and seating being excessively high, etc.' — this is the elaboration. Since bedding and seating that is excessively high is, for the ascetic, for the <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, a cause of pride, a cause of agitation, and a cause of contempt from people — for that reason, the Blessed One prohibited high beds and large beds. [The measure] exceeding the <s>Jina</s>'s eight-finger-width standard

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ uccaśayanamahāśayanaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the sixth [precept] — the training rule of abstaining from high beds and large beds (<s>uccaśayanamahāśayanaviratiśikṣāpada</s>) — is completed.

body.text: nṛttagītavāditra[viśokadarśanavirati]śikṣāpadamadhikṛtyāha | bāhuvikṣepakamityādi | dvayorbāhvorvikṣepaṇa sphoraṇaṃ kṛtvā yannartanaṃ tannṛttamucyate | etaccanṛttamunmattatvamiti bhagavānavocat | yaccoccaiḥ svareṇa gītametadāryāṇāṃ samunmūlitākhilākuśalamūlānāmajñānapaṭalapāṭanapaṭūnāṃ ruditaṃ kranditamiti | yasmādbhagavānavadat tasmātkāraṇāt vīṇāvaṃśamṛdaṅgādivāditraṃ yatirna vādayet | yasmin krīḍāsthāne utsavādike gatvā vigataśokāḥ syuḥ strīpuruṣāstatkrīḍāsthānaṃ vigataśokaṃ yatirna yāyāt | yastu śrāmaṇero hṛṣṭaḥ san nṛ[tya]ti gāyati vāditraṃ vādagrati, tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Addressing the training rule of abstaining from dancing, singing, playing music, and watching shows (<s>nṛttagītavāditraviśokadarśanaviratiśikṣāpada</s>), he says: 'throwing of arms, etc.' The dancing (<s>nṛtta</s>) that is performed by throwing and waving both arms is called '<s>nṛtta</s>.' This dancing, the Blessed One said, is madness (<s>unmattatva</s>). That which is sung in a loud voice — for the noble ones who have thoroughly uprooted all unwholesome roots and who are skilled in tearing apart the veil of ignorance — that is weeping, lamentation.

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanā[cā]rasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ nṛttagītavāditra[viśokadarśana]viratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāma sapta[maṃ] ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the seventh [precept] — the training rule of abstaining from dancing, singing, playing music, and watching shows — is completed.

body.text: gandhamālyavilepanaviratiśikṣāpadamadhikṛtyāha | candanetyādi | yatiścandanādikaṃ gandhaṃ dhā[ra]yet | kīdṛśo yatirityāha | vyādhiḥ saṃjāto yasyeti vyādhito, glāna ityarthaḥ | kasya vacanena dhārayedityāha | bhiṣagāderityāha | vaidyopadeśāt | katamena vidhinetyāha | datvetyādi | pūrvaṃ munaye buddhāya bhagavate candanādikaṃ gandhaṃ datvā paścādātmanā dhārayet | svasthastu yatiḥ kadācidapi candanādikaṃ gandhaṃ na dhārayet ||
body.translated_text: Addressing the training rule of abstaining from garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics (<s>gandhamālyavilepanaviratiśikṣāpada</s>), he says: 'sandalwood, etc.' An ascetic may wear perfume such as sandalwood and the like. An ascetic of what kind? He says: one who is afflicted by illness — meaning one who is sick (<s>glāna</s>). On whose instruction may he wear it? He says: 'by the physician, etc.' On the instruction of a doctor (<s>vaidya</s>). By what procedure? He says: 'having given, etc.' First, having offered [it] to the sage, the <s>Buddha</s>,

body.text: na tiṣṭhedityādi | sati prakaṭe deśe candanādyanuliptagātro yatiḥ glāno 'pi sanna tiṣṭhet | yadi bahirnirgantukāmo bhavati, tadā kṣālayitvā bahirvrajet | anenaiva vidhānena dhārayetkusumasrajamiti | kusumaṃ puṣpaṃ, srak mālā, tena kusumasrajamiti, puṣpamālāmityarthaḥ | kiṃ dhārayet? anenaiva vidhāneneti | pūrvaṃ tāvadbuddhāya dadyāt paścādātmanā dhārayediti | kīdṛśena glānena sragmālā dhārayitavyetyāha | netraduḥkhetyādi | netraduḥkhena śiraḥśūlena pūtanāgraheṇa ca rujituṃ śīlaṃ yasya yateḥ sa tathoktaḥ | tasya śīrṣaṃ kusumamālayā veṣṭayet | na ca puṣpamālāyāḥ mekhalāṃ lambayet ||
body.translated_text: 'One should not stand, etc.' Even a sick ascetic whose body is anointed with sandalwood and the like should not stand in a public, exposed place. If he wishes to go outside, then having washed [it off], he should go out. 'By this very procedure, one should wear a flower garland' — '<s>kusuma</s>' means flower, '<s>sraj</s>' means garland — thus 'flower garland' means a garland of flowers. What should one wear? 'By this very procedure,'

body.text: haritāletyādi | haritālādicūrṇena sugandhinā vā tailena varṇārthaṃ rūpaniṣpattyarthaṃ yatiḥ vadanādikaṃ gātraṃ na marṣayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Yellow orpiment (<s>haritāla</s>), etc.' An ascetic should not rub his face and other limbs with fragrant powder of yellow orpiment and the like, or with fragrant oil, for the purpose of complexion — for the purpose of improving appearance.

body.text: kimarthaṃ punarbhagavatā nṛttādi pratiṣiddhamityāha | yaterapratirūpatvādityādi | yasmānnṛttagītavāditraviśokadarśanaṃ gandhamālyavilepanadhāraṇañca yaterapratirūparāgakaraṃ auddhatyakaraṃ janānāñca kopakāraṇamavadhyā[na]karaṃ tasmājjinairbuddhairbhagavadbhirgarhitaṃ ninditaṃ ||
body.translated_text: For what purpose did the Blessed One prohibit dancing and the like? He says: 'because it is unbecoming for an ascetic, etc.' Since dancing, singing, playing music, watching shows, and wearing garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics is unbecoming for an ascetic, causes passion, causes agitation, is a cause of anger in people, and causes contempt — therefore it was censured, condemned by the <s>Jinas</s>, the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones.

body.text: prasaṅgenānyadapi pratiṣedhayati | na darpaṇa ityādinā | ādarśe tailabhājane jalabhājane vā mukhaṃ na nirīkṣeta | kṛtagaṇḍāditvena śirovyathena śirovedhaduḥkhena gadena vyādhinā ca ya āturo glānaḥ taṃ muktvā anyena nirīkṣaṇīyaṃ | kiñca vibhūṣaṇāyetyādi | yatiḥ maṇḍanārthamātmano mukhaṃ tailena nābhyañjayedantaśaḥ pānīyenāpi | śirorogetyādi | śirasi rogo vyādhiḥ, āsyaṃ mukhañca sphuṭitaṃ yasya yateḥ sa tathoktaḥ | tasmādṛte anyeneti yāvat | na kuṅkumetyādi | yatiścandanakuṅkumādicūrṇena vadanaṃ mukhaṃ na maṇḍayet | piṭakasya tu śamanārthaṃ tilakalāpaprabhṛtibhiḥ lepa iṣṭo 'bhipreta iti yāvat | yastu yatiḥ śaithilikatvādinā yathoktaṃ vidhiṃ na saṃpādayati, tasya duṣkṛtaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Incidentally, he prohibits other things as well, saying: 'not a mirror, etc.' One should not look at one's face in a mirror, an oil vessel, or a water vessel. Except for one who is afflicted — one who is sick with a boil on the cheek and the like, or with a headache, head-piercing pain, or illness — setting him aside, [it is] to be examined by another [means]. Moreover, 'for the purpose of adornment, etc.' — an ascetic should not anoint his face with oil for the purpose of self-decoration,

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ gandhamālyavilepanaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāmāṣṭamaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the eighth [precept] — the training rule of abstaining from garlands, perfumes, and cosmetics (<s>gandhamālyavilepanaviratiśikṣāpada</s>) — is completed.

body.text: vikālabhojanapratiṣedhakāraṇaṃ pradarśayannāha | rātrerityādi | rātreranyatra divase bhagavānaśanakṛtyaṃ kurvannalpābādhatāṃ samyagajānātsma, bhikṣava iti śrāvakān prati babhāṣe | kimiti | tathaiva vaḥ kāryamiti | yasmānmama rātreranyatra bhuñjānasyālparogatā babhūva, tasmād yuṣmābhirapi divase bhoktavyaṃ na rātrāviti | anena ślokena vikālabhojanaviratiśikṣāpadaprajñapteḥ kāraṇamākhyātaṃ | bhūyo 'pi tatkāraṇaṃ pratipādanāyāha | viṇmūtretyādi | rātrau piṇḍapātamaṭatāṃ aśucigarte mūtragarte ca pāto bhavati | aśvacoreṇa gocoreṇāhinā sarpeṇa ca samāgamo bhavati | evamapi sati ete yataya udarasya kukṣeḥ pūraṇārthaṃ rātrau naḥ asmākaṃ gṛhe piṇḍapātamaṭantīti jano 'vadhyātavān | janairavadhyāte 'pi te yatayaḥ divāpratyūṣasi sāyahnakāle ca piṇḍapātamaṭitumārabdhāḥ | tatrāpi janairavadhyātamiti darśayitumāha | sāyaṃ prātaścetyādi ślokaḥ | ete bhikṣavaḥ sāyahnakāle prātaḥ prabhāte ca sabhācatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu mandireṣu gṛheṣu ca aṭanti bhramanti bhuñjate cāsatkṛtyaṃ ca kurvantīti janairavadhyātaṃ | atastasmātkāraṇātkimityāha | sugataḥ prāhetyādi | praśastamapunarāvṛttyā niḥśeṣaṃ vā gata iti sugataḥ, yathākramaṃ surūpavatsunaṣṭakṣukhat supūrṇaghaṭavacca | sa prāha, bratīti sma | kimiti | yatiḥ kāle bhuñjīta | kīdṛśe kāla ityāha | uditādityetyādi | keśamātreṇāpyanatīto 'saṃkrānto madhyāhno yenoditenādityena sa evamucyate, tasmin |
body.translated_text: Showing the reason for the prohibition of eating at improper times, he says: 'at night' and so forth. 'Except at night, during the day' — the Blessed One, taking his meal [only during the day], came to know freedom from illness fully, and addressed the disciples (<s>bhikṣus</s>), saying: 'You should do the same.' 'Why?' 'Because when I ate at times other than night [i.e., during the day], I experienced freedom from illness; therefore you too should eat during the day, not at night.' By this verse, the reason for the prescription of the precept of abstaining from eating at improper times is declared. To establish yet another reason, he says: 'feces, urine' and so forth. Those going for alms at night fall into filth-pits and urine-pits. They encounter horse-thieves, cattle-thieves, and serpents. Even so, the people reproached [the monks]: 'These renunciants come to our houses at night seeking alms, just for the purpose of filling their bellies.' Although reproached by people, those renunciants began going for alms at dawn during the day and in the evening. To show that even then people reproached them, he says the verse 'in the evening and morning' and so forth. 'These <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the evening and at dawn, wander about in assembly halls, squares, crossroads, temples, and houses, and eat, and behave improperly' — thus people reproached them. From that reason, what [did the Buddha say]? 'The <s>Sugata</s> spoke' and so forth. '<s>Sugata</s>' — one who has gone excellently, or one who has gone without return, or one who has gone completely — like one of beautiful form, like [one from whom] hunger has been well removed, like a well-filled vessel, respectively. He spoke, saying: 'The renunciant should eat at the [proper] time.' 'At what kind of time?' He says: 'when the sun has risen' and so forth. '[The time] when the sun has risen [such that] midday has not been passed by even a hair's breadth' — that is called thus; at that [time].

body.text: kīdṛśaṃ punastūditādityakāle bhoktavyamityāha | sakturodanetyādi | pañcabhojanāni kālikānisaktubhaktakulmāṣamatsyamāṃsākhyāni | kadācidetāni pañcabhojanāni saptāhikādisammiśrāṇyapi bhavantītyāha | yāvajjīviketyādi | yāvajjīvikena pippalyādinā tailādinā pānakaiśca yatparivarjitaṃ tatkālikaṃ | kiṃ punaretadeva pañcavidhaṃ bhojanaṃ kālikamutānyadapi? anyadapītyāha | yatkiñcidadyate dantairiti | anena kharaviśadaṃ vastvabhidhīyate | galake vā praveśyata ityanena nāsikayāpi yatpīyate tadapi galakenevābhyavahriyata iti, tasyāpi pratiṣedhaḥ kṛto bhavati | anyathā hi vikāle kṣīrapānamadoṣāya syāt | kukṣiviṣṭaśabdenobhayapadābhihitaṃ vastvabhidhīyate | kukṣerupastambhakaṃ paripūrakaṃ karotīti kukṣiviṣṭabhaṃkṛt yade[ta]tsarvaṃ tatkāle ādyādityodite, madhyāhnādarvāgyatirbhakṣayedityarthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'But what kind of [food] should be eaten when the sun has risen?' He says: 'barley-flour, cooked rice' and so forth. The five foods that are time-bound (<s>kālika</s>) are called: barley-flour (<s>saktu</s>), cooked rice (<s>bhakta</s>), porridge (<s>kulmāṣa</s>), fish (<s>matsya</s>), and meat (<s>māṃsa</s>). 'Sometimes these five foods are also mixed with seven-day [provisions] and the like' — he says: 'with <s>yāvajjīvika</s>' and so forth. What is separated from <s>yāvajjīvika</s> [provisions] such as long pepper, oils, and drinks — that is <s>kālika</s> (time-bound). 'Is only this fivefold food time-bound, or other things as well?' 'Other things as well' — he says: 'Whatever is eaten with the teeth' — by this, hard and solid substances are indicated. 'Or [what] enters through the throat' — by this, even what is drunk through the nose is also consumed through the throat, so its prohibition is also established. Otherwise, drinking milk at an improper time would be faultless. By the word 'filling the belly' (<s>kukṣiviṣṭa</s>), the substance indicated by both terms is meant — whatever supports and fills the belly. All of this — at the time [beginning] from the first sunrise, [and ending] before midday — the renunciant should eat.

body.text: vikāle tu yadbhoktuṃ labhyate, taddarśayannāha | saktvādyāmiṣanirmuktamityādi | saktukulmāṣādibhirāmiṣaiḥ parityaktaṃ | kīdṛśaṃ? nīrajaṃrajorahitaṃ kardamādikaṃ | deve varṣati yā śilā patati, tadvarṣopalakaṃ aśnīyāt, bhakṣayet | pātumicchā pipāsā pānābhilāṣaḥ, tenārtaḥ san himaṃ yatiḥ pibediti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Showing what may be consumed at an improper time, he says: 'free from solid food like barley-flour' and so forth. [Food that is] free from solid foods such as barley-flour, porridge, and the like. Of what kind? Free from impurity — free from sediment, mud, and the like. 'Hailstones' (<s>varṣopalaka</s>) — stones that fall when the sky rains — one may eat them. 'The desire to drink is thirst' (<s>pipāsā</s>) — the wish for a beverage; afflicted by it, the renunciant may drink ice (<s>hima</s>).

body.text: kathaṃ punaḥ kalpikodakaṃ grāhyamityenaṃ vikalpya avasarīkartumāha | kalpyavārigrahamityādi | kalpikasya vāriṇo grahaṇaṃ kalpavārigrahaḥ, tasmin | kalpikodakagrahaṇa (

children.text: ) nimittamiti yāvat | yāvatā kālena dvau hastau prakṣālyamānau sarudhirau bhavataḥ, tāvantaṃ kālaṃ tau na prakṣālayitavyau | nāpyaṅgulī prakṣāla[ne] kalpikodakaṃ grāhyaṃ | māyetyādi | māyayā śāṭhyena | yukto yatistayoḥ prakṣālanaṃ na kuryāt yadi prakṛtyaiva snigdhatvagbhikṣubhavati, tasya snigdhatvaco yateḥ yau hastau tau saśabdau bhavataḥ, tadā śuddhau vedyau ||
children.translated_text: ) is as follows. For as long a time as two hands being washed become bloody, for that long they should not be washed. Nor should permissible water be taken for washing fingers. 'With deceit' and so forth — with deceit, with fraud. A renunciant engaged [in such conduct] should not wash them. But if a <s>bhikṣu</s> naturally has oily skin, [and] the hands of that renunciant with oily skin make a sound [when rubbed], then they should be considered clean.

body.translated_text: 'But how should permissible (<s>kalpika</s>) water be taken?' Analyzing this and explaining it, he says: 'the taking of permissible water' and so forth. The taking of permissible water is '<s>kalpavārigraha</s>'; regarding that — the occasion for taking permissible water

body.text: kiṃ punarvikāle glānenāpi na bhoktavyamityāha | na dāsyathetyādi | kṣudbubhukṣā | tṛṣṇāśabdenāpi lokapratītorthaḥ pānābhilāṣa ucyate | tābhyāṃ pīḍito 'haṃ mariṣyāmi, yadi mahyaṃ vikāle bhoktuṃ na dāsyatha ityevaṃ yadi kaścidvirukto yatirbūyāt, tadā sa yatiḥ pūrṇe maṇḍakuṇḍe prakṣeptavyaḥ | āgalakādityavaśeṣaṃ | athaivamapyatināmayituṃ na śaknoti, tadā kiṃ kāryamityāha | aṣṭāsvadhautetyādi | aṣṭābhiḥ jale dhautaṃ prakṣālitaṃ yaddhānyaṃ kalpikena ca vastreṇa baddhaṃ tadanāmiṣe pātre tāmrabhājane anyatra vā prasthāpanaṃ diśeddadyādityarthaḥ | yadi tu taddhānyaṃ sphuṭaṃ sphuṭitaṃ vā sat glānāya pātuṃ na kalpate ||
body.translated_text: 'But should even a sick person not eat at an improper time?' He says: 'will you not give' and so forth. '<s>Kṣut</s>' is hunger. By the word '<s>tṛṣṇā</s>' (craving), the commonly understood meaning of 'desire for drink' is also indicated. 'I am afflicted by them and will die if you do not give me food at an improper time' — if some distressed renunciant should say this, then that renunciant should be immersed in a full bathing-tank. The remainder [continues:] 'up to the throat.' But if even so he cannot be sustained, then what should be done? He says: 'washed eight times' and so forth. Grain that has been washed eight times in water, bound in a permissible cloth, [placed] in a non-meat vessel — a copper vessel — or elsewhere, should be given. But if that grain has been split or cracked, it is not permissible for the sick person to drink [its liquid].

body.text: prasaṅgenānyadapi pratiṣedhayati | lobhotthāpitetyādi | lobhenākuśalamūlena samutthāpitaṃ yatkāyavākkarma tena samupārjito yo vihāracīvarāhārastaṃ saviṣabhaktavadvarjayet | madyetyādi | madyavikrayaṇaṃ, śastravikrayaṇaṃ, viṣavikrayaṇaṃ, prāṇivikrayaṇaṃ, (

children.text: ) lākṣavikrayaṇaṃ ca vratī svayaṃ na kuryāt, na ca pareṇa kārayet, na ca tena madyādinā jīvikāṃ kalpayet | satkāretyādi | akṣāṇyucyante cakṣurādīndriyāṇi | teṣāṃ yaḥ saṃvaraḥ saṃyamaḥ lābhasatkārārthaṃ, sā kuhanā matā | vastrānnapānādikasya tu lābhasya prāptyartha yā cāṭuvāditā priyavāditā, sā lāpanā mateti | naiṣpeṣikatvamityādi | annapānādipratilaṃbhāya yatpareṣāṃ kutsanaṃ tad naiṣpeṣikatvamucyate | anyadīyasya tu pātrāderyadvarṇanaṃ guṇodbhāvanaṃ lābhārthaṃ mahayametat pātrādikaṃ dadyāditi tatraimittikatvamucyate | lābhena lipsetyādi | alpena lābhena yadvṛddhiparyeṣaṇaṃ lābhānāṃ sā lipsetyucyate labdhumicchā lipseti arthāt | ye kuhanalapananaiṣpeṣikādibhirniṣpannā lābhāḥ | tānetān mithyājīvān yatiḥ parivarjayet | kiṃ vadityāha | purīṣavadaśucivadityarthaḥ | krīḍetyādi | pareṣāmapahananaṃ paropaghātaḥ | krīḍākautūhalaṃ | kāyavāksamucchitaṃ sarvakālaṃ | viṭpradigdhamivoragaṃ, aśuciliptaṃ sarpaṃ yathā vratī parivarjayet | vipaṇītyādi | vipaṇiḥ vaṇikpathamucyate, yasya ghaṭṭa iti prākṛtajanapratītiḥ | tarantyasminniti taraḥ, kṣepaṇatīrthaṃ | gulmaṃ viṭapaḥ | evamādike channaprakaṭe bhūpradeśe kiṃ tiṣṭhettatra na cellaka iti vakṣyate | duṣṭapravrajitāyāḥ duḥśīlāpi sato pratijñāyāṃ āste | āha | pravrajite veśyārūpā jīvikāvā | guru (
children.translated_text: ) and the selling of lac — the vow-observer should not do these himself, nor cause another to do them, nor should he arrange a livelihood through liquor and the like. 'Out of honor' and so forth. '<s>Akṣas</s>' are called the sense-faculties beginning with the eye. Their 'restraint' (<s>saṃvara</s>) — self-control for the purpose of gain and honor — that is considered '<s>kuhanā</s>' (hypocrisy). But flattering speech and pleasant words for the purpose of obtaining gains of cloth, food, drink, and the like — that is considered '<s>lāpanā</s>' (flattery). '<s>Naiṣpeṣikatva</s>' (denigration) and so forth — the disparagement of others for the purpose of obtaining food, drink, and the like is called <s>naiṣpeṣikatva</s>. But the praising and extolling of another's bowl and the like for the purpose of gain — 'This bowl and the like is magnificent; please give [one]' — that is called '<s>naimittikatva</s>' (hinting). 'Through gain, desire' and so forth — the seeking of increase through a small gain — that desire to obtain is called '<s>lipsā</s>' (greed). Those gains that are produced through hypocrisy, flattery, denigration, and the like — the renunciant should avoid these wrong livelihoods. 'Like what?' He says: 'like feces' — meaning, like impurity. 'Sport' and so forth — the harming of others is '<s>paropaghāta</s>' (injury to others). Playful curiosity; bodily and verbal agitation at all times — these the vow-observer should avoid like a serpent smeared with excrement, like a snake covered with filth. 'Marketplace' and so forth — '<s>vipaṇi</s>' (marketplace) is the merchant's road, commonly known as '<s>ghaṭṭa</s>' in the vernacular. '<s>Tara</s>' (crossing) — that across which people cross — a ferry. '<s>Gulma</s>' is a thicket. In such concealed or open places on the ground — should one stay? 'One should not loiter there,' as will be stated. 'Of a corrupt female renunciant' — even one of bad conduct who has [formally] professed [the vows] — it is said — 'one who lives as a renunciant but in the manner of a courtesan.' 'Senior'

children.text: ) kumārikā sthale vasatā avyūḍhā āste | etāḥ kiṃ? dyūtakāragṛhaṃ bandhanāgāraṃ anyacca yadvandhanasthānaṃ tat agocaro 'viṣaya ākhyātaḥ | tasmāttatra na tiṣṭhediti |
