children.translated_text: ) 'maiden' — a young unmarried woman dwelling on the premises. These [places] — what? A gambling house, a prison, and whatever other place of confinement — these are declared to be out of bounds (<s>agocara</s>), forbidden territory. Therefore one should not stay there.

body.translated_text: Incidentally, he also prohibits other things: 'arisen from greed' and so forth. Whatever bodily and verbal action is produced by greed, the unwholesome root — the monastery, robe, or food acquired through that [action] should be abandoned as if it were poisoned food. 'Liquor' and so forth — the selling of liquor, the selling of weapons, the selling of poison, the selling of living beings,

body.text: sphuṭārthāyāṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṭīkāyāṃ vikālabhojanaviratiśikṣāpadaṃ nāma navamaṃ ||
body.translated_text: In the <s>Sphuṭārthā</s>, the commentary on the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, the ninth [section], the precept of abstaining from eating at improper times (<s>vikālabhojanaviratiśikṣāpada</s>) [is completed].

body.text: daśamaśikṣāpadamadhikṛtyāha | kāyetyādi | sakalena kāyena hastābhyāṃ pādābhyāṃ vastreṇa chatrādinā ca vratī rajataṃ rūpyaṃ, jātarūpaṃ suvarṇaṃ na spṛśet | kimivetyāha | jvalitāgnivata | prajvālitadahanavaditi | anena daśamaṃ śikṣāpadamabhihitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Regarding the tenth precept, he says: 'with the body' and so forth. With the entire body, with the hands, with the feet, with cloth, with an umbrella and the like, the vow-observer should not touch silver (<s>rajata</s>, <s>rūpya</s>) or gold (<s>jātarūpa</s>, <s>suvarṇa</s>). 'Like what?' He says: 'Like a blazing fire' — like an ignited flame. By this, the tenth precept is stated.

body.text: idānīṃ prasaṅgainānyadapyācāraṃ saṃgṛhṇāti campūkalahetyādinā | tatra campū hāsyaṃ, kalahaḥ kāyakalaho vākkalahaśca | dantakāṣṭhādanaṃ dantakāṣṭhabhakṣaṇaṃ | śeṣaṃ sugamaṃ | campūkalahetyādi dvandvaḥ | campūkalahadantakāṣṭhādanāni kriyā yasya vṛddhāntikasya yateḥ sa tathoktaḥ | snānañca pānañcāśanañca stotraṃ ceti snānapānāśanastotrāṇi, tairvyagro 'prāptāvasaro yaḥ sa evamucyate | snānādivyagraśca nagnaścaikavastraśceti punarvigrahaḥ | sa pūrvoktaśca kiṃ na vandyo yatinā yatiriti vakṣyate | mṛtkarmetyādi | mṛṇmayakarmaṇā yo vyāpṛto 'prāptāvasaraḥ yaśca tūrṇaṃ tvaritaṃ dvitribhūmikaṃ vihāramutkasati, āśu śīghraṃ ca yo vrajati, yaśca pātraṃ pacati, cīvarakarmaṇā vā vyagraḥ, sa vṛddhāntiko yatiḥ dvitribhūmikaṃ vihāramuttiṣṭhan yāvat pātraṃ vā pacan kiṃ na vandyo yatinā yatiriti vakṣyate | cūrṇetyādi | cūrṇakriyāyāṃ cailakriyāyāṃ vastrapātrādiśodhane ca yaḥ āsaktaḥ, akṣiṇī yaścākte dhūmaṃ vā pibati, pustakaṃ vā likhati, vācayati, so 'pi na vandyaḥ | viṭprastrāvetyādi | yaḥ śrāmaṇero varcakuṭi prastrāvakuṭiṃ vā gacchati, parasmai vā uddiśati, tamasi andhakāre vā tiṣṭhati, antarvāsaṃ vā vāsayati, uttarāsaṃgaṃ vā prāvṛṇoti, sa vṛddhāntiko yatiḥ varcakuṭiṃ gacchan yāvaduttarāsaṃgaṃ prāvṛṇvan na vandya ityanena yādṛśyāmavasthāyāmavasthito vṛddhāntiko yatirnavakena na vanditavyaḥ, sā avasthābhihitā ||
body.translated_text: Now, incidentally, he compiles additional rules of conduct with "joking, quarreling" and so forth. Therein, "<s>campū</s>" means jest; "quarrel" means bodily quarrel and verbal quarrel. "Tooth-stick eating" means chewing a tooth-stick. The rest is easy to understand. "Joking, quarreling" and so forth is a <s>dvandva</s> compound. A senior ascetic whose activities are joking, quarreling, and tooth-stick chewing is described thus. Bathing, drinking, eating, and reciting hymns — these are the "bathing-drinking-eating-hymns"; one who is occupied with them, without opportunity [to receive salutation], is described thus. One occupied with bathing and the like, and naked, and in a single garment — this is a further analysis. That aforementioned [senior] — is he not to be saluted by an ascetic? This will be stated. "Clay work" and so forth — one who is occupied, without opportunity, with work of clay; one who hurriedly, quickly climbs a two- or three-storied monastery; one who walks swiftly, rapidly; one who is cooking an alms-bowl; or one occupied with robe-work — is that senior ascetic, climbing a two- or three-storied monastery, or cooking an alms-bowl, not to be saluted by an ascetic? This will be stated. "Powdering" and so forth — one who is engaged in powdering, oiling, washing cloth and bowl, whose eyes are affected, or who is inhaling smoke, or who is writing or reciting a manuscript — he too is not to be saluted. "Going to the latrine" and so forth — a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> who is going to the latrine or the urinal, or who is pointing out [the way] for another, or who stands in darkness, or who is putting on the undergarment, or who is wrapping the upper robe — that senior ascetic, going to the latrine and so on up to wrapping the upper robe, is not to be saluted. By this, the state in which a senior ascetic should not be saluted by a junior is stated.

body.text: idānīṃ tu yādṛgvidhāvasthāvasthitena navakena yatinā na vaditavyaṃ, tathā darśayitumāha | avaguṇṭhitetyādi | avaguṇṭhitaṃ pidhitaṃ śīrṣaṃ śiro yasya yateḥ tena samantaprāvṛtena vā yatinā kiṃ vandya iti vakṣyate | saha upanahā vartete pādau yasya yateḥ sa sopānatkaḥ, tena upānahārūḍhenetyarthaḥ | jānu ca jānu ca jānunī, tayorjānunoryā jaṃghā tasyāṃ jaṃghāyāṃ muṇḍe[na] sphoṭaṃ na dadyāt | kimivetyāha | avinā yathā | avirmeṣaḥ | yathā avinā meṇḍakena dvayorjānunorjaṃghāyāṃ hanyate, tadvadyatirapi vṛddhāntikasya yaterjaṃghāyāṃ na vandeteti yāvat | bhadantadharmāvalokitamitrastvāha | sopānatkena na vanditavya | kimivetyāha | ravinā yathā | ravirādityaḥ | yathāsau ravirupānahārūḍhastadvadupānahārūḍhena yatinā na vandanīyamityakārapraśleṣenāvabodhayan vakti | kimetadbhadantamatameṣṭavyaṃ? neṣṭavyaṃ | kiṃ tarhi anveṣṭavyaṃ vinaye meḍhakasyaiva dṛṣṭāntadānāt |
body.translated_text: Now, to show the states in which a junior ascetic should not salute, he says: "With head covered" and so forth. An ascetic whose head is covered, concealed — by that [ascetic] who is completely wrapped, should he salute? This will be stated. One whose feet have sandals is "one with sandals" (<s>sopānatka</s>) — meaning one who has mounted sandals. [While in these states], even a junior

body.text: vidhiṃ darśayannāha | samavasthetyādi | samavasthopaviṣṭasya yateḥ pādayugalaṃ karkaṭagrāhaṃ gṛhītvā śirasā vanditavyaṃ | yadā samavasthāniṣaṇṇo yatiḥ pādarogeṇa glānaḥ syāttadā vināpi karkaṭagrāhikayā vandyamānasya na doṣaḥ | yadi kaścidāgatyāgantukaḥ samavasthāniṣaṇṇama[bhivādayati], tadānena vaktavyamāyuṣman, (

children.text: ) kati varṣosi, katamaste nikāyaḥ, kati ca tasya nikāyasya bhedāḥ, katamā te sāmayiketyādi | so 'pi yadi āryamahāsāṃghiko bhavati, tadānena vācyamāryamahāsāṃghiko 'smi | tasya cedbhedāḥ
children.translated_text: ) "How many rains-retreats have you completed?" "Which is your school (<s>nikāya</s>)?" "How many divisions does that school have?" "Which is your assembly (<s>sāmayikī</s>)?" and so forth. If he belongs to the <s>Āryamahāsāṃghika</s> school, then he should say: "I am an <s>Āryamahāsāṃghika</s>." And if its divisions [are asked]

body.translated_text: Showing the procedure, he says: "To one in equal posture" and so forth. The pair of feet of an ascetic sitting in equal posture should be grasped in the crab-grip and saluted with the head. When an ascetic seated in equal posture is afflicted with a foot disease, there is no fault in being saluted even without the crab-grip. If someone comes as a visitor and salutes [a senior] seated in equal posture, then [the senior] should say to him

children.translated_text: The <s>Vādin</s>s, the <s>Arthasiddhārtha</s>s, the <s>Śailadvayanīvāsin</s>s,
the <s>Bhādrāyana</s>s, and the <s>Haimatā</s>s — six divisions of the <s>Mūlasāṃghika</s>s.

children.text: dairghī haimantakī graiṣmī vārṣikī ca tathottarā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Dairghī</s>, the <s>Haimantikī</s>, the <s>Graiṣmī</s>, the <s>Vārṣikī</s>, and the <s>Uttarā</s> —
these five seasonal assemblies (<s>sāmavāyikā</s>s) should be known by a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>.

body.text: ityevamanyadapi vivarjayitavyaṃ | tatra yo navakastena vanditavyaṃ, vṛddhena cārogyamastviti vācyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Thus, other things also should be avoided. Therein, the junior should salute, and the elder should say: "May you be healthy" (<s>ārogyam astu</s>).

body.text: athārogyamiti ko 'rthaḥ? yathā vātapittaśleṣmādayaḥ kupitāḥ santo bādhanārthena rogā ityucyante, tadvat rāgādayo 'pi kleśā rujanārthena rogaśabdavācyāḥ | na rogaḥ arogastadbhāva ārogyaṃ | kleśaprahāṇaṃ tava bhavatu | tathā cāha-
body.translated_text: Now, what is the meaning of "health" (<s>ārogya</s>)? Just as wind, bile, phlegm, and the like, when agitated, are called diseases because they cause affliction, so too passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the other afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>s), because they cause suffering, are to be designated by the word "disease." The absence of disease is freedom from disease; the state of that is "health." [The meaning is:] "May the abandonment of afflictions be yours." And thus it is said:

children.text: rāgādayo hyatitarāṃ rujayanti yasmādvātādayaśca kupitāḥ sakalaṃ janaughaṃ |
children.translated_text: Since passion and the other [afflictions] cause extreme suffering, and since disturbed wind and the other [humors afflict] all the masses of people —

children.text: tacchāntivāñchina parāḥ praṇateṣu tasmādārogyamastviti vaco nigadanti buddhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore, those others who desire peace say to those who bow down: "May you be healthy" — the <s>Buddha</s>s utter this word.

body.text: anya āha-
body.translated_text: Another says:

children.translated_text: That which is free from old age, death, sorrow, and fear; that which is devoid of moon, fire, sun, and water;
that which is eternal, supreme, unfallen — that state [......]

body.text: sa[ka]lairbhikṣubhiḥ śikṣākāmaiḥ vikālabhojanādikaṃ kṛtaṃ kasmādvayaṃ na kurma iti | āvāsakalpaḥ- amuṣmin vihāre bhikṣavo 'nyonyaṃ kāyasaṃsargaṃ kurvanti kasmādvayamapi na kurma iti | deśakalpaḥ- amuṣmin deśe vārddhuṣikabhikṣavaḥ kasmādvayamapi vṛddhi na prayacchāmaḥ | sthavirakalpaḥ- amukasthaviraścāpi sandhikāle bhuṅkte, kiṃ vayaṃ na bhuñjāmaha iti ||
body.translated_text: [...] all <s>bhikṣu</s>s desirous of training have done [things like] eating at improper times and the like — "Why should we not do [the same]?" Residence-custom (<s>āvāsakalpa</s>): "In such-and-such a monastery, <s>bhikṣu</s>s engage in bodily contact with one another — why should we not also do so?" Regional-custom (<s>deśakalpa</s>): "In such-and-such a region, usurious <s>bhikṣu</s>s [lend at interest] — why should we not also charge interest?" Elder-custom (<s>sthavirkalpa</s>): "Such-and-such an elder

body.text: bhikṣuvinayātsamuddhṛtamācārāntaraṃ na tu svamanīṣikayānyatkṛtamiti darśayitumāha | vinaya iti | vinayante 'nena kleśā iti vinayaḥ | samadhigataprātimokṣasaṃvareṇa bhikṣuvinayasaṃkṣepāduddhṛtaḥ | anyattu śeṣaṃ yadbhikṣuvinaye vyāsato nirdiṣṭaṃ | aśanavasanādau yathā pratipattavyaṃ tadupādhyāyācāryavṛddhatarebhyaḥ sakāśādyatinā śrotavyaṃ, tena sagauravena ca bhāvyaṃ |
body.translated_text: To show that this other conduct is extracted from the <s>Bhikṣu</s> <s>Vinaya</s> and is not something produced by one’s own fancy, he says: "<s>Vinaya</s>" — that by which the afflictions are disciplined is the <s>Vinaya</s>. Extracted from the summary of the <s>Bhikṣu</s> <s>Vinaya</s> by one who has attained the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint. But the rest that is explained in detail in the <s>Bhikṣu</s> <s>Vinaya</s> — how one should conduct oneself regarding food, clothing, and the like should be learned from preceptors and teachers

body.text: śatadvayenetyādi | etadantaroktaṃ śrīghanācārasaṃgrahaṃ saṃhatya yatsukṛtaṃ kuśalakṛtaṃ tena sukṛtena karmaṇā jano lokaḥ asaṃskṛtaṃ nirvāṇaṃ prāpnotu labhatāmityanena ślokena pariṇāmayati ||
body.translated_text: "By two hundred [verses]" and so forth — having composed this <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> stated herein, by that well-done, wholesome deed, may the world, the people, attain the unconditioned, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — by this verse, he dedicates [the merit].

children.translated_text: Having composed this commentary by <s>Jayarakṣita</s>, which removes the impurity of the ignorance of all people —

children.text: śubhamativipulaṃ mayā yadāptaṃ bhavatu jano 'khilastu tena buddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the vast and auspicious [merit] that I have obtained, may all people become <s>Buddha</s>s.

children.text: suśrīghanācārasusaṃgrahasya kṛtvā hi ṭīkāṃ yadavāpi puṇyaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having composed the commentary on the excellent <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, by whatever merit [has been generated] —
may all people, by that auspicious [merit], swiftly become Conquerors, with the glory of renowned virtues arising.
